title: Faith Is The Substance
summary: William Branham teaches on the nature of faith as the sixth sense, using personal anecdotes and biblical references to illustrate that faith is a direct, positive evidence of things unseen. He emphasizes that true faith is not mere hope but a substance that can move objects and bring healing, and he challenges the congregation to move beyond intellectual belief to genuine faith.

title: The Angel of God
summary: William Branham speaks about his healing ministry and the Angel of God that appeared to him, describing miracles of healing including a crippled boy and a deaf woman. He emphasizes the need for faith and warns of coming judgment, calling the audience to believe in God's power.

title: The Children of Israel
summary: William Branham speaks about the importance of faith in healing, recounting recent miracles and emphasizing that healing comes through faith in God, not through the preacher. He draws parallels between the journey of the children of Israel and the spiritual journey of the Church, warning against lukewarmness and urging unity and love among believers.

title: Experiences
summary: William Branham shares a personal testimony of a spiritual crisis where he felt God's presence leave him during a healing service, leading to a period of deep repentance and renewal. He describes how the gift of healing returned with greater power, and he emphasizes the importance of unity among churches and trusting in God rather than human efforts.

title: Experiences
summary: William Branham shares personal struggles with physical weakness and mental strain in ministry, reflecting on the difference between preaching by the Word and operating in a gift. He recounts healings, the use of prayer cloths, and encourages unity among believers as end-time confederations form.

title: Experiences
summary: William Branham shares personal testimonies of miraculous healings, including a vision of a dying boy and a crippled girl, emphasizing the importance of faith and obedience to God's direction. He explains how the gift of healing operates through divine visions and warns against fanaticism.
themes: The role of the Holy Spirit

title: The Angel of God
summary: William Branham speaks about the Angel of God that appears in his meetings, emphasizing that healing comes through faith in Christ, not through any human power. He urges unity among believers and warns against sin after receiving healing.

title: At Thy Word, Lord
summary: William Branham preaches on the importance of taking God at His Word, using biblical examples such as Peter launching out into the deep, the woman with the issue of blood, Jairus's daughter, Lazarus, and the Hebrew children in the fiery furnace. He emphasizes that God is the same yesterday, today, and forever, and that healing and deliverance are available to those who believe and act on God's promises.

title: I Was Not Disobedient To The Heavenly Vision
summary: William Branham speaks at Grace Missionary Church in Zion, Illinois, encouraging the congregation to continue in faith and prayer for revival. He shares testimonies of healings, including a cross-eyed baby and a deaf, dumb, crippled boy, and emphasizes the importance of believing in God's healing power. He also recounts a prophecy by Alexander Dowie about a revival forty years after his death.
themes: The role of the Holy Spirit

title: The Deity of Jesus Christ
summary: William Branham preaches on the deity of Jesus Christ, emphasizing that Christ is not merely a baby in a manger but Almighty God incarnate. He discusses the need for the baptism of the Holy Ghost, the coming revival, and the end-time drama unfolding in the world.

title: Moses
summary: William Branham opens a seventeen-night revival in Houston, emphasizing the importance of faith and the role of angelic guidance in ministry. He recounts his own calling and the gift of healing, including the ability to discern secrets of the heart, and draws parallels between Moses' mission and his own.

title: Believest Thou This?
summary: William Branham preaches on the resurrection of Lazarus from John 11, emphasizing the importance of taking God at His Word without waiting for signs. He contrasts the faith of Mary with the doubt of Zacharias, and discusses the foreordination of gifts and the need for a fresh daily infilling of the Holy Ghost.

title: God In His People
summary: William Branham speaks on the nature of divine healing, emphasizing that God alone is the healer and that men are merely channels. He discusses the gift of healing, the importance of faith, and the role of the Holy Spirit in revealing the secrets of hearts, as demonstrated through his own ministry.
themes: signs and wonders in the last days

title: Expectation
summary: William Branham speaks on the theme of expectation, using Simeon as an example of one who expected to see Christ before death. He encourages the audience to expect healing and miracles, sharing personal testimonies of divine guidance and healings. He emphasizes that the right mental attitude toward God's promises brings them to pass.

title: Baptismal Service
summary: William Branham conducts a baptismal service at the Branham Tabernacle, baptizing several candidates including his son Billy and nephew Melvin. He reflects on the resurrection of Christ and the significance of baptism as a public confession of faith.

title: Ministry Explained
summary: William Branham explains his healing ministry, emphasizing that he is not a divine healer but a channel for God's power. He describes the gift of discernment, which reveals people's conditions and sins to build faith, and stresses that healing comes through faith in God's Word. He also shares testimonies of healings and calls for unity among believers.

title: Obey the Voice of the Angel
summary: William Branham shares his testimony of being visited by an Angel who commissioned him to take a gift of divine healing to the nations. He reads from Exodus 23 about the Angel sent before Israel, and begins a prayer line, discerning diseases and casting out spirits through the Holy Spirit's power.

title: At Thy Word
summary: William Branham speaks on the importance of faith and the power of God's Word, sharing testimonies of healings and a supernatural photograph. He emphasizes that healing comes through faith in Christ and encourages believers to launch out into the deep at God's Word.

title: Led By The Spirit
summary: William Branham speaks on being led by the Holy Spirit, sharing personal testimonies of divine guidance and healing. He emphasizes that sons of God are led by the Spirit and recounts several instances where the Spirit directed him to specific people for healing. The sermon concludes with a prayer line and healings.

title: Believest Thou This?
summary: William Branham speaks on faith and divine healing, emphasizing that healing is already provided through Christ's atonement. He uses the story of Mary and the angel Gabriel to illustrate taking God at His Word without signs, and encourages believers to accept healing by faith.

title: Healing And What Sickness Is
summary: William Branham discusses the nature of sickness and healing, emphasizing that sickness is of the devil and that healing comes through faith in God. He explains that diseases are often caused by spirits that can be cast out, and that true healing requires a personal faith in Jesus Christ.

title: Expectations
summary: William Branham speaks on the importance of expecting God's promises, using the example of Simeon who was promised by the Holy Spirit that he would not die before seeing the Christ. He encourages believers to expect healing and to testify of their faith rather than their symptoms.

title: The Pool of Bethesda
summary: William Branham preaches on the pool of Bethesda, explaining that Jesus healed only one man because He did only what the Father showed Him. He applies this to his own ministry, emphasizing that he can only do what God reveals. The sermon includes prayer for the sick and testimonies of healing.
themes: the role of the Holy Spirit

title: The Resurrection of Lazarus
summary: William Branham preaches on the resurrection of Lazarus from John 11, emphasizing faith in Christ as the Resurrection and Life. He contrasts the doubt of Zacharias with the faith of Mary, and encourages believers to take God at His Word regardless of circumstances.

title: God Revealing Himself to His People
summary: William Branham preaches on how God reveals Himself to His people through various signs and wonders, including a pillar of fire and angelic visitations. He shares personal testimonies of divine encounters and healings, emphasizing faith and the power of God's Word.

title: Testimony
summary: William Branham opens a revival meeting with a reading from John 4 about the nobleman's son, emphasizing belief in Jesus' word. He shares testimonies of healings, including a man sent by a dream and a blind man healed after a vision. He then prays for the sick in a prayer line, discerning ailments and ministering healing.

title: Who Is God?
summary: William Branham preaches on the nature of God, emphasizing the authority of believers through faith in Christ. He recounts testimonies of healing and deliverance, including a woman with a demonic spirit, to illustrate the power of God's Word and the importance of unwavering faith.

title: Looking To The Unseen
summary: William Branham preaches on looking to the unseen, using the story of Elisha and the servant whose eyes were opened to see the heavenly host. He shares testimonies of miraculous healings, including a woman with cancer and a girl named Georgie Carter healed from tuberculosis, emphasizing faith in God's supernatural power.

title: IT SHALL BE EVEN AS IT WAS TOLD ME
summary: William Branham shares personal anecdotes and a powerful testimony of a vision predicting a boy's resurrection, which later occurs in Finland. He emphasizes faith in God's promises and the confirmation of gifts through the Holy Spirit.

title: Show Us The Father And It Suffices
summary: William Branham speaks on how to see God through His universe, His Word, His Son, and His people. He emphasizes faith in God's promises and the importance of believing in divine healing.

title: My Life Story
summary: William Branham shares his life story, from his humble beginnings in a log cabin in Kentucky to his ministry of divine healing. He emphasizes his poverty, his rejection by others, and his reliance on God, while urging listeners to seek the eternal city to come.

title: Believe Ye That I Am Able To Do This?
summary: William Branham preaches on the power of faith in Jesus Christ to heal, using the biblical account of two blind men and a deaf-mute. He shares testimonies of miraculous healings, including a woman raised from a coma and a blind girl receiving sight, emphasizing that faith in Christ, not human effort, brings healing.

title: The Angel and the Commission
summary: William Branham speaks about the burden of the supernatural gift of healing, recounting his encounter with the Angel of the Lord who commissioned him to pray for the sick. He emphasizes that the gift is for prayer, not for performing miracles, and urges the congregation to believe without needing a sign.

title: Faith Without Works Is Dead
summary: William Branham preaches on the relationship between faith and works, using James 2:21-26 to show that faith is made perfect by works. He shares testimonies of healing and transformation, emphasizing that true faith must be acted upon.

title: Testimony
summary: William Branham shares personal testimonies and encourages faith in God's healing power. He recounts a vision of three girls and a police encounter, emphasizing the Holy Spirit's guidance. The sermon includes a prayer line and a healing demonstration.

title: To Whom Is The Arm Of The Lord Revealed?
summary: William Branham preaches on the revelation of God's power through faith in Jesus Christ, emphasizing that the same Holy Spirit that worked in the early church is present today to heal and save. He calls the congregation to commit themselves to God's Word and believe in their healing as they pass through the prayer line.
themes: the power of the Holy Spirit
the contract between God and His people

title: Prodigal
summary: William Branham preaches on the parable of the Prodigal Son, emphasizing God's love for the lost and the need for repentance. He contrasts man-made religion with the covering of Christ's blood, and warns against worldly influences and the dangers of sin.

title: Take the Rod and Gather the People
summary: In this closing sermon of a series in Cleveland, William Branham encourages the congregation to speak to the Rock (Christ) for healing, drawing from Numbers 20:7-8. He emphasizes the importance of believing in Jesus as the Healer and demonstrates the Holy Spirit's power through discernment and prayer for the sick.

title: The Works That I Do Bear Witness of Me
summary: William Branham preaches on the importance of unity among believers and the love of God, emphasizing that faith without works is dead. He calls for breaking down denominational barriers and loving one another as evidence of true discipleship. The sermon also includes a call to seek the Giver before the gifts and a testimony of the Angel of the Lord's guidance.

title: The Angel of the Lord
summary: William Branham uses the analogy of birds eating strawberries despite a scarecrow to illustrate how believers should not be deterred by fear or criticism from partaking in God's blessings. He discusses the role of the Angel of the Lord, the importance of faith, and the need to discern true spirituality from false. The sermon includes testimonies of healing and a call to approach God with a sincere heart.

title: Life Story
summary: William Branham shares his early life experiences, including memories of his father, childhood poverty, and the angelic visitation that warned him not to drink or smoke. He reflects on the longing for home and the importance of family, while also addressing moral issues such as smoking and the need for genuine salvation.

title: The Hour Is Come
summary: William Branham preaches on the urgency of making a decision for God, using biblical examples such as Noah, the Hebrew children, and the woman with the issue of blood. He emphasizes that the hour has come for the congregation to believe in divine healing and take God at His Word.

title: Exhortation of Divine Healing
summary: William Branham opens a healing meeting in California, expressing gratitude for the audience and explaining his ministry's purpose. He emphasizes that healing is already purchased at Calvary and that faith in God's Word is key. Branham shares his personal calling and the supernatural signs accompanying his ministry, encouraging attendees to believe for their healing.

title: The Angel of the Lord
summary: William Branham preaches on the Angel of the Lord as a type of Christ, drawing parallels between the Exodus of Israel from Egypt and the spiritual deliverance of the Church today. He emphasizes the role of the Holy Spirit and angelic ministry in healing and preparing the Church for the end times.

title: As I Was With Moses
summary: William Branham speaks about his divine commission to pray for the sick, recounting the Angel of the Lord's appearance and the two signs given to vindicate his ministry. He encourages the congregation to have faith in Christ's healing power and prays individually for several people, demonstrating the gift of discernment.

title: My Commission
summary: William Branham shares his personal testimony of being called by God to pray for the sick, including the supernatural visitation of an angel and the gift of discernment. He emphasizes that faith without works is dead and encourages the audience to act on their faith in Jesus Christ for healing.

title: Believest Thou This?
summary: William Branham speaks on faith and healing, using the resurrection of Lazarus as a text. He shares personal testimony of his ministry and the physical and mental strain of spiritual work, encouraging believers to trust God even in the last moment.

title: At Thy Word
summary: William Branham preaches on the power of taking God at His Word, using the story of Peter's miraculous catch of fish as an illustration. He emphasizes that faith in God's Word brings healing and miracles, and shares testimonies of healings including Congressman Upshaw and King George VI.
themes: The Power of the Holy Spirit

title: Expectations
summary: William Branham speaks on the importance of expecting God's promises to be fulfilled, using the example of Simeon who waited for the Messiah. He encourages believers to look beyond symptoms and circumstances to God's Word, and to claim their healing through faith in Christ's atonement.

title: Faith Is the Substance
summary: William Branham teaches on faith as the substance of things hoped for, emphasizing that divine healing is already provided in the atonement and must be accepted by faith. He explains that faith is a real sense of the inward man, distinct from the five physical senses, and that healing comes through believing in what Jesus has already done. The sermon includes a call for ministers to pray for the sick and a demonstration of the gift of discernment as a sign of God's presence.
themes: The inward man vs. outward senses

title: Testimony
summary: William Branham shares testimonies of healings, including an elderly congressman and Apache Indians, and preaches on faith and the Holy Spirit's work. He emphasizes that Jesus is the same yesterday, today, and forever, and encourages the audience to believe in divine healing.

title: Expectation
summary: William Branham speaks on the theme of expectation, using the biblical example of Simeon who was led by the Holy Spirit to see the Christ child. He encourages the congregation to expect God's healing power and shares testimonies of healings and Spirit-led encounters.

title: The Manifestation of the Spirit
summary: William Branham opens a six-night revival in Toledo, emphasizing that divine healing is based on God's Word and the atonement of Christ. He shares his personal calling and the appearance of an angel, explaining that the prophetic gift is meant to increase faith for healing. He urges the audience to believe and accept Jesus as Healer.

title: The Angel of the Lord
summary: William Branham speaks about the Angel of the Lord, a supernatural light that appears in his meetings, and recounts various instances where the Angel was seen and photographed, including a famous event in Houston, Texas. He emphasizes that divine healing is part of the atonement and that faith in Christ is necessary for healing.

title: Who Hath Believed Our Report?
summary: William Branham preaches on the sovereignty of God in healing, emphasizing that he can only minister as the Father shows him through visions. He shares testimonies of healings, including Congressman Upshaw and a little girl in Finland, and reads from John 5 to illustrate Jesus' dependence on the Father.

title: The Angel of God
summary: William Branham preaches on the ministry of angels, particularly the Angel of the Lord, and shares testimonies of divine healing and visions. He emphasizes faith, the importance of God's Word, and the need to be led by the Spirit rather than human understanding.

title: Life of Demons, and Visions
summary: William Branham recounts a vision leading him to Milltown, Indiana, where he prays for a bedridden woman named Georgie Carter who is miraculously healed. He then ministers to others in a healing service, discerning illnesses through spiritual gifts.

title: Life Story
summary: William Branham shares his life story, from his impoverished childhood in Kentucky and Indiana to his early ministry. He reflects on family memories, the hardships of poverty, and the lessons learned, emphasizing the importance of faith and the hope of heaven.

title: The Second Miracle
summary: William Branham expresses gratitude for the warm reception in Toledo and shares testimonies of healings, including the use of prayer cloths. He reads from John 4 about the second miracle of Jesus, emphasizing that healing is already provided through Christ's atonement and must be accepted by faith.

title: The Church of the Living God
summary: William Branham preaches on faith and divine healing, using the story of the pool of Bethesda from John 5 to illustrate that God works in seasons and through His Word. He emphasizes that healing comes through faith in Christ's finished work, not through any human power, and shares testimonies of miraculous healings.
themes: the Word of God as seed
the Church as the body of believers

title: Three Witnesses
summary: William Branham speaks on the three witnesses that testify of Jesus Christ: God the Father, John the Baptist, and Jesus Himself. He shares testimonies of healings and visions, emphasizing faith over education and the importance of sincerity in ministry.

title: The Resurrection of Lazarus
summary: William Branham speaks on the resurrection of Lazarus, using it as a text to encourage faith in divine healing and the power of God. He emphasizes that Christians do not die but are separated from God, and that God's power is available to believers today.

title: The Second Miracle
summary: William Branham speaks on faith and healing, emphasizing that God's promises are sure even when symptoms persist. He shares testimonies of healings that occurred after the meetings, and teaches that faith is the substance of things hoped for, not dependent on physical senses. He also recounts the second miracle of Jesus healing the nobleman's son from a distance, illustrating the importance of believing God's word.

title: The Principles of Divine Healing
summary: William Branham speaks on the principles of divine healing, sharing testimonies of healings and emphasizing that healing comes from God alone, not from any human. He explains that faith in God's Word and a right mental attitude toward His promises bring healing, and that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever.
themes: the role of the Holy Spirit

title: At Thy Word
summary: William Branham speaks on the importance of spiritual gifts and the need for unity in the church. He shares testimonies of healings and a vision of a boy raised from the dead, emphasizing that God's Word is fulfilled through faith and obedience.

title: Our Hope Is In God
summary: William Branham speaks on the hope of the Church being in God alone, not in human power or weapons. He shares testimonies of healings and visions, including a boy raised from the dead in Finland and his own baby's healing, demonstrating that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever.

title: What Think Ye Of Christ?
subtitle: 51-0930A
summary: William Branham preaches on the deity of Christ, defending the virgin birth against scientific skepticism. He calls witnesses from Scripture and history to testify that Jesus is the Son of God, and emphasizes the power of His blood for salvation and healing.

title: Expectation
summary: William Branham speaks on the theme of expectation, using the biblical example of Simeon who waited for the Lord's Christ. He encourages believers to expect God's healing and presence, sharing testimonies of healings and divine guidance. The sermon closes the revival series in New York, with Branham expressing gratitude and preparing for a mission trip to Africa.

title: Believest Thou This?
summary: William Branham speaks on the importance of taking God at His Word, using the examples of Mary and Martha from John 11. He contrasts childlike faith with doubt and emphasizes the need for a living, present-tense relationship with God rather than relying on past experiences.

title: Believing God
summary: William Branham teaches on the nature of faith, using Abraham's willingness to sacrifice Isaac as a primary example. He emphasizes that true faith requires looking beyond physical circumstances to God's promises, and that believers must anchor God's Word in their hearts to see it produce results.
themes: The nature of the new birth

title: Early Spiritual Experiences
summary: William Branham shares his early spiritual experiences, including supernatural signs at birth, childhood visions, and the call to ministry. He emphasizes that gifts and callings are without repentance, given by God's grace, and recounts how the Holy Spirit led him to Hammond for a revival.

title: God Testifying of His Gifts
summary: William Branham speaks on the nature of divine healing, explaining that all healing comes from God and that sickness often stems from sin. He describes his own gift of discerning spirits and visions, emphasizing that he is not a healer but a vessel for God's power. He encourages faith and warns against fear, preparing the congregation for a prayer line.
themes: The role of the Holy Spirit

title: Faith in the Son of God
summary: William Branham speaks on faith in Jesus Christ, contrasting the tree of knowledge with the tree of life. He shares personal testimonies of healing and conversion, emphasizing that true faith transcends human understanding and that unbelief is the root of sin. He also recounts encounters with skeptics and the power of the Holy Spirit in discerning truth.

title: Thou Knowest All Things
summary: William Branham speaks on the power of prayer and faith, using the example of Hezekiah's prayer for extended life. He emphasizes that God knows all things and reveals secrets through the Holy Spirit, as seen in the ministry of Jesus and the apostles. Branham encourages believers to have faith and trust in God's sovereignty for healing and provision.

title: Get the People to Believe
summary: William Branham speaks about the importance of prayer and faith in healing, sharing his commission from the Angel of the Lord to pray for the sick. He emphasizes that healing comes from God alone and encourages the congregation to believe and be sincere in prayer. He then prays for individuals in a prayer line, demonstrating the power of faith.

title: For Him Will I Accept
summary: William Branham speaks on the power of prayer and the importance of unity among believers, using the story of Job to illustrate how God honors the prayers of the righteous. He emphasizes that healing is already provided through Christ's sacrifice and encourages the audience to believe and receive their healing.

title: Make the Valley Full of Ditches
summary: William Branham preaches on the biblical account of Elisha and the kings of Israel and Judah, emphasizing the need to dig ditches of faith to receive God's blessings. He warns against yoking with unbelievers and encourages the congregation to prepare their hearts for healing and the Holy Spirit's power.

title: Life Story
summary: William Branham shares his humble childhood in Kentucky and Indiana, recounting memories of poverty, family, and early struggles. He reflects on the importance of faith, the dangers of alcohol, and the hope of eternal life through Jesus Christ.

title: Who Has Believed Our Report?
summary: William Branham delivers a closing sermon in Hammond, Indiana, emphasizing faith in Jesus Christ as the same yesterday, today, and forever. He reads from Isaiah 53, declares that healing is already provided through the atonement, and demonstrates the Holy Spirit's presence through discernment and prayer for the sick.
themes: the role of the Holy Spirit

title: Experiences
summary: William Branham shares personal experiences and defends divine healing against critics, recounting a debate in Houston where a Baptist minister challenged him. He emphasizes that God is not the author of sickness and that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever, healing the sick through faith.
themes: the role of the Holy Spirit

title: Faith (Africa Trip Report)
summary: William Branham recounts his trip to South Africa, describing visions and divine guidance that led him to disobey the Lord's instructions, resulting in suffering and illness. He shares testimonies of healings and the consequences of stepping out of God's will, emphasizing the importance of following God's perfect will over human plans.

title: Led by the Holy Spirit
summary: William Branham speaks on being led by the Holy Spirit, using the examples of Simeon and Anna who were led to the infant Jesus. He encourages believers to expect God's promises and to be led by the Spirit in their own lives.

title: Deep Calleth Unto The Deep
summary: William Branham preaches on the faith of Simeon and Anna, who were led by the Holy Spirit to recognize the infant Jesus as the Messiah. He emphasizes that God's promises are fulfilled when believers take Him at His Word, and that the same Holy Spirit leads people to healing and salvation today.
themes: the deep calling to the deep

title: I Am The Resurrection And The Life
summary: William Branham speaks on the importance of serving God rather than money or popularity, sharing personal anecdotes about refusing offerings and his humble background. He then reads from John 11 about the raising of Lazarus, emphasizing faith in Christ as the resurrection and life, and encourages believers to take God at His Word without doubting.

title: Jesus Christ The Same Yesterday, Today, And Forever
summary: William Branham preaches on the unchanging nature of Jesus Christ, emphasizing that He is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He discusses divine healing, the atonement, and the importance of faith, using biblical examples such as the healing at the pool of Bethesda and the woman at the well to illustrate how Jesus only did what the Father showed Him.
themes: the role of visions in ministry

title: Faith (Africa Trip Report)
summary: William Branham recounts his experiences in Africa, emphasizing the importance of obeying God's direct guidance over human plans. He shares a vision where the Angel of the Lord instructed him not to follow a planned itinerary, leading to difficulties when he disobeyed. Branham applies this lesson to a recent decision to change meeting locations, urging listeners to prioritize God's will above all.

title: Expectancy
summary: William Branham speaks on the theme of expectancy, encouraging believers to expect God to move in their lives. He shares testimonies of healings and miracles, emphasizing that faith and expectation are key to receiving from God. He also discusses missionary plans for South Africa and India.

title: DO YOU NOW BELIEVE?
summary: William Branham preaches on the unchanging nature of Jesus Christ and the power of faith, recounting miracles including a boy raised from the dead and a crippled Finnish girl healed. He emphasizes that healing comes from God alone and that the Holy Spirit confirms the Word through signs and wonders.

title: Jesus Christ the Same Yesterday, Today, and Forever
summary: William Branham preaches on the unchanging nature of Jesus Christ, emphasizing that healing was accomplished at Calvary and that believers must accept it by faith. He demonstrates the gift of discernment as a confirmation of Christ's presence, and prays for the sick, urging them to believe in the finished work of Christ.
themes: Christ the same yesterday, today, and forever
The Word of God defeats Satan

title: Jesus Christ The Same Yesterday, Today, And Forever
summary: William Branham opens a revival meeting in Tallahassee, Florida, emphasizing that he is not a healer but that healing was already purchased at Calvary. He prays for the sick, demonstrating the Holy Spirit's ability to reveal hidden conditions and call people to faith in Christ.
themes: Jesus Christ the same yesterday, today, and forever
healing through faith in Christ's finished work
restoration of spiritual gifts in the last days

title: My Angel Shall Go Before Thee
summary: William Branham preaches on God's Angel leading His people, drawing from Exodus 23:20-23. He emphasizes that God has always had someone to work through, and that the same Holy Spirit who led Israel leads the church today. He encourages faith in divine healing, noting that prayer and belief in God's Word are powerful weapons against Satan.

title: Only Believe
summary: William Branham speaks on the importance of believing God's promises, using the example of Simeon who was promised he would not die before seeing the Christ. He encourages believers to trust in the redemptive blessings of Jesus and to exercise faith in the supernatural power of God.

title: All Things Are Possible To Them That Believe
summary: William Branham preaches on the power of belief, emphasizing that all things are possible to those who believe. He demonstrates the gift of discernment through prayer line healings, revealing specific conditions and personal details to individuals, and calls the congregation to accept their healing by faith.

title: Accept God's Gift
summary: William Branham preaches on accepting God's gift of salvation and healing through faith in Jesus Christ. He emphasizes that healing is already purchased at Calvary and must be received by confession and refusal of symptoms. He also discusses the Holy Spirit as a gift after believing.

title: Israel And The Church 1
summary: William Branham begins a five-night series on the Church, starting with Israel in Egypt. He emphasizes that salvation is by God's election and grace, not human works, and that the Old Testament is a shadow of the New. He teaches that God's covenant with Abraham is unconditional and fulfilled in Christ, and that the Holy Spirit is the seal of that covenant.
themes: Typology of Old and New Testaments
The Holy Spirit as the seal
The Church as the called-out people

title: Israel and the Church 2
summary: William Branham continues his study on the relationship between Israel and the Church, using Exodus as a type. He discusses election, justification, grace, and perfection through the patriarchs, and emphasizes the necessity of being born again by the Holy Spirit.

title: Israel and the Church 4
summary: William Branham continues his typological study of Israel's journey, comparing the Old Testament pilgrimage to the New Testament church. He focuses on the Israelites at Kadesh-barnea, where ten spies brought back an evil report of unbelief while Caleb and Joshua trusted God's promise. Branham applies this to the modern church, urging believers to have faith to enter the promised land of spiritual blessings.
themes: typology of Israel and the church
judgment beginning at the house of God
the sealing of the Holy Spirit
the contrast between true and false religion

title: Israel and the Church 5
summary: William Branham continues his series on Israel and the Church, drawing parallels between Joshua leading Israel into the Promised Land and the Church's journey today. He emphasizes the need to follow the Pillar of Fire (the Holy Spirit) rather than becoming trapped in organizations, and calls believers to put God first and cross their own Jordan.

title: The Cruelty of Sin, and the Penalty That It Cost to Rid Sin from Our Lives
summary: William Branham preaches on Good Friday about the cruelty of sin and the penalty required to remove it, using Isaiah 53 and the story of Cain and Abel to illustrate that only God's provided sacrifice—the blood of Christ—can atone for sin. He emphasizes the necessity of being born again and receiving the Holy Spirit, contrasting human efforts with God's way.

title: Witnesses
summary: William Branham preaches on the theme of being a witness for God, drawing from Acts 1:8. He emphasizes that a true witness must have a personal experience with God, not just secondhand knowledge. Using Old Testament examples like Noah, Shadrach, Meshach, Abednego, and David, he illustrates how God stands by those who courageously witness for Him, even through trials.

title: Prayer
subtitle: 53-0405M
summary: A prayer delivered on Easter morning, reflecting on the resurrection of Christ and the hope of resurrection for believers. The speaker thanks God for Christ's victory over death and prays for forgiveness and faithfulness.

title: Go, Tell My Disciples
summary: In this Easter sermon, William Branham reflects on the resurrection of Jesus Christ as the foundational proof of His divinity. He contrasts the fear of death seen in unbelievers with the hope and victory believers have through Christ's resurrection, emphasizing that Jesus alone has power over death. Branham encourages believers to trust in the resurrection promise and to recognize Christ's presence in their lives.

title: Jesus Christ the Same Yesterday, Today, and Forever
summary: William Branham speaks at the Bible Hour Tabernacle in Jonesboro, Arkansas, reflecting on his past meetings there and the faithfulness of God. He emphasizes that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever, and that divine healing is already provided at Calvary, requiring only faith to receive it. He illustrates this through biblical examples, including Jesus' encounter with Nathanael and the woman at the well, showing that Jesus only did what the Father showed Him.
themes: Jesus Christ the same yesterday, today, and forever

title: Expectations
summary: William Branham teaches on the character of Jesus Christ and how His Spirit works today, emphasizing that believers must expect God's promises to be fulfilled. He contrasts true faith with counterfeit spirituality, urging the congregation to claim their legal rights as children of God and refuse to accept Satan's afflictions.
themes: the Word of God as a seed

title: God Commissioning Moses
summary: William Branham preaches on God commissioning Moses and the importance of using what God has placed in your hand. He encourages believers to have faith and courage, using biblical examples like David and Goliath, Shamgar, and Samson to illustrate that God can use anyone who trusts Him.

title: The Pillar of Fire
summary: William Branham preaches on the Pillar of Fire that led Israel, identifying it as the Angel of the Covenant, Jesus Christ, who is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He shares personal testimony of a supernatural photograph taken in Houston, Texas, which he presents as scientific proof of the supernatural Being leading the Church today. He encourages believers to trust in God's leading and not to fear, as the same God who led Israel is present with them.

title: Testimony
summary: William Branham shares a testimony of God's healing power, recounting a vision of two Easter flowers that foretold the healing of a Finnish boy and the raising of another from the dead. He emphasizes faith in God's Word and the Holy Spirit's work today, urging believers to trust in Jesus Christ, the same yesterday, today, and forever.

title: We Have Found Him, Come And See
summary: William Branham preaches on the encounter between Philip and Nathanael, emphasizing that when one finds Jesus, they should invite others to 'come and see.' He discusses the importance of personal faith and confession in receiving healing, and demonstrates the gift of discernment by revealing specific conditions and sins to individuals in the congregation.
themes: The supernatural nature of the new birth

title: Speak to the Rock
summary: William Branham preaches on the resurrection and the importance of speaking to the Rock, Christ Jesus, for salvation and healing. He emphasizes that God's Word must be quickened by the Spirit and that faith comes by hearing and believing. The sermon includes a prayer line and demonstrations of the Holy Spirit's presence.

title: God's Provided Way
summary: William Branham preaches on God's provided way for salvation and healing, using the example of Moses lifting up the brass serpent in the wilderness. He emphasizes that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever, and that healing is already provided through the atonement. He encourages believers to trust in God's provision and to look to Christ for their needs.

title: Seeking After Jesus
summary: William Branham opens a revival meeting in Indiana, emphasizing that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He discusses divine healing, the importance of faith, and how Jesus' ministry is continued through the Holy Spirit in the church today. The sermon includes prayer for the sick and demonstrations of spiritual gifts.
themes: Jesus Christ the same yesterday, today, and forever
the role of the Holy Spirit in the church
rejection of Christ by religious leaders

title: Whatever He Says To You, Do It
summary: William Branham preaches on the importance of doing whatever Jesus says, using the wedding at Cana as a text. He emphasizes faith over hope, the reality of divine healing, and the presence of the Holy Spirit to confirm God's Word. The sermon includes prayer for the sick and several demonstrations of the gift of knowledge.

title: The Authority Of The Word
summary: William Branham preaches on the authority of God's Word and faith, using the centurion's story to illustrate that faith does not rely on symptoms but on God's spoken Word. He demonstrates the gift of discernment through prayer for the sick, calling out specific conditions and encouraging the congregation to accept their healing.

title: God Commissioning Moses
summary: William Branham preaches on God commissioning Moses and leading Israel by a pillar of fire, drawing parallels to the present-day ministry of the Holy Spirit. He shares a testimony of a supernatural photograph taken in Houston, Texas, as evidence of the same pillar of fire today, and emphasizes that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever.
themes: Jesus Christ the same yesterday, today, and forever

title: The Angel of the Lord
summary: William Branham preaches on the Angel of the Lord, emphasizing that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He shares testimonies of healings, including Congressman Upshaw and a young girl with tuberculosis, to demonstrate God's power and the importance of faith. Branham encourages believers to trust in God's Word and the Holy Spirit's work.

title: The Beginning of Jesus' Fame
summary: William Branham preaches on the unchanging nature of Jesus Christ, emphasizing that He is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He shares testimonies of divine healing, including the healing of Reverend Hall from cancer and the provision of a clinic for Dr. Sam Adair, demonstrating that God's power is still active today.

title: An Ensign
summary: William Branham preaches on the biblical typology of the brass serpent lifted by Moses as an ensign, connecting it to Christ's crucifixion as the ultimate ensign for salvation and healing. He emphasizes that looking to Jesus in faith brings both forgiveness and physical healing, and demonstrates the Spirit's discernment through a prayer line.

title: The Ministry of Christ
summary: William Branham preaches on the early ministry of Christ, using the raising of Lazarus as a central text. He emphasizes taking God at His Word, as exemplified by Mary's faith, and contrasts it with Zacharias's doubt. The sermon also touches on the need for a fresh daily experience with God.
themes: power of the name of Jesus

title: A Testimony
summary: William Branham shares a testimony of God's healing power, recounting a vision of a boy raised from the dead in Finland and a crippled girl healed. He emphasizes that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever, and that God confirms His Word through signs and wonders.
themes: Jesus Christ the same yesterday, today, and forever

title: Demonology, Physical Realm
summary: William Branham discusses the nature of demons and their role in sickness and disease, explaining that all sickness originates from Satan. He uses the analogy of a bear cub eating honey to illustrate the joy of the Holy Spirit, and delves into the spiritual and physical aspects of healing, emphasizing that faith is essential to maintain healing after a demon is cast out.
themes: the role of the Holy Spirit

title: At Thy Word
summary: William Branham opens a week of services, thanking God and the local officials. He preaches on taking God at His Word, using the story of Peter launching out into the deep at Jesus' command, and encourages believers to act on their faith.

title: Demonology, Religious Realm
summary: William Branham discusses demonology, explaining how demons can impersonate Christianity and work among believers. He shares personal experiences, including a vision about a future African crusade, and emphasizes the importance of testing spirits by Scripture and fruit.

title: MAKE THE VALLEY FULL OF DITCHES
summary: William Branham preaches on the need for faith and the moving of God's Spirit, using the story of Elisha and the kings of Israel and Judah. He emphasizes that God's presence is with those who respect Him and His Word, and encourages believers to seek a double portion of the Spirit.
themes: the double portion of the Spirit

title: Jesus Christ The Same Yesterday, Today, And Forever
summary: William Branham preaches on the unchanging nature of Jesus Christ, demonstrating through prayer and healing that Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He calls the congregation to faith and repentance, leading many to salvation and the baptism of the Holy Spirit.

title: Show Us The Father And It'll Satisfy Us
summary: William Branham speaks on the deep human longing to see God, using nature, Scripture, and personal experience to reveal God's presence. He emphasizes that God is visible in His creation, His Word, His Son, and His people, and that true satisfaction comes from seeing the Father through faith.

title: Palmerworm, Locust, Cankerworm, Caterpillar
summary: William Branham confesses that he has relied too much on the gift of discernment instead of simply praying for the sick as God commanded. He criticizes false healing practices and calls for unity among Pentecostal groups. He then reads from Joel 1:4 and discusses the spiritual condition of the church in the last days.

title: God's Provided Way
summary: William Branham shares testimonies of divine healing, including a woman healed by a prayed-over handkerchief and a demon-possessed woman delivered. He then preaches on God's provided way of salvation through Jesus Christ, using Old Testament types like Noah's ark and the Passover lamb to illustrate that God always provides a way of escape before judgment.

title: Earnestly Contending For The Faith That Was Once Delivered To The Saints
summary: William Branham preaches on Jude 3, urging believers to earnestly contend for the original faith delivered to the saints. He contrasts true faith with religious imitation, using Cain and Abel as examples of sincere but misguided worship versus God-ordained sacrifice. Branham emphasizes the need for a living, supernatural faith demonstrated by the power of the Holy Spirit.

title: I Perceive That Thou Art a Prophet
summary: William Branham speaks on the gifts of the Spirit, distinguishing between the gift of prophecy and the office of a prophet. He shares testimonies of healings and emphasizes that healing comes through personal faith in Christ. He also discusses the importance of financial integrity in ministry and the signs of the times.

title: Questions and Answers on Genesis
summary: William Branham answers questions about the creation of man in Genesis, explaining the difference between the spirit man created in God's image (Genesis 1:26-28) and the physical man formed from dust (Genesis 2:7). He discusses the pre-existence of souls, the origin of Eve, and where Cain got his wife, emphasizing that all races come from the same human stock.

title: The Testimony of Jesus Christ
summary: William Branham preaches on the testimony of Jesus Christ, emphasizing that Jesus is the same yesterday, today, and forever, and that His works continue through the Church. He shares a testimony of a man healed from cancer through a divine vision and message, and then ministers to the sick, demonstrating the Spirit's discernment and power.

title: Why I Am a Holy-Roller
summary: William Branham explains why he identifies with the term 'holy-roller' by tracing the biblical lineage of true faith from Genesis onward. He contrasts the faith of Abel, Israel, and the early church—marked by signs and wonders—with mere fundamentalism that lacks divine vindication. Branham argues that the genuine church has always been a phenomenal people, persecuted by religious fundamentalists but vindicated by God through supernatural manifestations.

title: Come And See
subtitle: 53-0830E
summary: William Branham preaches on the importance of believing God's Word and the supernatural power of Christ. He reads John 1:44-51, focusing on Philip's invitation to Nathanael to 'come and see' Jesus. Branham then prays for the sick, demonstrating the gift of discernment and healing through the Holy Spirit.

title: God Talked to Moses
summary: William Branham preaches on the journey of Israel as a type of the Church, emphasizing the need to destroy spiritual enemies and claim God's promises. He contrasts the formalized churches with the moving of the Holy Spirit, and encourages believers to fight for their healing and baptism of the Holy Spirit.
themes: the Church as a called-out people
the Pillar of Fire as a type of the Holy Spirit

title: Lord, I Believe
summary: William Branham preaches on the healing of the blind man in John 9, emphasizing that faith must be accompanied by works. He prays for the sick, calling out specific ailments and encouraging believers to act on their faith.
themes: the power of the Holy Spirit

title: Testimony
summary: William Branham shares personal testimonies of God's grace and healing power, including a lesson about not judging others, a woman healed of a nose cancer, a demon-possessed woman delivered, and a blind girl healed in a parking lot. He emphasizes the importance of faith in Jesus Christ as the Healer.

title: Expectancy
summary: William Branham preaches on the theme of expectancy, using the biblical account of Simeon and Anna in the temple to illustrate how God leads those who are looking for Him. He emphasizes that God always has a witness and that the same Holy Spirit who led Simeon to see the Christ child leads people today to receive healing and salvation. The sermon includes a prayer line where Branham demonstrates the gift of discernment, revealing specific conditions and personal details to strangers as a sign of God's presence.

title: Healing (What Cancer Is)
summary: William Branham teaches on the nature of cancer as a spirit and explains the process of divine healing, emphasizing that healing is already provided at Calvary and must be received by faith. He also conducts a prayer line, demonstrating the gift of discernment and calling out specific conditions.

title: Faith Without Works Is Dead
summary: William Branham preaches on the necessity of faith accompanied by works, using James 2 as his text. He shares testimonies of healing and discernment, emphasizing that unconfessed sin blocks healing and that faith must be acted upon. The service includes prayer for the sick and a demonstration of the gift of discernment.

title: Believest Thou This?
summary: William Branham preaches on the resurrection of Lazarus from John 11, emphasizing faith in Jesus as the Resurrection and Life. He contrasts doubt with childlike faith, using examples like Mary's acceptance of Gabriel's message and the power of Jesus' name. He also shares personal anecdotes about missions, healing, and the need for genuine Christian love.

title: The Living Jesus Christ
summary: William Branham preaches on the living Jesus Christ, emphasizing His resurrection and continued work through the Holy Spirit. He shares testimonies of healings among Apache Indians and calls believers to have simple faith in God's Word.

title: Lord, Show Us The Father And It Sufficeth Us
summary: William Branham speaks on the longing to see God, using John 14:8 as a text. He explores seeing God in His universe, nature, and Word, and encourages believers to trust the Holy Spirit's leading over human organizations.

title: Healing Line
summary: William Branham conducts a healing service in Chicago, praying for the sick and demonstrating the gifts of the Spirit through words of knowledge and healing. He emphasizes faith in Jesus Christ as the Healer and encourages the congregation to believe and receive their healing.
themes: The power of the Holy Spirit
The Church as the body of Christ

title: Elijah
summary: William Branham uses the story of Elijah to call for spiritual preparation and unity among believers, emphasizing the need for heartfelt repentance and prayer to break the drought and bring revival. He warns that America's prosperity and moral decline mirror Israel's apostasy, urging individuals and churches to return to God.

title: Taking God at His Word
summary: William Branham preaches on the nature of faith as the sixth sense, contrasting it with the five physical senses. He emphasizes taking God at His Word, using the example of Peter letting down his net at Jesus' command, and encourages believers to trust in God's promises for healing and salvation.

title: Deep Calleth Unto The Deep
summary: William Branham preaches on the principle that a deep calling requires a deep to respond, using illustrations from nature, electricity, and healing. He explains the gift of visions and healing, demonstrating God's power through prayer and deliverance from deaf spirits and other ailments.

title: DO YOU NOW BELIEVE?
summary: William Branham preaches on the necessity of faith and the confirmation of God's Word through signs and wonders. He shares testimonies of healings and miracles, including a little boy raised from the dead in Finland and a woman healed of cancer, to encourage believers to trust in Christ as Healer and Saviour.

title: Jesus Christ The Same Yesterday, Today, And Forever
summary: William Branham demonstrates the gift of discernment and healing, showing that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He prays for individuals, revealing their conditions and bringing healing through faith. The sermon emphasizes that Jesus healed all believers 1900 years ago and that accepting this truth brings healing.
themes: Jesus Christ the same yesterday, today, and forever

title: Life Story
summary: William Branham shares his life story, from his impoverished childhood in Kentucky and Indiana to his calling by God. He recounts early hardships, his father's alcoholism, and his own determination to avoid sin, culminating in a divine encounter that set him apart for ministry.

title: Expectancy
summary: William Branham preaches on the theme of expectancy, using the biblical example of Simeon who waited for the Messiah. He encourages believers to expect God's intervention and healing, emphasizing that faith in God's Word brings results. The sermon includes prayer for the sick and demonstrations of spiritual gifts.

title: How the Angel Came to Me
summary: William Branham shares personal testimonies of divine healing and the ministry of the Angel of the Lord. He discusses the nature of faith, the baptism of the Holy Spirit, and the importance of obedience to God's word. The sermon includes accounts of healings and the role of visions in his ministry.

title: I Will Restore
summary: William Branham preaches on the restoration of the Church, using Joel 2:25 as a text. He contrasts true spiritual life with dead formalism, tracing the seed of the Church from Cain and Abel through Israel and the Reformation to the present day, emphasizing that God vindicates His people by signs and wonders.

title: Preparation
summary: William Branham speaks on the theme of divine preparation, explaining how God always prepares His people before major events. He contrasts man-made religion with God's provision, using examples from Eden, Noah, Moses, and Samson to illustrate that God's ways often seem foolish to human reason but are always effective. He calls for a genuine new birth and baptism of the Holy Spirit as the only true preparation for the last days.
themes: New birth and Holy Spirit baptism
God's ways seem foolish to man

title: Demonology
summary: William Branham discusses the reality of demons and spiritual warfare, contrasting true spiritual gifts with counterfeit spiritualism. He uses the example of a healing miracle featured in Reader's Digest to illustrate God's power, and warns against deception by demonic spirits that mimic the Holy Spirit.
themes: the Word of God as standard

title: Africa Trip Report
summary: William Branham shares his experiences from a missionary trip to Africa, recounting miraculous healings and visions. He emphasizes the importance of obeying God's direction over human plans, and describes how the Angel of the Lord appeared to confirm his ministry.

title: Speak to the Rock
summary: William Branham preaches on the journey of Israel from Egypt to the Promised Land as a type of the Christian experience, emphasizing the importance of staying under the blood of Christ and being filled with the Holy Spirit. He warns of coming judgment and urges repentance and a deep relationship with God.

title: A Greater Witness
summary: In this closing sermon of a revival in Owensboro, Kentucky, William Branham expresses gratitude to the congregation and emphasizes that healing comes through faith in Jesus Christ, not through any human gift. He reads from John 5:36 about the greater witness of Christ's works and calls the audience to accept their healing by faith, demonstrating God's presence through visions and prayer.
themes: The presence of the Holy Spirit
The role of prophets and gifts

title: Prayer Line
summary: William Branham conducts a prayer line, calling out various ailments and conditions through spiritual discernment. He emphasizes faith in Jesus Christ as the healer and encourages the congregation to believe for their healing.

title: Demonology
summary: William Branham shares his personal experiences with demonic spirits, including visions of demons leaving people and a dramatic confrontation with a possessed man in Portland. He discusses the importance of sincerity and faith in casting out devils, and recounts recent healings and the need for believers to cooperate fully with God.
themes: the role of the Holy Spirit

title: Brass Serpent
summary: William Branham preaches on the brass serpent in Numbers 21 as a type of Christ's crucifixion, emphasizing that looking to Jesus brings healing and salvation. He shares testimonies of healings and discusses the nature of God as Father, Son, and Holy Ghost.
themes: the nature of God as triune

title: The Resurrection of Lazarus
summary: William Branham speaks on the resurrection of Lazarus, emphasizing faith in God's power and the importance of believing in Jesus Christ as the resurrection and the life. He shares testimonies of healing and discusses the need for a genuine, Spirit-filled faith beyond mere church membership.

title: Prayer Line
summary: William Branham conducts a prayer line, calling out specific ailments and personal details of individuals in the congregation through the gift of discernment. He prays for healing and deliverance, encouraging faith in Jesus Christ. The sermon includes testimonies of healings and calls for repentance.

title: The Faith That Was Once Delivered To The Saints
summary: William Branham speaks on the need to earnestly contend for the faith once delivered to the saints. He contrasts the worship of Cain and Abel, emphasizing that true faith requires being born again, not just outward religion. He calls for a return to Holy Ghost revival and moral integrity.

title: Testimony
summary: William Branham shares a personal testimony about a debate on divine healing in Houston, Texas, where he and F.F. Bosworth defended the biblical basis of healing. He recounts how a supernatural light was photographed, providing scientific proof of God's presence. Branham also tells of healing miracles, including Florence Nightingale's granddaughter and King George VI.

title: Has The Lord Spoken Only To Moses?
summary: William Branham preaches on the power of the Gospel and the importance of believing in divine healing. He uses the story of Miriam and Aaron questioning Moses to illustrate the danger of speaking against God's servant. Branham shares testimonies of healings, including Congressman Upshaw, to demonstrate that God's power is still active today.
themes: The Gospel as power and demonstration

title: God's Provided Way
summary: William Branham preaches on God's provided way of escape through faith in His Word, using examples from Noah, Job, Moses, and the Passover. He emphasizes that salvation and healing come only through the Blood of Jesus Christ, and that believers must separate from the world and trust God's Word regardless of how foolish it may seem.
themes: the ark as a type of Christ

title: Testimony (Raising Dead Boy)
summary: William Branham shares a testimony about a vision he received of a little boy being raised from the dead, which he believed would come to pass. He encourages believers to claim God's promises by faith, using the example of Israel taking possession of the Promised Land. He also reflects on the importance of following the Spirit's leading rather than human reasoning.

title: At Thy Word
summary: William Branham shares personal testimonies of divine guidance and healing, emphasizing the importance of obeying the Holy Spirit's leading. He recounts stories of miraculous healings and visions, illustrating God's sovereignty and love for all people regardless of race or status.

title: The Resurrection
summary: William Branham preaches on the resurrection, emphasizing that believers will be restored to their youthful perfection. He contrasts the power of God's Word against Satan, discusses the sealing of the Holy Spirit, and calls for a return to old-fashioned Holy Ghost revival.

title: Life Story
summary: William Branham recounts the tragic loss of his father, brother, wife, and baby within a short period, leading him to contemplate suicide. He describes a vision of heaven where he meets his deceased daughter and wife, which renews his faith and commitment to God.

title: DO YOU NOW BELIEVE?
summary: William Branham speaks on the closing night of a small meeting, expressing gratitude and emphasizing the importance of sincerity and faith. He shares testimonies of healings and visions, including a story about Dr. Sam Adair's clinic and a woman's deliverance from nervousness through confession of sin. He concludes by reading John 5:33-36 and John 16:27-31, asking the congregation, 'Do you now believe?'
themes: the unchanging nature of Jesus Christ

title: The Inside Man
summary: William Branham speaks on the need for soul travail and unity among believers, emphasizing that sin is unbelief and that the Holy Spirit within believers enables them to do greater works. He uses the story of the brass serpent in Numbers 21 to illustrate faith and healing.

title: Faith
summary: William Branham speaks on faith, using the Exodus account of God sending an angel before Israel to illustrate that God's promises are already given and must be possessed by faith. He shares personal experiences of divine intervention and healing, emphasizing the need to abide in Christ and reject unbelief.

title: What Think Ye Of Christ?
summary: William Branham preaches on the identity of Jesus Christ as the Son of God, using biblical testimonies and personal anecdotes to affirm the virgin birth and Christ's divinity. He encourages believers to have faith in God's promises and to recognize the power of Christ's name.

title: Questions and Answers
summary: William Branham answers questions about the afterlife, explaining that believers go immediately into God's presence while sinners face judgment. He also discusses the meaning of Exodus 4:24, where God sought to kill Moses for neglecting circumcision, and interprets Isaiah 4:1 as a prophecy of moral decay in the last days.

title: Questions and Answers
summary: William Branham addresses various questions from the congregation, including whether one should be rebaptized, the position of the church when the Gospel returns to the Jews, and the identity of the giants in biblical times. He also shares personal updates about his overseas ministry and a vision concerning Brother George Wright.

title: Jairus and Divine Healing
summary: William Branham speaks on the nature of faith, divine healing, and the story of Jairus from Luke 8. He emphasizes the importance of believing God's Word, the reality of spiritual forces behind sickness, and the need to separate from unbelief. He also prays over handkerchiefs for the sick.
themes: the role of the Holy Spirit

title: Jesus On The Authority Of The Word
summary: William Branham speaks on the authority of God's Word, emphasizing that it must be confirmed by the Holy Spirit to become effective. He shares testimonies of healings, including Congressman Upshaw and a paralyzed girl, illustrating how God's Word is made manifest through visions and faith.
themes: the role of the Holy Spirit

title: Expectation
summary: William Branham shares testimonies of healing, including a woman delivered from insanity, and encourages believers to expect God's power. He reflects on Simeon's expectation of seeing the Messiah and urges the congregation to trust in God's promises.

title: At Thy Word, Lord
summary: William Branham preaches on the importance of taking God at His Word, using the story of Peter letting down the net at Jesus' command. He encourages the congregation to believe and confess their healing despite circumstances, sharing personal testimonies and experiences from his ministry.

title: Expectation
summary: William Branham opens a series of meetings in Phoenix, expressing joy at being in the 'valley of the sun' and preaching about the Son, Jesus Christ. He discusses the importance of faith, love, and unity among believers, and outlines his ministry approach of mixing healing services with Gospel preaching. He emphasizes that all blessings come from accepting Christ and that unbelief is the root of sin.

title: Looking For Jesus
summary: William Branham speaks about the unchanging nature of Jesus Christ, emphasizing that He is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He discusses the importance of faith, the role of the Holy Spirit in healing, and the need for the Church to demonstrate the power of God as Jesus did.
themes: Jesus Christ the same yesterday, today, and forever

title: The Angel of the Covenant
summary: William Branham preaches on the Angel of the Covenant, the Pillar of Fire that led Israel, identifying it as Christ. He encourages believers to possess their healing by faith, using the example of Israel taking the Promised Land. He also discusses the progressive movement of the Spirit through church history.

title: The Resurrection of Jairus' Daughter
summary: William Branham preaches on the resurrection of Jairus' daughter, emphasizing faith over symptoms and the importance of believing God's Word despite circumstances. He encourages the audience to trust in Jesus as the same yesterday, today, and forever, and to make contact with Him through faith.
themes: Jesus Christ the same yesterday, today, and forever
the Holy Spirit in the Church

title: Witnesses
summary: William Branham preaches on the necessity of being a witness for Christ through the baptism of the Holy Spirit, emphasizing that a true witness must have a personal experience of God's power. He uses biblical examples like Moses, David, and Shamgar to illustrate how God uses ordinary people who have encountered His glory to accomplish extraordinary things.

title: Elijah and Elisha
summary: William Branham preaches on the biblical account of Elijah and Elisha, drawing parallels to Christ and the Church. He emphasizes the need for faith, the power of the Holy Spirit, and the importance of digging spiritual trenches to receive God's blessings.

title: God's Provided Way of Dealing with Sin
summary: William Branham preaches on God's provided way for dealing with sin, emphasizing that human efforts are insufficient and only God's way through Jesus Christ's sacrifice brings salvation and healing. He uses biblical examples like Adam and Eve, Cain and Abel, and Isaiah's prophecy to illustrate God's plan, and calls for faith in Christ as the only means of redemption.

title: The Unconditional Covenant That God Made With His People
summary: William Branham speaks on God's unconditional covenant with Abraham, emphasizing that salvation and healing are based on God's election and promise, not human effort. He encourages believers to recognize their identity as Abraham's seed and to trust God's Word regardless of circumstances.

title: The End Time
summary: William Branham speaks on the urgency of missions, recounting his experiences in Africa where thousands converted through the power of the Holy Spirit. He then uses the book of Joel to discuss the end times, tracing the origin of religious confusion back to Cain and Abel, and emphasizing the need for spiritual renewal.

title: Do You Now Believe?
summary: In this closing sermon of a Phoenix campaign, William Branham expresses gratitude to supporters and shares testimonies of healing. He emphasizes that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever, and calls the congregation to believe in His resurrection power. The sermon includes a vision of a future overseas revival and a prayer for the sick.
themes: Unity in the body of Christ

title: Why I'm Praying for the Sick
summary: William Branham explains his background and calling to pray for the sick, emphasizing that healing was accomplished at Calvary and must be accepted by faith. He shares personal experiences, including visions and the Angel of the Lord, to validate his ministry and the reality of Jesus Christ as the same yesterday, today, and forever.
themes: the need for supernatural confirmation of the Gospel

title: Faith Cometh By Hearing
summary: William Branham speaks on the nature of faith, emphasizing that true faith comes by hearing the Word of God. He contrasts hope with faith, explaining that hope looks to the future while faith claims the promise now. Using biblical examples like Abraham, Sarah, Hannah, and Mary, he illustrates how faith is based solely on God's Word.

title: What Think Ye of Christ?
summary: William Branham preaches on the deity of Jesus Christ, asking the question 'What think ye of Christ?' He examines testimonies from biblical figures, enemies, friends, and hymn writers to affirm that Jesus is the virgin-born Son of God. Branham emphasizes that one's attitude toward Christ determines their eternal destiny.

title: Sirs, We Would See Jesus
summary: William Branham opens a revival in Louisville, emphasizing that God is the Divine Healer and that healing was completed at Calvary. He reads from John 12:20-22 about Greeks seeking Jesus, and explains that the true desire of every heart is to see Jesus, not just learn theology. He encourages faith and orderly worship, and prepares to pray for the sick.

title: Redemption By Power
summary: William Branham continues a series on redemption, moving from redemption by blood to redemption by power. Using the Exodus account, he draws parallels between Israel's deliverance from Egypt and the believer's journey from sin to salvation, emphasizing faith, the Holy Spirit's guidance, and God's power to overcome obstacles.

title: Redemption in Completeness, in Joy
summary: William Branham preaches on the journey of Israel as a type of the believer's redemption, covering redemption by blood, by power, and the baptism of the Holy Spirit. He encourages the congregation to step out in faith and experience the fullness of God's provision, including divine healing and the joy of the Holy Spirit.

title: The Resurrection of Jairus' Daughter
summary: William Branham shares testimonies of divine healing and visions, then preaches on the raising of Jairus' daughter, emphasizing faith, the need to press through doubt and criticism, and the importance of complete surrender to God.

title: God's Preparation
summary: William Branham speaks on the dual conscious and subconscious in relation to faith and healing, then reads from Luke 2 about Simeon. He emphasizes that God always prepares and sends warnings before judgment, using examples from Noah, Elijah, and the first coming of Christ. He contrasts the faith of Mary with the doubt of Zacharias, urging believers to trust God's Word completely.

title: Blind Bartimaeus
summary: William Branham preaches on the story of blind Bartimaeus, emphasizing faith and God's provision through the Lamb of God. He shares testimonies of healings through prayer cloths and calls the congregation to believe in Jesus' healing power.

title: The Hand of the Lord Came Upon Him
summary: William Branham preaches on the story of Elisha and the kings of Israel, emphasizing the need to get into the Spirit to receive God's guidance and power. He calls for a revival of genuine faith, digging out doubt and unbelief to receive the living water of the Holy Spirit.
themes: The double portion of the Spirit

title: God Has A Provided Way
summary: William Branham speaks on God's provided way of approach, escape, and provision for every need, using the story of Abraham and Isaac, the wilderness journey of Israel, and the Book of Ruth as types of Christ's redemptive work. He emphasizes faith in God's Word and the atoning sacrifice of Jesus Christ for salvation and healing.

title: Earnestly Contending for the Faith
summary: William Branham preaches on Jude's exhortation to earnestly contend for the faith once delivered to the saints. He contrasts the early church's power and unity with modern denominational divisions and spiritual decline, urging a return to apostolic faith marked by signs, wonders, and holiness.

title: Thy Faith Has Saved Thee
summary: William Branham preaches on the story of blind Bartimaeus, emphasizing that faith in Jesus Christ can stop Him and bring healing. He contrasts the religious leaders' unbelief with Bartimaeus's persistent faith, and encourages the audience to have an audience with Jesus, who is the same yesterday, today, and forever.
themes: Jesus Christ the same yesterday, today, and forever

title: The Invasion Of The United States
summary: William Branham discusses the spiritual condition of the United States and the church, using the Old Testament story of King Ahab and Jehoshaphat as a warning against making alliances with unbelievers and lukewarm Christianity. He criticizes the commercialization and glamorization of the Gospel, calling for a return to old-fashioned, sincere repentance and holiness.
themes: the danger of alliances with unbelievers

title: The Seven Church Ages
summary: William Branham introduces a series of teachings on the Seven Church Ages from the Book of Revelation, emphasizing the need for the Church to understand prophecy and the times. He discusses the background of Revelation, the role of the Holy Spirit, and the importance of being in the Spirit to receive divine revelation.

title: The Mark Of The Beast
summary: William Branham preaches on the Mark of the Beast, a vital subject for the end times. He explains the third angel's message from Revelation 14, warning against worshiping the beast and receiving its mark. Branham contrasts this with the Seal of God, emphasizing the need to discern between God's brand and Satan's brand according to Scripture.

title: The Seal of God
summary: William Branham preaches on the Seal of God, contrasting it with the Mark of the Beast. He emphasizes that both marks are spiritual, not physical, and warns against apostasy and reliance on church organizations over walking in the light of God's Word.

title: Questions and Answers
summary: William Branham answers questions from the congregation about the mark of the beast, the image of the beast, and the connection between Protestant and Catholic churches. He emphasizes that the Holy Spirit is the Seal of God and warns against organized religion that replaces the Bible with creeds.

title: Questions and Answers (Law Having a Shadow)
summary: William Branham addresses the congregation on church order, spiritual gifts, and the work of grace. He explains the distinction between justification, sanctification, and the baptism of the Holy Spirit, emphasizing that the Holy Spirit is the true teacher and guide. He also corrects misunderstandings about speaking in tongues and the proper use of spiritual gifts in the church.
themes: Justification, Sanctification, Baptism of the Holy Spirit
Unity and Love in the Church

title: Prayer Line
summary: William Branham discusses the importance of discerning God's will and the dangers of presumption, using the example of Moses striking the rock twice. He shares his experiences with the gift of discernment and healing, emphasizing that it is God who heals, not man. The sermon includes a prayer line where many are healed through faith in Jesus Christ.
themes: The power of the Holy Spirit

title: I Will Restore
summary: William Branham preaches on the two spirits represented by Cain and Abel, tracing them through Scripture from Genesis to Revelation. He contrasts mere religious fundamentalism with God's vindication through signs and wonders, urging believers to seek the Holy Spirit's confirmation of their faith.

title: Divine Healing
summary: William Branham speaks on divine healing, sharing personal testimonies and visions, and uses the story of blind Bartimaeus to illustrate faith. He emphasizes that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever, and that faith can bring healing.
themes: the role of the Holy Spirit

title: The Deep Calleth to the Deep
summary: William Branham preaches on the principle that deep calls to deep, using the example of Simeon and Anna who were led by the Holy Spirit to see the Christ. He explains that the desire for healing or the Holy Spirit proves there is a source to fulfill it, and he demonstrates this through prayer line healings and visions.
themes: the same yesterday, today, and forever

title: The Great Coming Revival and the Outpouring of the Holy Spirit
summary: William Branham speaks on the signs of the end times, emphasizing that the world is nearing the second coming of Christ. He draws parallels between biblical events (Noah, Sodom, the star of Bethlehem) and current world events, urging listeners to recognize the signs and prepare for the coming revival and outpouring of the Holy Spirit.

title: To See Jesus
summary: William Branham opens an eight-day campaign in Chicago, expressing his desire for revival and healing. He preaches on the theme of seeing Jesus, emphasizing that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever, and that He manifests Himself through the Holy Spirit in the church today.
themes: Jesus Christ the same yesterday, today, and forever
the Holy Spirit's work in the church
the danger of unbelief and blasphemy against the Holy Spirit

title: God's Provided Way of Healing
summary: William Branham teaches on the nature of faith for divine healing, emphasizing that true faith comes by revelation from the Holy Spirit and must be received, not merely believed intellectually. He contrasts the gift of prophecy with the office of a prophet, and explains that God has always provided a way of healing for His people, using the example of Moses and the children of Israel.
