title: God Providing Healing For This Generation
summary: William Branham preaches on God as Jehovah-jireh, the Lord who provides, using the story of Abraham and Isaac and the ram caught in the thicket. He emphasizes that God has provided healing for this generation through Jesus Christ, and that the Holy Spirit continues to manifest His presence with signs and wonders.

title: The Maniac of Gadara
summary: William Branham shares his testimony of the Angel of the Lord and the supernatural photograph taken in Camden, Arkansas. He then preaches on the story of the demon-possessed man from Gadara, emphasizing Jesus' power over demons and His willingness to cross any storm to save a single soul.

title: IT IS I, BE NOT AFRAID
summary: William Branham preaches on Jesus walking on water, emphasizing that Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He encourages believers not to be afraid of supernatural manifestations, as they are signs of Jesus' presence and power to heal and save.

title: Sirs, Be of a Good Cheer
summary: William Branham encourages the congregation to have faith in God's promises, using the account of Paul's shipwreck in Acts 27. He prays over prayer cloths, shares a testimony of a vision about Brother Bosworth, and ministers healing through the gift of discernment.

title: WHATEVER HE SAITH UNTO YOU, DO IT
summary: William Branham preaches on the importance of doing whatever Jesus says, using the wedding at Cana as a text. He shares personal testimonies of divine guidance and healing, emphasizing obedience and faith over knowledge. The sermon includes prayer for the sick and a call to love one another.

title: The Prophet Elisha
summary: William Branham preaches on the Old Testament prophet Elisha, drawing parallels between Elisha's ministry and the church today. He emphasizes the importance of separating from unbelief, seeking God's guidance, and having faith for miracles. The sermon includes a testimony of a demon-possessed woman healed through prayer.

title: A Personal Experience With God
summary: William Branham preaches on the necessity of a personal experience with God, drawing from biblical examples like Moses, David, Samson, and Shamgar. He emphasizes that the church today needs a fresh vision and the baptism of the Holy Spirit to restore faith and power, and shares testimonies of divine healing, including Congressman Upshaw's healing after 66 years in a wheelchair.

title: Do You Now Believe?
summary: William Branham preaches on the unchanging nature of Jesus Christ, emphasizing that He is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He demonstrates the gift of discernment through prayer for the sick, calling out specific ailments and bringing healing to many in the congregation.

title: Jairus
summary: William Branham preaches on the story of Jairus, a synagogue ruler who sought Jesus to heal his dying daughter. He contrasts Jairus's borderline faith with the woman with the issue of blood, emphasizing the need for complete surrender to God. The sermon culminates in a healing service where Branham calls out specific ailments by the Holy Spirit's anointing.

title: Simeon
summary: William Branham preaches on Simeon, an old sage who was promised by the Holy Spirit that he would see the Christ before he died. Branham draws parallels between Simeon's faith and expectation and the need for believers today to expect God's promises, including healing. He emphasizes that the Holy Spirit leads believers to Jesus, just as He led Simeon and Anna to the infant Christ.

title: I Will Restore Unto You, Saith The Lord
summary: William Branham preaches on the restoration promised by God in Joel, using the allegory of two vines from Genesis—Cain and Abel—to contrast mere fundamentalism with Spirit-filled, sign-vindicating faith. He calls for a return to old-fashioned Holy Ghost revival and warns against dead religious forms.

title: The Manifestation of Thy Resurrection to the People of This Day
summary: William Branham preaches on the resurrection power of Jesus Christ, demonstrating healing through the Holy Spirit. He calls the audience to faith, recounts biblical stories of healing, and prays for the sick, emphasizing that Jesus is the same yesterday, today, and forever.

title: Prayer Line
summary: William Branham conducts a prayer line, demonstrating the gift of discernment by revealing specific details about individuals' lives and ailments, such as heart trouble, kidney issues, and family concerns. He emphasizes that Jesus Christ is present to heal and save, calling for faith and repentance.

title: Show Us The Father
summary: William Branham preaches on seeing God in His universe, His Word, His Son, and His people. He uses nature illustrations and biblical references to encourage faith in God's promises and the power of the Holy Spirit.

title: Prayer Line
summary: William Branham conducts a prayer line, calling on the congregation to have faith in Jesus Christ for healing. Through the gift of discernment, he reveals specific ailments and personal details about individuals, declaring their healing in Jesus' name.

title: Jesus Christ The Same Yesterday, Today, And Forever
summary: William Branham preaches on the power of confession and faith in God's Word, using the story of Hezekiah and Isaiah to illustrate how prayer changes things. He emphasizes that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever, and demonstrates the gift of discernment through the Holy Spirit, calling out specific ailments and personal details to confirm God's presence and healing power.
themes: The High Priest of our Confession
Jesus Christ the Same Yesterday, Today, and Forever

title: The Unconditional Covenant That God Made With The People
summary: William Branham preaches on God's unconditional covenant with Abraham and his seed, emphasizing that salvation and healing are by grace alone, not by human works. He encourages believers to trust in God's promises and not be fearful, using Abraham's faith as an example.

title: Jesus Christ the Same Yesterday, Today, and Forever
summary: William Branham opens a campaign in New York City, emphasizing that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He discusses the need for unity among believers, the signs of the times, and the importance of faith in Christ for healing and salvation.

title: We Have Found Him
summary: William Branham opens the service with prayer, then explains his ministry of praying for the sick through the gift of discernment. He reads John 1:44-50 about Philip finding Nathanael, and demonstrates the Holy Spirit's presence by revealing specific conditions and personal details to individuals in the prayer line, calling them to faith in Christ's finished work.

title: I Will Restore, Saith the Lord
summary: William Branham preaches on the restoration promised by God in Joel 2:25, using the allegory of the tree eaten by locusts and caterpillars. He contrasts the spirits of Cain and Abel, emphasizing that true salvation comes through a spiritual revelation of Jesus Christ, not mere religious works or church membership.

title: Jesus Christ The Same Yesterday, Today, And Forever
subtitle: 54-0829E
summary: William Branham preaches on the unchanging nature of Jesus Christ, emphasizing that healing comes from God alone and that faith in Christ is essential. He demonstrates the gift of discernment through the Holy Spirit, revealing specific ailments and personal details to individuals in the audience, leading to healings and deliverances.

title: South Africa Testimony
summary: William Branham shares testimonies from his ministry in South Africa, including healings and visions, and discusses the importance of obedience to God's will. He also addresses the need for revival and the dangers of sin and unconfessed sin in hindering healing.
themes: The role of the Holy Spirit

title: Jubilee Year
summary: William Branham preaches on the concept of the Jubilee Year from the Old Testament, drawing parallels to the present time of grace and the Holy Spirit's outpouring. He warns against rejecting the Holy Spirit and emphasizes the urgency of accepting Christ before the opportunity passes.

title: The Word Became Flesh (India Trip Report)
summary: William Branham reports on his missionary trip to India and other countries, describing the poverty, superstitions, and religious diversity he encountered. He recounts miracles performed, including healing a deaf and dumb boy and a blind man, and calls for prayer and support for India.

title: Law or Grace
summary: William Branham contrasts the Old Testament law with the grace of Jesus Christ, emphasizing that animal sacrifices under the law could not take away sin, but Christ's perfect sacrifice provides eternal redemption. He encourages believers to rest in Christ's perfection rather than their own works.

title: The Unpardonable Sin
summary: William Branham teaches on the unpardonable sin, explaining that it is not suicide, abortion, or backsliding, but willful sin after receiving knowledge of the truth—specifically, rejecting and despising the blood of Jesus Christ. He emphasizes the importance of being born again, sealed by the Holy Spirit, and walking in boldness and love.

title: Redemption By Judgment
summary: William Branham discusses the importance of faith in God's Word, using the story of Moses lifting up the brass serpent and Israel at Kadesh-barnea as types of redemption through judgment. He emphasizes that true faith is based on God's promises, not circumstances, and calls believers to stand firm on the Word.

title: The Law Having a Shadow
summary: William Branham speaks on the law as a shadow of good things to come, explaining that animal sacrifices could not make the worshiper perfect, but Christ's one sacrifice perfects forever those who are sanctified. He emphasizes being born again and sealed by the Holy Spirit, and encourages believers to stand on God's Word rather than feelings.

title: We Would See Jesus
summary: William Branham preaches on the theme that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever, using the story of the Greeks who wanted to see Jesus and the woman at the well to illustrate that Jesus still manifests His power today. He challenges the congregation to believe that Jesus is alive and can heal and save as He did in biblical times.
themes: Jesus Christ the same yesterday, today, and forever

title: Expectation
summary: William Branham speaks on the theme of expectation, using the biblical figure Simeon as an example of one who expected to see the Lord's Christ. He shares personal testimonies of visions and healings, emphasizing the importance of faith and confession of sin. Branham encourages believers to expect God's blessings and revival, despite criticism from others.

title: At Thy Word, Lord, I'll Let Down the Net
summary: William Branham speaks on the importance of faith and confession in receiving healing, using the biblical account of Peter letting down his net at Jesus' word. He emphasizes that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever, and that believers should trust God's Word regardless of circumstances.
themes: Jesus Christ the same yesterday, today, and forever
the role of the Holy Spirit

title: He Swore By Himself
summary: William Branham preaches on the Abrahamic covenant, emphasizing that God swore by Himself to confirm His promise to Abraham. He explores the relationship between the Old Testament types and New Testament realities, particularly regarding divine healing and the security of believers. The sermon encourages steadfast faith and endurance, grounded in God's unchangeable oath.

title: Acts of the Holy Spirit
summary: William Branham speaks on the Acts of the Apostles as the acts of the Holy Spirit, emphasizing the necessity of being filled with the Holy Spirit to do God's work. He shares testimonies of healings and visions, and teaches on the rejection of the cornerstone, the importance of the revelation of Jesus Christ, and the unity of the true Church.

title: Divine Healing
summary: William Branham preaches on divine healing, emphasizing that all Scripture is inspired and that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He encourages believers to have faith in God's Word and to expect the same miracles and healings that occurred in the early church.

title: Everlasting Life and How to Receive It
summary: William Branham shares testimonies of God's healing power, including a baby healed through the Holy Spirit's leading. He emphasizes that everlasting life is received by believing on the Lord Jesus Christ, not through outward signs or works. He calls the church to unity and prayer in the last days.

title: Beginning and Ending of the Gentile Dispensation
summary: William Branham preaches on the Gentile dispensation from Daniel's prophecies, emphasizing the rise and fall of Gentile kingdoms, the coming of Christ as the Stone cut without hands, and the signs of the end times including the restoration of Israel and the outpouring of the Holy Spirit.

title: Melchisedec, The Great Prince And King
summary: William Branham teaches on the assurance of faith based on God's immutable promises, using Hebrews 6-7 and Genesis 14. He emphasizes that God swore by Himself to bless Abraham and his Seed, Christ, and that believers have an anchor of the soul within the veil through Jesus, a high priest after the order of Melchisedec.

title: The Fundamental Foundation for Faith
summary: William Branham preaches on the foundational basis for faith, explaining that man was originally created to have dominion over all things but lost that through the fall. Through Christ's redemption, believers are restored to that original state and can operate in faith when they abide in Christ and His Word. He emphasizes that faith is an unconscious trust in God's Word, and that the Holy Spirit works through believers to manifest the same works Jesus did.

title: Doctor Moses
summary: William Branham preaches on the biblical account of Moses lifting up the brass serpent in the wilderness as a type of Christ's crucifixion. He emphasizes that healing and salvation come through spiritual revelation and faith in God's Word, not through human effort or psychology. Branham also shares testimonies of healings and encourages the congregation to seek a genuine revival through repentance and confession.
themes: Typology of Christ in the Old Testament

title: Law
summary: William Branham preaches on the law as a shadow of good things to come, contrasting the imperfect sacrifices of the Old Testament with the perfect and final sacrifice of Jesus Christ. He emphasizes that true perfection comes through faith in Christ's blood, which cleanses sin and transforms the believer, and warns against willful unbelief as the unpardonable sin.

title: The Believer's Position in Christ
subtitle: 55-0116A
summary: William Branham teaches on the believer's position in Christ, emphasizing that believers are chosen before the foundation of the world and must be in Christ through the Blood to worship God. He uses the Old Testament tabernacle and the story of Moses to illustrate God's timing and the need for direct revelation. The sermon concludes with the concept of adoption into God's family, where believers are given authority and a specific ministry.

title: Jesus Christ the Same Yesterday, Today, and Forever
summary: William Branham speaks on the unchanging nature of Jesus Christ, emphasizing that He is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He shares testimonies of healings and deliverances, and calls the congregation to faith in Christ's finished work at Calvary.

title: How The Angel Came To Me, And His Commission
summary: William Branham recounts his early life and the supernatural experiences that shaped his ministry, including visions, an encounter with Jesus, and the commissioning by an angel. He emphasizes that gifts and callings are without repentance and shares lessons learned about discerning true spirituality.

title: This Great Warrior, David
summary: William Branham preaches on David as a type of the believer who is elected, called, anointed, and placed in Christ. He contrasts David's faith with Israel's reliance on outward appearances and human wisdom, urging believers to trust God's Word and their position in Christ.

title: This Great Warrior, Joshua
summary: William Branham preaches on Joshua as a type of Christ and the believer's position in God. He contrasts the faith of Joshua and Caleb with the unbelief of Israel at Kadesh-Barnea, drawing parallels to the modern church's hesitation to fully embrace the Holy Spirit and divine healing. Branham emphasizes that God's promises are sure and that believers must fight spiritually to possess their inheritance.

title: The Seven Compound Names of Jehovah
summary: William Branham preaches on the seven compound names of Jehovah, focusing on Jehovah-jireh (the Lord will provide a sacrifice) and Jehovah-shammah (the Lord is present). He emphasizes that God is always present to fulfill His redemptive promises, using the story of Abraham and Isaac as a type of Christ's sacrifice.

title: The Water of Separation
summary: William Branham preaches on the Old Testament type of the red heifer and the water of separation, showing how it prefigures Christ's sacrifice and the cleansing power of the Word. He emphasizes that life comes through death, and that believers are separated from sin and sickness by applying the Word of God. The sermon concludes with a healing service where Branham demonstrates the gift of discernment.

title: This Great Servant, Moses
summary: William Branham preaches on the life of Moses, focusing on the rod of judgment as a type of Christ. He draws parallels between Moses' rod and the cross, emphasizing that Christ bore judgment for sin and sickness. The sermon encourages believers to speak to the Rock, Christ Jesus, for healing and deliverance.

title: The Approach to God
summary: William Branham preaches on the necessity of approaching God through His provided way, which is the shed blood of Jesus Christ. He contrasts man's self-made approaches with God's ordained method, using examples from Adam, Job, Abraham, and Israel. The sermon emphasizes that only through the blood sacrifice can one have an audience with God and receive His blessings.
themes: El Shaddai as the all-sufficient One

title: Earnestly Contend for the Faith
summary: William Branham preaches on Jude 3, urging believers to earnestly contend for the faith once delivered to the saints. He contrasts the original apostolic faith—characterized by signs, wonders, and divine revelation—with modern denominational divisions, emphasizing that true Christianity is the life of Christ reproduced in believers through the Holy Spirit.

title: The Second Coming
summary: William Branham opens a revival meeting in Phoenix, discussing his ministry policies, the importance of preaching the Gospel to all the world, and sharing experiences from his missionary trip to India. He emphasizes that the Gospel must be accompanied by the power and demonstration of the Holy Spirit, and expresses his belief that the second coming of Christ is near.

title: Contend For The Faith
summary: William Branham opens a series of meetings, emphasizing that healing and salvation come through faith in the finished work of Christ, not human power. He explains the gift of discernment and visions as a means to build faith, and urges believers to contend for the faith once delivered to the saints, as exemplified by Jesus' ministry of supernatural knowledge and healing.
themes: God's attitude toward sinners and sick

title: Christ
summary: William Branham preaches on Christ as the fulfillment of Old Testament types, focusing on the red heifer sacrifice in Numbers 19 as a symbol of Christ's blood for redemption and purification. He emphasizes that fellowship with God is only possible through the shed blood of Jesus, and calls believers to come to the waters of separation—the Word—and enter into the blood for true fellowship and power.

title: Jehovah-Jireh
summary: William Branham preaches on the redemptive name Jehovah-Jireh, emphasizing God's provision and the unconditional covenant with Abraham. He encourages faith in God's promises, drawing from the story of Abraham and Isaac, and calls believers to trust in El Shaddai, the all-sufficient God.

title: Job
summary: William Branham preaches on the theme of redemption, using the story of Job as a central example. He emphasizes that redemption was planned before the foundation of the world and is accomplished through the shed blood of Christ, the Lamb of God. Branham encourages believers to trust in God's provided way of redemption and to live in the freedom that Christ has secured.

title: Water From The Rock
summary: William Branham preaches on the Old Testament story of Moses striking the rock at Meribah, using it as a lesson about obeying God's specific instructions. He contrasts his own healing ministry with others, emphasizing the need to find the cause of sickness before the cure. He also discusses the journey of Israel as a type of the church, the importance of following the Spirit, and the danger of grumbling and division among believers.

title: Glorified Jesus
summary: William Branham speaks on the spiritual revelation of Jesus Christ as the foundation of the Church, using Matthew 16:15-18 as a text. He contrasts the offerings of Cain and Abel to illustrate that true faith comes from divine revelation, not human effort. The sermon emphasizes the hope of resurrection and being buried in Christ.

title: The Position Of A Believer In Christ
summary: William Branham shares about a powerful healing meeting with Apache Indians, then teaches on the believer's position in Christ, emphasizing that true faith comes from being baptized by the Holy Spirit into Christ's body, bearing the fruit of the Spirit, and working in harmony with God's laws.
themes: fruit of the Spirit vs. gifts of the Spirit

title: The Healing of Jairus' Daughter
summary: William Branham preaches on the healing of Jairus' daughter, emphasizing faith in Christ's atonement and the power of the Holy Spirit. He contrasts the Old Testament sacrificial system with Christ's sacrifice, which imparts eternal life through the Holy Spirit. Branham encourages believers to touch Jesus by faith, regardless of opposition or doubt.
themes: the Holy Spirit as the life of Christ

title: Separation from Unbelief
summary: William Branham speaks on the importance of separating from unbelief and worldly associations, using the biblical account of Jehoshaphat's alliance with the wicked king Jehoram as a cautionary example. He emphasizes that true faith comes from the heart through the Holy Spirit, not from intellectual knowledge, and warns against being unequally yoked with unbelievers.
themes: The Holy Spirit's role in healing

title: Elijah
summary: William Branham preaches on the Shunammite woman's faith and persistence in seeking the prophet Elisha when her son died. He emphasizes the importance of going forward in faith, not slacking, and trusting God's servants. The sermon encourages believers to maintain their faith even when circumstances seem hopeless.
themes: the power of God through His prophets

title: The Resurrected Lord Jesus
summary: William Branham speaks on the resurrected Lord Jesus, emphasizing that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He encourages believers to have faith in God's healing power and shares personal testimonies of God's intervention.

title: The Seal Of The Antichrist
summary: William Branham preaches on the seal of the antichrist, warning against religious spirits that mimic true Christianity. He emphasizes that outward signs like speaking in tongues or shouting do not guarantee salvation; only receiving the Person of Jesus Christ and bearing the fruits of the Spirit matter. Using the Old Testament type of the Hebrew servant who chose to remain in bondage, he illustrates how rejecting truth leads to being sealed out of God's Kingdom.

title: The Seal of the Christ
summary: William Branham contrasts the seal of the Antichrist with the seal of Christ, emphasizing that the true seal of God is the Holy Spirit, which produces the fruit of the Spirit in believers. He warns against mere religious formality and emotionalism, stressing that only those who sigh and cry over the abominations in the city receive God's seal.
themes: Seal of God vs. seal of the beast
Fruit of the Spirit as evidence of salvation
Rejection of truth leads to judgment

title: Fellowship By Redemption
summary: William Branham speaks on the theme of fellowship with God through redemption. He shares testimonies of healings from recent meetings, announces plans for a healing service and baptism on Easter Sunday, and teaches that true fellowship with God requires a new foundation in Christ, not mere reformation. He emphasizes that faith must go beyond intellectual acceptance to a born-again experience.
themes: The Word of God as eternal truth
The presence of God in the believer

title: Prayer
subtitle: 55-0410E
summary: William Branham offers a prayer of thanksgiving for the privilege of coming to God, for the hope of resurrection, and for the church and its members. He asks for God's blessing on the service and for the Word to be planted in hearts.

title: Proof of His Resurrection
summary: William Branham delivers an Easter sermon emphasizing the resurrection of Jesus Christ as a present reality, not just a historical event. He argues that the Holy Spirit's work in believers, including healing and spiritual gifts, provides infallible proof that Christ is alive today. Branham calls for a personal experience of the resurrection through faith and the new birth, moving beyond tradition and intellectual belief.

title: My Redeemer Liveth
summary: In this Easter sermon, William Branham celebrates the resurrection of Jesus Christ as the central hope of Christianity. He contrasts the empty rituals of dead religion with the living assurance that comes from experiencing the resurrected Christ personally. Drawing on Job's declaration 'I know my Redeemer liveth,' he calls believers to move beyond mere hope to a confident 'know-so' faith.

title: Fellowship
summary: William Branham speaks on the theme of fellowship with God and with one another, emphasizing that true fellowship is only possible through the blood of Jesus Christ. He contrasts this with denominational divisions and worldly substitutes, urging believers to return to a blood-bought revival and a carefree trust in God.

title: The Faith That Was Once Delivered to the Saints
summary: William Branham speaks on the faith that was once delivered to the saints, emphasizing that true faith is a direct revelation from God, not intellectual belief. He uses examples from the Bible, such as Abel, Peter, and the woman at the well, to illustrate that this faith is accompanied by signs and wonders. Branham also shares personal anecdotes and reflects on the passing of Brother Ryan.

title: The Ark
summary: William Branham teaches on the typology of the ark in the Old Testament, showing how Noah's ark, Moses' basket, and the ark of the covenant all foreshadow Christ as the ultimate ark of salvation. He emphasizes that believers are sealed by the Holy Spirit and protected from judgment through the atonement of Christ's blood.

title: Jesus Christ the Same Yesterday, Today, and Forever
summary: William Branham preaches on the unchanging nature of Jesus Christ, emphasizing that the same signs and wonders that accompanied Jesus in the Bible should be present in the church today. He calls believers to contend for the faith once delivered to the saints, which includes divine healing and the operation of spiritual gifts.

title: Jairus, A Secret Believer
summary: William Branham speaks on faith based on God's Word, using the story of Jairus as a secret believer who sought Jesus for his dying daughter. He emphasizes that prayer changes things and that true faith rests on God's promises, not human reasoning.

title: Fellowship Through The Reconciliation of The Blood
summary: William Branham speaks on the necessity of fellowship with God through the blood of Jesus Christ, emphasizing that true fellowship is not found in church membership, education, or good works, but only through the shed blood of Christ. He uses the examples of Adam and Eve, Cain and Abel, and Job to illustrate that reconciliation with God requires a spiritual revelation and acceptance of God's provided sacrifice.

title: The Waters of Separation
summary: William Branham preaches on the Old Testament type of the red heifer and the waters of separation, showing how it prefigures Christ's sacrifice and the cleansing power of the Word. He emphasizes that the Word is the waters of separation that cleanses believers from sin and sickness, and calls for a heart-faith rather than mere intellectual assent.

title: The True Vine and a False Vine
summary: William Branham contrasts the true vine (Abel's line) with the false vine (Cain's line), tracing these two spirits through Scripture from Genesis to the end times. He warns against religious sincerity without divine revelation and emphasizes that the true church is marked by the supernatural power of the Holy Spirit, not by organization or intellectual theology.
themes: The church's departure from supernatural faith

title: Abraham
summary: William Branham speaks on the faith of Abraham, emphasizing God's sovereign election and the importance of taking God at His Word regardless of circumstances. He recounts the debate in Houston where the Angel of the Lord was photographed, and explains the covenant God made with Abraham as a type of the New Covenant in Christ.

title: A Greater Witness Than John
summary: William Branham preaches on the greater witness of Jesus Christ compared to John the Baptist, emphasizing that Jesus' works bear witness of Him. He shares a testimony of being led by the Holy Spirit to pray for a dying man in Memphis, and then ministers to the sick with the gift of discernment.

title: DO YOU NOW BELIEVE?
summary: William Branham speaks on the power of love and faith in healing, sharing personal testimonies of miracles and the importance of creating an atmosphere of belief. He emphasizes that God's presence brings healing and encourages the congregation to trust in God's Word.

title: What Is That In Thy Hand?
summary: William Branham preaches on the power of God to use whatever we have in our hands, using the examples of Moses' rod and David's sling. He encourages believers to trust God's promises and step out in faith, even with seemingly small resources.

title: The Presence of the Lord Jesus
summary: William Branham speaks at the close of a revival meeting in Macon, Georgia, sharing testimonies of healings and a resurrection in Finland. He emphasizes the presence of Jesus Christ and the importance of faith, using the story of Lazarus to illustrate that Jesus is the resurrection and the life.

title: Contending For The Faith
summary: William Branham preaches on Jude 1:3, urging believers to earnestly contend for the faith once delivered to the saints. He emphasizes that true faith rests on God's Word, not creeds or denominations, and demonstrates the same works of Jesus through the Holy Spirit, including healing and discernment.
themes: the Word of God as foundation

title: The Roman Nobleman
summary: William Branham preaches on the faith of the Roman centurion who believed Jesus could heal his servant with just a word. He emphasizes that healing comes through faith in Christ's finished work at Calvary, not through any human power. Branham then demonstrates the gift of discernment by calling out specific ailments and conditions in the audience, leading many to receive healing.

title: Abraham
summary: William Branham speaks on the faith of Abraham, emphasizing that God's promises are seeds that produce when received without unbelief. He connects Abraham's encounter with God in Genesis 18 to the ministry of Jesus and the present-day manifestation of God's power through visions and healings.

title: Show Us The Father
summary: William Branham preaches on seeing God in His creation, His Word, His Son, and His people. He encourages faith and healing, demonstrating the Holy Spirit's presence through prayer and discernment.

title: My Life Story
summary: William Branham shares his personal testimony, from his humble birth in a log cabin to his call to ministry. He recounts the hardships of his early life, the loss of his wife and daughter, and his commitment to preach the Gospel despite persecution.

title: I Will Restore
subtitle: 55-0626E
summary: William Branham preaches on the restoration of the church, contrasting the spirit of Cain (formalism, dead religion) with the spirit of Abel (spiritual revelation, signs and wonders). He uses Joel 2:25 as his text, promising that God will restore the years that the locusts have eaten. Branham calls for a return to the power of Pentecost and warns against denominations that deny the supernatural.

title: Enticing Spirits
summary: William Branham warns against 'enticing spirits' that lead believers away from the Word of God, using the biblical account of King Jehoshaphat and the prophet Micaiah to illustrate how false prophets and demonic influences can deceive even sincere people. He emphasizes the need for genuine Holy Ghost conversion over intellectual faith, emotionalism, or worldly substitutes in the church.

title: The Uncertain Sound
summary: William Branham preaches on the need for a certain sound in the Gospel, contrasting the uncertainty of the world with the certainty found in Christ and His Word. He warns against relying on intellectual reasoning rather than the soul's connection to God, and emphasizes the importance of a genuine new birth experience.
themes: The power of the Holy Spirit

title: Jesus Christ the Same Yesterday, Today, and Forever
summary: William Branham preaches on the unchanging nature of Jesus Christ, emphasizing that the faith delivered to the early saints must be contended for today. He contrasts intellectual reasoning with soul-faith, and uses biblical examples to show that God vindicates His Word through supernatural works.

title: Pride
summary: William Branham preaches on the sin of pride, using the story of Simon the Pharisee inviting Jesus to dinner. He contrasts the Pharisee's self-centered motives with Jesus' humility, and warns against acting like a Pharisee—putting on a show rather than being genuine. Branham emphasizes that Jesus takes the lowly place and calls believers to humble themselves.

title: Leading of the Spirit of God
summary: William Branham preaches on being led by the Spirit of God, using the examples of Simeon and Anna who were expecting the Messiah. He contrasts faith and expectation with education and formalism, emphasizing that God's promises are fulfilled to those who believe and are led by the Holy Spirit.

title: Fellowship
summary: William Branham speaks on the importance of fellowship with God through the blood of Jesus Christ. He explains that divine healing is part of the atonement and encourages believers to have faith like Abraham, accepting God's promises without doubt. He also contrasts man-made religion with God's provision of the blood sacrifice.

title: Earnestly Contending For The Faith That Was Once Delivered Unto The Saints
summary: William Branham preaches on Jude 3, urging believers to earnestly contend for the original faith delivered to the saints. He emphasizes that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever, and demonstrates this through prayer for the sick, including discernment of illnesses and visions.

title: Jehovah-Jireh
summary: William Branham preaches on God's compound redemptive names, focusing on Jehovah-Jireh, meaning 'God will provide Himself a sacrifice.' He uses the story of Abraham and Isaac to illustrate God's provision and faithfulness, and encourages the congregation to believe in God's promises for healing and salvation.

title: Blind Bartimaeus
summary: William Branham preaches on the story of blind Bartimaeus, emphasizing that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He encourages the congregation to have faith and believe in Jesus as their healer, and demonstrates the gift of discernment through prayer for the sick.

title: Being Led By The Holy Spirit
summary: William Branham speaks on being led by the Holy Spirit, using the example of Simeon who was promised he would see the Christ before he died. He emphasizes that the same Holy Spirit leads believers today, and demonstrates the power of God through healing and discernment.
themes: Being Led by the Holy Spirit

title: The Same Jesus Tonight
summary: William Branham preaches on the unchanging nature of Jesus Christ, emphasizing that He is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He recounts the story of Lazarus and Martha, highlighting faith in Jesus as the Resurrection and Life. Branham then demonstrates the Holy Spirit's power through words of knowledge and healing, calling the audience to believe in Jesus' presence and power.

title: The Unwelcomed Christ
summary: William Branham preaches on the story of Simon the Pharisee and the sinful woman who anointed Jesus' feet, contrasting the Pharisee's lack of hospitality with the woman's loving devotion. He urges believers to give Jesus first place in their lives and not to treat Him as unwelcome.
themes: the value of tears and devotion

title: Sir, We Would See Jesus
summary: William Branham shares testimonies of healings and visions, emphasizing that Jesus is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He calls the audience to have faith in Christ for healing and salvation, demonstrating the gift of discerning spirits and prophecy.

title: The Unwelcomed Christ
summary: William Branham recounts his recent overseas meetings in Switzerland and Germany, describing opposition from state churches and miraculous healings including a blind girl and a deaf-mute man. He defends his ministry against accusations of witchcraft, presents photographic evidence of the Angel of the Lord, and reflects on the need for unity among believers. The sermon then transitions to a dramatic exposition of Luke 7:36-50, focusing on the Pharisee's hidden motives and the sinful woman's love.

title: Prayer Line
summary: William Branham conducts a prayer line, calling out specific ailments and personal details of attendees through the gift of discernment. He emphasizes faith in Jesus Christ for healing and encourages the audience to believe and accept their healing.

title: The Unwelcomed Christ
summary: William Branham preaches on the story of Simon the Pharisee inviting Jesus to dinner but failing to welcome Him, contrasting the Pharisee's hypocrisy with the love of a sinful woman who anoints Jesus' feet. He urges believers to genuinely welcome Christ into their hearts and homes, not just invite Him.

title: Faith In Action
summary: William Branham speaks on the importance of putting faith into action, using biblical examples like Noah, Moses, David, and Jesus. He encourages believers to trust God's Word wholeheartedly and not rely on intellectual faith alone, emphasizing that God is the same today as in biblical times.

title: Come, Let Us Reason Together
summary: William Branham addresses ministers and laity, explaining the nature of spiritual gifts and visions, emphasizing that gifts are given by God's sovereignty and operate through faith. He uses parables and biblical examples to illustrate how the gift of healing works, and calls for unity and reason among believers.

title: The Power of the Devil
summary: William Branham preaches on the power of the devil, faith, and God, using the Book of Exodus as a foundation. He emphasizes that Satan's dominion ends at death, but God's power of resurrection goes beyond. He calls believers to exercise faith, trust in God's Word, and claim healing through Christ's atonement.

title: A Hidden Life
summary: William Branham speaks on the need for a hidden life with Christ, using the Old Testament tabernacle as a type of the believer's walk from the outer court to the Holy of Holies. He emphasizes entering into the secret place with God, where the veil drops behind and one lives in the Shekinah glory, eating the hidden manna and bearing fruit. He calls ministers to seek this place of adoption and rest in God's presence.

title: The Power of God
summary: William Branham preaches on the power of faith and God's deliverance, using the Exodus account of Moses' mother and the Red Sea crossing as examples. He emphasizes that faith sees beyond death and trials to God's resurrection power, and that God's promises are sure despite opposition.

title: The Power of Decision
summary: William Branham preaches on the power of decision, using the Exodus of Israel as a type of the Church's journey. He emphasizes following the Pillar of Fire (Holy Spirit), living by faith, and partaking of the spiritual manna. He also shares personal experiences of the Holy Spirit's intercession and healing.

title: The Results of Decision
summary: William Branham preaches on the journey of Israel from Egypt to the Promised Land as a type of the Church's spiritual journey. He emphasizes the power of decision, faith, and God's provision, urging believers to cross over into the full blessings of the Gospel rather than remaining on the borderline.

title: The Way To Have Fellowship
summary: William Branham speaks on the necessity of love and fellowship with God through the shed blood of Jesus Christ. He emphasizes that perfect love casts out fear and that true fellowship with God and one another is only possible through the Blood of Christ. He shares personal experiences of how love conquers fear and brings divine protection.

title: A Hidden Life in Christ
summary: William Branham preaches on the necessity of a consecrated, hidden life in Christ, using the Old Testament tabernacle as a type. He contrasts the outer courts and holy place with the Holiest of Holies, where believers can dwell in constant communion with God, bearing lasting fruit.

title: Where I Think Pentecost Failed
summary: William Branham discusses the failure of Pentecostalism, emphasizing the need for a genuine born-again experience over intellectual religion. He critiques organizational stagnation and calls for continued movement with the Holy Spirit, using biblical typology to illustrate spiritual progression.

title: Jesus Christ the Same Yesterday, Today, and Forever
summary: William Branham preaches on the unchanging nature of Jesus Christ, emphasizing that divine healing is part of the atonement and that believers must contend for the faith once delivered to the saints. He shares personal experiences and challenges the church to demonstrate the same works Jesus did, proving His resurrection.

title: The Darkest Hour, Then Jesus Comes Along
summary: William Branham preaches on the theme that in the darkest moments of life, Jesus arrives to bring deliverance. He uses the story of Lazarus, Martha, and Mary to illustrate how Jesus allows trials to deepen before He intervenes, and he explains the operation of spiritual gifts and visions in his ministry.

title: Blind Bartimaeus
summary: William Branham preaches on the story of blind Bartimaeus, emphasizing faith that stops Jesus amidst the crowd. He contrasts the simplicity of faith in other nations with the skepticism in America, and encourages believers to keep their thoughts positive and focused on Christ.

title: The Calling of Abraham
summary: William Branham preaches on the calling of Abraham from Genesis 12, emphasizing God's sovereign election and unconditional covenant. He contrasts Abraham's faith, which believed God's promise despite natural impossibility, with worldly skepticism, and encourages believers to hold fast to God's Word.

title: Jehovah-Jireh
summary: William Branham preaches on God as Jehovah-Jireh, the Lord who provides a sacrifice, using the story of Abraham and Isaac. He connects this Old Testament name to Jesus Christ and emphasizes that God is the all-sufficient provider for both spiritual and physical needs, including healing. Branham encourages believers to trust in God's promises and lean on His bosom for strength and satisfaction.

title: The Faith of Abraham
summary: William Branham preaches on the faith of Abraham, emphasizing that God's promises are unconditional and that believers must look to God's Word rather than circumstances. He uses Abraham's willingness to sacrifice Isaac as a type of Christ's sacrifice, and declares that God is Jehovah-jireh, the Lord who provides.
themes: the sacrifice of Isaac as a type of Christ

title: Redeemer, Redemption
summary: William Branham preaches on the theme of redemption, using Job 19:25-27 as a text. He illustrates redemption through the story of Ruth and Boaz, emphasizing that Christ is the Redeemer who frees sinners from bondage. Branham encourages believers to stay rooted in Christ and not be swayed by emotionalism or formalism.

title: What Is That In Your Hand?
summary: William Branham preaches on the story of Moses and the burning bush, emphasizing that God can use whatever we have in our hand, no matter how insignificant, when we surrender it to Him. He encourages believers to turn aside from criticism and approach God reverently, allowing Him to transform their failures into victories.

title: Why Are People So Tossed About?
summary: William Branham teaches on the difference between intellectual faith and experiential faith, using the Old Testament manna as a type. He explains that many Christians are tossed about because they only eat the manna that falls daily but have not entered into the inner court where the manna is preserved in the golden pot. True rest and stability come from being hid with Christ in the heart, where the Holy Spirit lives through the believer.

title: God Hath A Provided Way
summary: William Branham preaches on God's provision for healing and salvation, using the example of Abraham and Isaac to illustrate that God prepares a way before making a promise. He encourages believers to accept God's promises with bold faith, as healing and redemption are already provided through Christ's sacrifice.

title: The Junction of Time
summary: William Branham preaches on the concept of 'junctions' in biblical history—moments when God performs miraculous signs and wonders before transitioning to a new dispensation. He argues that the current age is at such a junction, evidenced by the increase of evil and the outpouring of the Holy Spirit, and calls believers to recognize the signs and prepare for Christ's return.

title: Fellowship With God Through Reconciliation
summary: William Branham speaks on the theme of fellowship with God, emphasizing that true fellowship is restored only through the shed blood of Jesus Christ, not through church membership, education, or human efforts. He contrasts the separation caused by sin with the reconciliation available through Christ's atonement, and calls for a genuine, Holy Ghost revival.

title: The Inter-Veil
summary: William Branham preaches on the hidden life in Christ, emphasizing rest and grace over struggle. He uses the Old Testament tabernacle and the veil as a type of Christ's flesh, urging believers to enter the holiest by faith. He contrasts intellectual faith with heart faith, warning against unbelief and moral compromise.

title: The Junction Time
summary: William Branham speaks about the importance of interdenominational fellowship and the signs of the times, emphasizing that God works in unexpected ways at each junction of history. He shares testimonies from his healing campaigns in Germany and Switzerland, and calls believers to follow the Holy Spirit as instinctively as ducks follow their leader.

title: Inspiration
summary: William Branham speaks on the importance of casting down reasoning and following the soul's witness to God's Word, using the story of Elijah and Elisha as a type of Christ and the Church. He emphasizes the need for total commitment to God, preparing a place for the Lord's coming, and the danger of grieving the soul through disobedience.

title: The Supernatural
summary: William Branham speaks on the supernatural nature of God and the importance of living in the atmosphere of God's presence. Using the story of Elisha and Naaman, he emphasizes that God is the same yesterday, today, and forever, and that believers must abide in Christ to experience His power.

title: Fellowship
summary: William Branham speaks on the theme of fellowship, emphasizing that true fellowship with God and among believers is only possible through the shed blood of Jesus Christ. He contrasts this with denominational barriers and human efforts, urging unity and a return to the simple Gospel. Branham also shares personal anecdotes and insights from Scripture, particularly the Book of Job and the Old Testament sacrificial system, to illustrate the necessity of the Blood for reconciliation.

title: Hidden Life With Christ
summary: William Branham teaches on the need for a hidden, consecrated life with Christ, using the Old Testament tabernacle as a type. He contrasts the manna in the outer court, which perishes, with the manna in the holiest of holies, which remains fresh, illustrating the difference between a superficial faith and a deep, abiding relationship with God.

title: When Love Is Projected
summary: William Branham speaks on the power of divine love and sovereign grace, sharing testimonies of healing and deliverance. He emphasizes that when human efforts fail and love is projected, God's grace steps in to perform miracles.

title: The Worst Sinner in the City
summary: William Branham preaches on the Pharisee's banquet where Jesus was invited but neglected, drawing parallels to modern churches that invite Christ but fail to honor Him. He contrasts the Pharisee's hypocrisy with the repentant harlot who anoints Jesus' feet, emphasizing that the worst sinner is the one who rejects Christ's love and forgiveness.
themes: God's grace for the worst sinners

title: Being Led of the Holy Spirit
summary: William Branham shares a vision about his future ministry, emphasizing the need to keep supernatural matters private to avoid carnal impersonations. He then preaches on being led by the Holy Spirit, using the examples of Simeon, Mary, and Joseph to illustrate faith and obedience to God's Word.
themes: Being led by the Holy Spirit
The power of the shed blood
The role of women in the Spirit

title: God's Covenant With Abraham And His Seed
summary: William Branham teaches on God's unconditional covenant with Abraham, emphasizing that God's promises are based on His own will and faithfulness, not human effort. He contrasts faith with knowledge, explains election and foreknowledge, and encourages believers to trust God's Word absolutely for salvation and healing.

title: Jehovah-Jireh
summary: William Branham preaches on the compound redemptive name Jehovah-Jireh, emphasizing that God is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He uses the account of Abraham and Isaac to illustrate faith and God's provision, and draws parallels between Old Testament types and New Testament truths, urging believers to live a fully surrendered life in the Shekinah Glory.

title: Jesus Christ the Same Yesterday, Today, and Forever
summary: William Branham preaches on Hebrews 13:8, emphasizing that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He argues that the same signs and wonders that accompanied Jesus' earthly ministry should be present in the church today, as the Holy Spirit continues His work. Branham calls believers to contend for the faith once delivered to the saints, warning against unbelief and denominational division.

title: Making A Way
summary: William Branham speaks on God's provision of a way of escape in every trial, using biblical examples from Noah, Daniel, Jonah, and the scapegoat. He emphasizes that faith must be anchored in God's eternal Word and the finished work of Christ at Calvary.

title: The True and False Vines
summary: William Branham preaches on the true and false vines, using the Old Testament types of Cain and Abel, Jacob and Esau, and Israel and Moab to illustrate the difference between true and false worship. He emphasizes that mere religious profession is not enough; one must be born again and have the Spirit of God.

title: God Using His Gift
summary: William Branham speaks on how God uses His gift through believers' faith, using the story of Blind Bartimaeus to illustrate that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He emphasizes that miracles are not past but present, and that faith can touch God today just as it did in biblical times.
themes: the gift of the Holy Spirit

title: The Mighty Conqueror
summary: In this Easter sermon, William Branham emphasizes the resurrection of Jesus Christ as the central proof of His divinity and the foundation of Christian faith. He recounts personal testimonies of healings and miracles to demonstrate that Christ is alive and active today, just as He was in the Gospels. Branham urges believers to trust solely in Christ, not in denominations or human wisdom, and to recognize His presence in their daily lives.

title: Easter Sunrise
subtitle: 56-0401S
summary: William Branham preaches on the resurrection of Jesus Christ, emphasizing that because He lives, believers shall live also. He reflects on the sorrow of Mary and Martha at the tomb, the rejection and death of Christ, and the triumph of His resurrection. Branham encourages the congregation to have the blessed hope of resurrection and eternal life, and announces that Jesus is alive and present among them.

title: Shepherd of the Sheepfold
summary: William Branham shares his recent experiences in Mexico, including a miraculous healing of a dead baby and a large altar call. He reflects on the relationship between the shepherd and the sheep, emphasizing God's care and the helplessness of humanity without Christ.

title: The Infallibility of God's Spoken Word
summary: William Branham teaches on the absolute perfection and unchangeable nature of God's spoken Word. He explains that once God speaks a promise, He is bound to fulfill it because He is infallible and cannot contradict Himself. Using examples from the Old Testament, Branham illustrates how God always makes a way to keep His Word, whether through the ark for Noah, the fiery furnace for Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, or the ladder to heaven for Jacob.

title: The Resurrection of Jesus
summary: William Branham preaches on the resurrection of Jesus, emphasizing that Christ is alive today through the Holy Spirit and continues His ministry among believers. He uses the account of the disciples on the road to Emmaus to illustrate how Jesus reveals Himself through Scripture and familiar actions, and he encourages the congregation to recognize Christ's presence and power in their midst.
themes: Presence of Christ through the Holy Spirit

title: The Infallible Word of God
summary: William Branham preaches on the absolute reliability and divine authority of the Bible as God's infallible Word. He uses the analogy of a bridge builder who tests every material to illustrate how God has time-tested His Word and provided Jesus Christ as the only bridge between humanity and God. Branham calls listeners to build their faith solely on Scripture, warning against false signs and doctrines that deviate from the finished work of Christ.
themes: Testing of spirits by the Word

title: Blind Bartimaeus
summary: William Branham preaches on the story of blind Bartimaeus, emphasizing faith in Jesus Christ as the same yesterday, today, and forever. He encourages believers to trust God's Word and power for healing and salvation, despite criticism and unbelief.

title: What Is A Vision?
summary: William Branham explains the nature of visions, describing them as material and real experiences given by God. He shares personal accounts of visions and discusses the operation of the Holy Spirit in healing ministry, emphasizing that the gift is for God's glory and not for public show.

title: The Time Is At Hand
summary: William Branham preaches on the urgency of the present time as the fulfillment of biblical prophecy, emphasizing that the end times are near and calling for decision for Christ. He highlights the universal revival and signs of the times, urging healing and salvation.

title: Blind Bartimaeus
summary: William Branham preaches on the story of blind Bartimaeus, emphasizing that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever, and that faith in Him can bring healing and salvation. He encourages the congregation to trust in God's provision and to keep their promises to Him.

title: The Deep Calling to the Deep
summary: William Branham speaks on the theme of 'the deep calling to the deep,' using examples from nature and Scripture to illustrate how God's Spirit calls to the human spirit. He emphasizes that God always has a witness on earth and that believers should trust in God's promises, as exemplified by Simeon who was promised to see the Christ before his death.

title: Earnestly Contending For The Faith That Was Once Delivered Unto The Saints
summary: William Branham explains the nature of divine healing, emphasizing that healing comes from God through faith, not from any human healer. He urges believers to contend for the faith once delivered to the saints, which includes the same works and signs that Jesus performed, such as healing the sick and discerning thoughts. Branham contrasts true faith with denominational traditions and calls for a return to the apostolic faith.
themes: the same yesterday, today, and forever

title: When Their Eyes Were Opened
summary: William Branham speaks on the resurrection of Jesus Christ and the need for believers to recognize His living presence today. He emphasizes that the same works Jesus performed on earth, such as healing and discerning thoughts, are still available through the Holy Spirit. Branham encourages the audience to shut out distractions and invite Christ into their hearts to experience His power.
themes: Divine healing as earnest of resurrection
Rejection of Christ's works as blasphemy

title: What Visions Are
summary: William Branham explains the nature of visions as divine revelations from God, using biblical examples and personal experiences to illustrate how visions operate and how faith interacts with healing. He emphasizes the importance of believing God's Word and the role of visions in his ministry.
themes: the role of the Holy Spirit

title: Show Us The Father And It'll Satisfy
summary: William Branham speaks on seeing God through His universe, His Word, His Son, and His people. He emphasizes that God reveals Himself in nature and that faith is required to perceive Him. The sermon includes personal anecdotes and a call to recognize God's presence in all things.
themes: the Father revealed in the Son

title: Jesus Christ the Same Yesterday, Today, and Forever
summary: William Branham preaches on the unchanging nature of Jesus Christ, emphasizing that Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He urges believers to seek a simple, faith-based relationship with Jesus rather than relying on education or denominational doctrines, and highlights that the same works Christ did should be evident in His church today.
themes: Holy Spirit's work in the church

title: Faith
summary: William Branham speaks on the importance of faith, using the story of Abraham and Isaac to illustrate unwavering trust in God's promises. He emphasizes that God's redemptive names, such as Jehovah-jireh, are unchanging and that believers should rest in God's Word rather than be swayed by circumstances or feelings.

title: God's Covenant With Abraham
summary: William Branham speaks on the covenant God made with Abraham, emphasizing the importance of unwavering faith in God's promises regardless of circumstances. He encourages believers to look to God's Word rather than symptoms, and illustrates this with stories of healing and faith.

title: Jehovah-Jireh
summary: William Branham preaches on God as Jehovah-Jireh, the Lord who provides, using the story of Abraham and Isaac on Mount Moriah. He emphasizes that God provides a sacrifice for sin and healing, and that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever, working through the Holy Spirit in the Church.

title: Teaching on Moses
summary: William Branham speaks on Mother's Day, addressing mothers and children. He uses the story of Moses' parents, Amram and Jochebed, to illustrate faith and prayer under oppression, emphasizing the value of the soul and the importance of losing one's life for Christ.

title: At Kadesh-Barnea
summary: William Branham preaches on the Old Testament account of Israel at Kadesh-Barnea, using it as a type for the modern church. He warns against the 'mixed multitude' of nominal believers and calls for a genuine, born-again faith that stands firm under trial.
themes: The mixed multitude in the church
The need for a born-again experience
Judgment beginning at the house of God

title: The Lamb's Book of Life
summary: William Branham teaches on the value of souls over material wealth, using personal anecdotes and biblical references. He explores the concept of perfection through Christ, the shadow of the law, and the sealing of the Holy Spirit, urging believers to separate from the world and win souls.

title: Perfection
summary: William Branham discusses the concept of perfection through the lens of Hebrews 10, explaining how the law was a shadow of good things to come and how Christ's sacrifice provides true purification. He emphasizes that only through the blood of Christ can a worshipper be purged of sin and have no more conscience of sin.

title: Hear Ye Him
summary: William Branham preaches on the transfiguration of Jesus, emphasizing that the church must hear and follow Christ alone, not the law or prophets. He calls for a return to God's love and holiness, criticizing modern church worldliness and denominational division.

title: Life Is The Healer
summary: William Branham teaches that life itself is the healer, not medicine, and that healing was already purchased at Calvary. He contrasts faith in God with reliance on medical science, explaining that sickness is a devil that must be cast out, and that true healing comes from the life of God within.

title: Jehovah-Jireh
summary: William Branham preaches on the faith of Abraham and the covenant name Jehovah-Jireh, emphasizing God's sovereign grace and the believer's inheritance of all redemptive promises through Christ. He calls for separation from the world and trust in God's Word despite circumstances.

title: God Provided a Lamb
summary: William Branham preaches on Abraham's faith and God's covenant, emphasizing that believers are Abraham's seed and heirs of the promise. He discusses divine healing as part of the atonement, the importance of love over gifts, and the need for a faith that goes beyond intellectual assent to a deep soul experience.

title: An Exodus
summary: William Branham preaches on the Exodus of the Israelites from Egypt as a type of the church's calling out from the world. He emphasizes the need for a genuine experience with God, the power of faith over circumstances, and the importance of being filled with the Holy Spirit.

title: Revelation, Book of Symbols
summary: William Branham speaks on the Book of Revelation as a book of symbols, emphasizing that God hides truth from the wise and reveals it to babes. He discusses election, the love of God, and the importance of the new birth over theological knowledge. He also shares testimonies of healing and the need for the Church to receive the revelation of Jesus Christ in the last days.

title: The Law Having a Shadow
summary: William Branham teaches from Hebrews 10 about the law being a shadow of good things to come, emphasizing that the Old Testament law foreshadowed Christ. He explains that the law could not make worshippers perfect, but Christ's sacrifice perfects believers forever through the Holy Spirit. Branham also shares testimonies of healings and discusses the importance of faith in God's Word.

title: The Mark Of The Beast
summary: William Branham preaches on the mark of the beast, emphasizing that it begins with rejecting the Gospel and sealing one's ears to the truth. He uses Old Testament types like the jubilee year and the boring of the slave's ear to illustrate how refusal to accept Christ's liberation leads to spiritual bondage. Branham warns against worldliness, particularly in dress and behavior, as evidence of the antichrist spirit.

title: All Things Are Possible To Him That Believeth
summary: William Branham preaches on Mark 9:23, emphasizing that all things are possible to those who believe. He discusses the relationship between faith and healing, arguing that divine healing is included in the atonement. He uses the story of the epileptic boy to illustrate how doubt and unbelief hinder God's power, and encourages believers to have simple faith in God's Word.

title: Led by the Spirit of God
summary: William Branham preaches on being led by the Spirit of God, emphasizing that true believers walk not after the flesh but after the Spirit. He discusses the proper use of spiritual gifts, the necessity of the Holy Spirit baptism, and the importance of separating from worldly influences.

title: Love
summary: William Branham speaks on the power of divine love, emphasizing that love is the greatest force and that when human love reaches its limit, sovereign grace takes over. He shares personal stories and biblical examples to illustrate that genuine love for God transforms a person and is the true evidence of the Holy Spirit.

title: Making the Valley Full of Ditches
summary: William Branham preaches on the need for genuine, Holy Ghost-filled Christianity, contrasting it with lukewarm, borderline belief. Using the story of Elisha and the kings of Israel, Judah, and Edom, he emphasizes the importance of being separated from the world and filled with the Spirit to receive God's provision.

title: Raising Jairus' Daughter
summary: William Branham preaches on the raising of Jairus' daughter, emphasizing Jesus' compassion and power over death. He encourages faith in Christ's resurrection and His ability to heal and save today.

title: The Arrow of God's Deliverance Shot from a Bow
summary: William Branham preaches on the need for the church to fully receive the Holy Spirit as the arrow of God's deliverance, warning against worldliness and lukewarm faith. He uses the story of King Joash and Elisha to illustrate how the church has struck short of God's blessings, and calls for a return to old-fashioned Holy Ghost revival.

title: The Church And Its Condition
summary: William Branham preaches on the condition of the church, using the symbolism of the lamb and the dove to illustrate the need for meekness, gentleness, and submission to the Holy Spirit. He contrasts the nature of a true Christian with that of a hypocrite, and calls for a return to sacrificial living and holiness.

title: Divine Love and Sovereign Grace
summary: William Branham preaches on the necessity of divine love as the foundation for all spiritual gifts, using the Exodus account of Israel at the Red Sea to illustrate how love projected toward God brings sovereign grace into action. He emphasizes that love casts out fear and that when human effort ends, God's grace takes over.

title: Faith
summary: William Branham preaches on the nature of faith, using Abraham as the prime example. He emphasizes that true faith holds to God's promise regardless of circumstances, and that believers must separate from unbelievers and ignore symptoms. He encourages the congregation to call those things which are not as though they were, because God said so.

title: The Working of the Holy Spirit
summary: William Branham speaks on the operation of the Holy Spirit in his ministry, using the analogy of a carnival knothole to explain how the gift of God works through him. He emphasizes that it is the faith of the people that draws from the gift, and shares a vision of healing in Denver to illustrate God's direct intervention. The sermon also covers the covenant with Abraham and the role of the Holy Spirit in the Church.
themes: The role of the Holy Spirit

title: Divine Love
summary: William Branham speaks on the nature of divine love and how it leads to sovereign grace. He shares personal testimonies of healing and protection, emphasizing that when human efforts fail, God's grace takes over through love.

title: The Handwriting On The Wall
summary: William Branham preaches on the biblical account of Belshazzar's feast and the handwriting on the wall, drawing parallels to the moral and spiritual decline of modern society. He urges believers to purpose in their hearts to serve God faithfully despite worldly pressures, and warns of impending judgment for those who reject God's Word.

title: Azusa Jubilee
summary: William Branham speaks at the Azusa Street Jubilee celebration at Angelus Temple, calling for a return to the old-fashioned Pentecostal experience and a rededication to the Holy Spirit. He uses the Old Testament year of jubilee as a type of spiritual freedom, urging believers to break free from captivity to worldliness and denominational barriers.

title: The Lamb and the Dove
summary: William Branham preaches on the symbolism of the Lamb and the Dove, representing Christ and the Holy Spirit. He emphasizes the need for believers to have a lamb-like nature of meekness and surrender to allow the Holy Spirit (the Dove) to abide in them. He calls for a return to the humility and holiness of the early Pentecostal Azusa Street revival.

title: Spiritual Adoption
summary: William Branham speaks on the concept of spiritual adoption, using the Transfiguration as a backdrop to discuss how believers are adopted as sons of God through Christ. He emphasizes the role of the Holy Spirit as a tutor, training believers to be obedient children, and the importance of revelation in building the Church.

title: Hear Ye Him
summary: William Branham preaches on the Mount of Transfiguration, emphasizing that the Church is built upon the revelation of Jesus Christ, not on denominations, laws, or works. He calls believers to hear Jesus alone, who is the only way to salvation, healing, and eternal life.

title: Witnesses
summary: William Branham preaches on the biblical call for believers to be witnesses of Jesus Christ, emphasizing that a true witness must have a personal encounter with God. He recounts examples from Scripture—Noah, Daniel, the Hebrew children, Moses, Joshua, John the Baptist, and the apostles—and modern testimonies of healing and transformation, urging the audience to take their stand for Christ.

title: The Ministry Explained
summary: William Branham explains the biblical basis for spiritual gifts and divine healing, emphasizing that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He contrasts the faith of the queen of Sheba and the Ninevites with the unbelief of the religious leaders of his day, urging listeners to come and see for themselves.
themes: Jesus Christ the same yesterday, today, and forever
The Messianic sign of the prophet
The role of spiritual gifts in the Church
The queen of Sheba as a example of seeking God

title: Father, The Hour Has Come
summary: William Branham preaches on the need for the church to return to the old landmarks of the Bible, using the story of Jehoshaphat and Ahab as a warning against compromise and worldliness. He calls for unity, holiness, and a stand on God's Word, emphasizing that true faith is based on revelation and the Blood of Christ, not on human wisdom or denominational pride.

title: Elisha The Prophet
summary: William Branham preaches on the Old Testament prophet Elisha, focusing on the Shunammite woman who built a room for Elisha and was rewarded with a son. He draws parallels between Elisha's double portion of Elijah's spirit and the Church's reception of the Holy Spirit, emphasizing the importance of respecting God's servants and the power of faith.

title: Painted-Face Jezebel
summary: William Branham preaches on the story of Jezebel from 2 Kings 9, using her as an example of sin and worldliness that has infiltrated the modern church. He condemns practices such as face painting, hair cutting, and worldly music, calling for a return to holiness and the Holy Spirit.

title: A Wedding Supper
summary: William Branham preaches on the parable of the wedding supper from Matthew 22, emphasizing that God has prepared everything for salvation and healing, and that the Holy Ghost is the robe provided for all who accept the invitation. He calls for repentance and a return to the power of Pentecost.
themes: the robe of the Holy Ghost

title: A Blushing Prophet
summary: William Branham preaches on the need for repentance and revival, using the biblical example of Ezra who blushed before God for the sins of Israel. He condemns the moral decay and worldliness in the church, calling for a return to holiness and a Holy Ghost revival.

title: A Secondhanded Robe
summary: William Branham preaches on the story of Elijah and Elisha, emphasizing the need for a fresh, firsthand anointing from God rather than relying on secondhand religious experiences or robes. He encourages believers to keep their eyes on God's promises and to seek the power of the God of Elijah for their lives and ministries.

title: A Secondhanded Robe
summary: William Branham preaches on the story of Elisha receiving Elijah's mantle, emphasizing the need for a personal relationship with God rather than relying on denominational robes or secondhand faith. He calls for a purging of worldly influences and a sincere pursuit of the Holy Spirit's power.

title: Gifts
summary: William Branham speaks on spiritual gifts, emphasizing that they are rays from the same Spirit of God. He uses the type of Joseph and Moses to illustrate Christ, and explains that Jesus did nothing until the Father showed Him, as seen in the raising of Lazarus. He encourages faith in God's promises regardless of circumstances.
themes: Christ as fulfillment of Old Testament types

title: Abraham
summary: William Branham preaches on the faith of Abraham, emphasizing God's unconditional covenant and the importance of separation from the world. He encourages believers to claim God's promises, including healing, by faith, and demonstrates the power of God's Word through the example of Abraham's unwavering belief.

title: God Making His Promise
summary: William Branham preaches on God's faithfulness to His promises, using the biblical imagery of the Lamb and the Dove to illustrate the nature of Christ and the Holy Spirit. He challenges believers to examine their lives, repent of worldliness, and return to a genuine, holy walk with God.

The Holy Spirit as a Dove
Holiness and separation from the world
The unity of the Dove and the Lamb

title: Jehovah-Jireh
summary: William Branham preaches on God's covenant with Abraham, focusing on the name Jehovah-Jireh and the finished work of Christ. He emphasizes faith in God's promises, divine healing in the atonement, and the sealing of the Holy Spirit.

title: Hear Ye Him
summary: William Branham preaches on the transfiguration of Christ, emphasizing that Jesus is the final authority and that believers should 'hear ye Him.' He discusses the finished work of Christ, the relationship between sin and unbelief, and the importance of faith in receiving healing and salvation.

title: Joseph Meeting His Brethren
summary: William Branham teaches on the biblical account of Joseph meeting his brethren, drawing parallels to the life of Jesus Christ and the ongoing conflict between the righteous and evil seeds. He emphasizes the importance of divine revelation and the supernatural vindication of God's chosen people.

title: Sirs, We Would See Jesus
summary: William Branham opens a series of meetings in Cleveland, Tennessee, emphasizing the importance of seeing Jesus through the Word and the Holy Spirit. He discusses the nature of sin as unbelief, the finished work of Calvary for healing, and the necessity of the supernatural confirmation of the Gospel. He challenges believers to live up to the promises of Christ, who is the same yesterday, today, and forever.

the supernatural confirmation of the Gospel

title: Hear Ye Him
summary: William Branham preaches on the transfiguration of Jesus, emphasizing that believers should hear and follow Christ alone, not the law or prophets.
