Branham also discusses the role of the Holy Spirit as a tutor and the need for Christians to be salty examples.

title: Jehovah-Jireh
summary: William Branham speaks on God's covenant with Abraham, emphasizing that believers are Abraham's seed and heirs to all promises. He encourages faith in God's Word despite symptoms, using the example of Abraham's unwavering belief. The sermon concludes with a call to separate from unbelief and trust in Jehovah-jireh, the Lord who provides.

title: What Does It Take To Make A Christian Life?
summary: William Branham discusses the necessity of the Holy Spirit in the church, contrasting the flexibility of new believers with the rigidity of old denominations. He uses the metaphor of new wine in new bottles to illustrate that God's Spirit cannot be contained by intellectualism or tradition. Branham emphasizes that true Christian life comes from the Holy Spirit controlling the believer, not from outward emotions or denominational affiliation.

title: The Infallible Proof of the Resurrection
summary: William Branham preaches on the resurrection of Jesus Christ as the foundational proof of Christianity. He contrasts the living Christ with dead religious founders, emphasizing that the resurrection is demonstrated through the Holy Spirit's work in believers today. He challenges the church to prove the resurrection by manifesting the same works Jesus did.

title: God Keeps His Word
summary: William Branham preaches on the infallibility of God's Word, using the example of Isaiah's prophecy that the people could not believe in Jesus because the prophet had spoken it. He contrasts true faith in God's Word with empty religious formalism and warns against associating with those who deny the Bible's authority.

title: God Keeps His Word
summary: William Branham preaches on the infallibility of God's Word, warning against false teachings and the spirit of the age. He uses the story of Ahab and Jehoshaphat to illustrate the danger of mixing truth with error, and calls believers to stand on the Word alone.

title: The Impersonation of Christianity
summary: William Branham preaches on the need for a genuine heart transformation by the Holy Spirit, contrasting it with intellectualism and emotional fanaticism. He emphasizes that true Christianity is not about outward acts or intellectual knowledge but about receiving a new heart and God's Spirit, which produces authentic fruit and order.

title: Hear Ye Him
summary: William Branham preaches on the transfiguration of Jesus, emphasizing that believers should hear Christ alone rather than the law or prophets. He contrasts the love of God with human religiosity and calls the church to rise above division and unbelief through faith in the Holy Spirit.

title: India Trip Report
summary: William Branham shares a report on his trip to India, emphasizing the need for the church to demonstrate the supernatural power of the Gospel as evidence of Christ's resurrection. He recounts a conversation with a Muslim who challenged Christians to produce the signs promised in Mark 16, and reflects on the poverty he witnessed in India, calling for unity and action among believers.

title: When Divine Love Is Projected, Sovereign Grace Takes Its Place
summary: William Branham preaches on the theme of divine love and sovereign grace, using John 3:16 as his text. He shares personal stories and testimonies to illustrate how projecting love in faith allows God's grace to intervene in impossible situations, including healings and deliverances.

title: The Impersonation of Christianity
summary: William Branham preaches on the need for genuine Christianity, emphasizing that it is an experience of the Holy Spirit, not a denomination or intellectual creed. He uses Ezekiel 36:27 to discuss God's promise to put His Spirit in believers, and warns against impersonating Christianity through empty religious forms.

title: Blind Bartimaeus
summary: William Branham preaches on the story of blind Bartimaeus, emphasizing faith that persists despite opposition. He draws parallels between Bartimaeus's faith in Jesus as the Son of David and the need for modern believers to trust in Christ for salvation and healing. The sermon includes an altar call for those who want Jesus to stand for them on judgment day.

title: SIRS, WE WOULD SEE JESUS
summary: William Branham speaks on the desire to see Jesus, emphasizing that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He discusses the importance of faith, the baptism of the Holy Spirit, and the power of God to heal, challenging the audience to experience the living Christ through His Word and Spirit.

title: A Greater Than Solomon Is Here
summary: William Branham preaches on the queen of Sheba's journey to witness Solomon's God-given gift, contrasting her faith with the unbelief of Jesus' generation. He emphasizes that divine healing comes through faith in God's Word and that the same Holy Spirit works today through gifts of discernment and healing, calling believers to press in and believe.

title: Blind Bartimaeus
summary: William Branham preaches on the story of blind Bartimaeus, emphasizing faith that stops Jesus despite distractions. He calls for reverence and faith, then prays for the sick, demonstrating the gift of discernment as a sign of Christ's presence.

title: And Then Jesus Came
summary: William Branham preaches on the power of Jesus' presence in the darkest moments, using the raising of Lazarus as a central text. He contrasts human weakness with divine power, emphasizing that Jesus is more than a prophet—He is God manifested in the flesh. Branham calls believers to stand firm on God's promises, as Jesus always arrives in the darkest hour.

title: Why Is It That So Many Christians Find It So Hard to Live the Christian Life?
summary: William Branham preaches on the need for a new heart and spirit, emphasizing that the Christian life is not about intellectualism or outward signs but about the indwelling Holy Spirit as the mainspring of the believer's life. He uses the analogy of an eagle and a watch to illustrate the freedom and power of a Spirit-filled life.

title: What Think Ye Of Christ?
summary: William Branham preaches on the question Jesus asked the Pharisees: 'What think ye of Christ?' He emphasizes that one's answer determines eternal destiny, healing, and salvation. Branham calls witnesses from Scripture and history to testify that Jesus is the virgin-born Son of God, and urges listeners to accept Him personally.

title: Divine Love
summary: William Branham preaches on the power of divine love, illustrating how God's love, when projected through believers, produces sovereign grace and miracles. He shares personal stories of love overcoming fear, including encounters with a violent man, hornets, a killer bull, and a dying opossum, to demonstrate that love casts out fear and brings healing.

title: God Keeps His Word 1
summary: William Branham preaches on God's faithfulness to His Word, using the story of Caleb and Joshua to contrast faith in God's promises with fear of circumstances. He warns against false signs and sensations, urging believers to stay grounded in Scripture.

title: God Keeps His Word 2
summary: William Branham preaches on the infallibility of God's Word, using the story of Micaiah and the false prophets to contrast true prophecy based on Scripture with deceptive signs and sensations. He warns against basing salvation on experiences, fasting, or prayer, emphasizing that only faith through the Word saves. Branham calls the church to return to the Bible and avoid being led astray by emotionalism and false doctrines.

title: The Good Shepherd Of The Sheep
summary: William Branham preaches on Jesus as the Good Shepherd, using the metaphor of sheep to illustrate the relationship between believers and Christ. He emphasizes the shepherd's care, the sheep's dependence on the shepherd's voice, and the security of those who follow Him.

title: I Will Restore
summary: William Branham speaks at a Christian Businessmen's breakfast in Phoenix, using Joel 1:4 and 2:25 to discuss four destroyers (palmerworm, locust, cankerworm, caterpillar) that have eaten away at the church's heritage. He calls for a restoration of brotherly love, unity, and true worship, urging believers to overcome denominational divisions.

title: Jehovah-Jireh
summary: William Branham preaches on the redemptive name Jehovah-Jireh, using Abraham's willingness to sacrifice Isaac as a type of God providing the sacrifice. He emphasizes taking God at His Word unconditionally, as Abraham did, and applies this to divine healing and faith for the impossible.
themes: Christ as the fulfillment of Old Testament types

title: Washing Jesus' Feet
summary: William Branham preaches on the story of the Pharisee who invited Jesus to dinner but neglected to wash His feet, anoint His head, or give Him a kiss. He contrasts the cold, formal religion of the Pharisees with the heartfelt devotion of the sinful woman who washed Jesus' feet with her tears and anointed them with ointment. Branham calls for genuine love and worship of Jesus, warning against hypocrisy and worldliness.

title: Hear Ye Him
summary: William Branham preaches on the transfiguration of Jesus, emphasizing the need to hear Christ above the law and justice represented by Moses and Elijah. He calls for unity and love among believers, urging them to stand for Jesus so that He will stand for them in heaven.

title: Hear Ye Him
summary: William Branham calls for unity among denominations, urging believers to focus on Christ rather than doctrinal differences. He contrasts the law, justice, and love, emphasizing that salvation comes only through hearing and obeying Jesus, the beloved Son of God.

title: Hear Ye Him
summary: William Branham preaches on the Transfiguration, emphasizing that God's voice declared 'Hear ye Him'—pointing to Christ as the ultimate revelation of God's love, surpassing the law (Moses) and justice (Elijah). He calls the church to return to genuine love, holiness, and obedience to the Holy Spirit's tutoring through the Word, warning against worldliness and denominational barriers.

title: God In His Word
summary: William Branham preaches on four ways to see God: in His universe, in His Word, in His Son, and in His people. He uses nature, Scripture, and personal testimony to demonstrate God's presence and faithfulness, encouraging believers to have faith in God's promises and to recognize God dwelling within them.

title: Why Some People Can't Keep The Victory
summary: William Branham preaches on the need for a genuine Holy Spirit revival, using the analogy of the eagle to describe prophets and the new wine in new bottles to illustrate the necessity of flexible hearts to receive God's Spirit. He emphasizes that victory is kept not by intellectualism or denominationalism but by a new heart and spirit from God.
themes: The church as a living organism

title: The Lamb and the Dove
summary: William Branham preaches on the nature of the Lamb and the Dove as representations of Christ and the Holy Spirit. He emphasizes that true Christianity is not about outward demonstrations but about bearing the fruit of the Spirit through a changed nature. He calls for a return to holiness and surrender to the leading of the Holy Spirit.

title: Jehovah-jireh
summary: William Branham speaks on the redemptive name Jehovah-jireh, emphasizing God's unconditional covenant with Abraham and the importance of faith in God's promises. He encourages believers to separate from the world and trust in God's provision, using Abraham's example of unwavering faith.
themes: The Holy Spirit as the covenant seal

title: Then Jesus Came
summary: William Branham preaches on the theme that Jesus arrives in the darkest hour, using the story of Lazarus and other biblical examples to illustrate how Christ's presence brings hope and healing when all seems lost. He emphasizes that despite the world's troubles, Jesus is still the same yesterday, today, and forever, and He comes to those who trust in Him.

title: God Keeps His Word
summary: William Branham preaches on God's faithfulness to His Word, using the examples of Israel's deliverance from Egypt and the testing at Kadesh-barnea. He warns that the Church must stay true to the Word and be ready for Christ's return, as judgment is coming upon nations that reject God.

title: Corinthians, Book of Correction
summary: William Branham warns against basing salvation on sensations, gifts, or religious rituals, using 1 Corinthians 10 as a text. He emphasizes that true salvation comes only through a genuine new birth and love for God, not through outward experiences. He also condemns false prophets and worldly influences in the church.

title: The Second Coming of the Lord
summary: William Branham preaches on the imminent Second Coming of Christ, urging the church to examine its spiritual condition and return to genuine devotion. He interprets current events as signs of the end times and calls for repentance and holiness.

title: The Communion
summary: William Branham preaches on the meaning of Communion as a commemoration of Christ's finished work, not a means of salvation. He draws parallels between the Old Testament Passover and the Lord's Supper, emphasizing the importance of testing and faithfulness. The sermon includes a personal testimony of his own Gethsemane experience and an altar call.

title: The Perfection
summary: William Branham preaches on the theme of perfection, explaining that the law could not make worshippers perfect, but Christ's one sacrifice perfects forever those who are sanctified. He emphasizes that salvation is not by works but by grace through faith in Christ's atoning blood.

title: The Entombment
summary: William Branham preaches on the infallibility of God's Word, using the examples of Job, Abraham, and other Old Testament saints who trusted God's promises. He describes Jesus' descent into hell and paradise during His entombment, His victory over Satan, and the assurance of resurrection for those in Christ.

title: And Their Eyes Were Opened And They Knew Him
summary: William Branham preaches on the resurrection of Jesus Christ, emphasizing that Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He demonstrates the living presence of Christ through the gift of discernment and healing, calling the congregation to recognize and believe in the risen Lord.

title: The Great And Mighty Conqueror

He emphasizes that Christ's victory is complete and believers can rejoice in the finished work of salvation.

title: We Would See Jesus
summary: William Branham preaches on the unchanging nature of Jesus Christ, emphasizing that He is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He calls for spiritual healing and unity among believers, and prepares the congregation for a healing service where the Holy Spirit will manifest the works of Jesus.

title: The Queen of Sheba
summary: William Branham preaches on Matthew 12:42, comparing the Queen of Sheba's journey to hear Solomon's wisdom with the generation that rejected Jesus. Branham contrasts the queen's faith and sacrifice with the unbelief of his own generation, warning of judgment.

title: Stand Still

title: Hear Ye Him
summary: William Branham preaches on the transfiguration of Jesus, emphasizing that God's voice from the cloud commanded 'Hear ye Him,' signifying that the law and prophets are fulfilled in Christ. title: Love

title: Life

title: Faith Once Delivered to the Saints
summary: William Branham preaches on Jude 3, urging believers to earnestly contend for the faith once delivered to the saints. He emphasizes that true faith comes from God's Word, not creeds or denominations, and shares testimonies of divine healing as evidence of this faith operating today.

title: God Keeps His Word

title: The Queen of the South

title: Believe from the Heart
summary: William Branham preaches on the necessity of believing from the heart rather than the intellect, using the example of a bridge builder who tested every material before building. title: Stand Still And See The Salvation Of The Lord
summary: William Branham preaches on the need to stand still and see God's salvation, using the story of Jehoshaphat and the invading Moabites. title: Thirsting for Life
summary: William Branham preaches on the soul's thirst for God, contrasting worldly pleasures with true spiritual life. Using Psalm 63 and the metaphor of a deer fleeing wild dogs, he calls for a deep, desperate longing for God alone.

title: The Eagle In Her Nest
summary: William Branham uses the metaphor of an eagle stirring her nest to describe how God challenges and lifts His Church. He contrasts the eagle's heavenly nature with earthbound chickens, urging believers to set their faith on God's promises and soar above worldly cares. The sermon includes testimonies of healings and deliverances, and calls for a fresh move of the Holy Spirit.

summary: William Branham uses the eagle as a metaphor for the Church, describing how God feeds His people through His Word, lifts them to heavenly places, and stirs the nest to prepare them for spiritual flight. title: Hear Ye Him
summary: William Branham preaches on the transfiguration of Christ, emphasizing that God the Father declared 'This is my beloved Son; hear ye him.' He contrasts the law (Moses) and justice (Elijah) with the mercy and love of Christ, and calls the church to obedience and separation from worldliness.

title: Thirsting for Life

title: The Great Commission
summary: William Branham speaks on the Great Commission from Mark 16, emphasizing that signs and wonders should follow believers. He shares testimonies of his worldwide ministry, including a massive crusade in South Africa, and calls the church to return to the power of the Holy Spirit.

title: Sirs, We Would See Jesus
summary: William Branham preaches on the unchanging nature of Jesus Christ, emphasizing that He is the same yesterday, today, and forever. title: God Manifesting His Gifts
summary: William Branham preaches on God's pattern of sending gifts and witnesses throughout history, using the Queen of Sheba's journey to see Solomon's wisdom as a type of seeking God's gifts. He contrasts human love (phileo) with divine love (agapao), sharing personal testimonies of how love overcame fear and produced miracles, including healing the sick and taming wild animals. He emphasizes that love is the greatest force and that God's love, when received as a pardon, brings salvation and healing.

title: Hear Ye Him
summary: William Branham preaches on the Transfiguration, emphasizing that God commands us to hear His Son Jesus rather than the law or prophets. He calls for genuine Christian love and obedience over denominationalism and worldly distractions.

title: The Mighty Conqueror
summary: William Branham preaches on Jesus Christ as the ultimate conqueror who overcame sin, death, hell, and the grave. He contrasts worldly conquerors like Napoleon with Christ's victory at Calvary and resurrection, urging believers to have faith and be gallant in their Christian walk.

title: Blind Bartimaeus
summary: William Branham preaches on the story of blind Bartimaeus, emphasizing faith in Jesus as the Lamb of God who heals and saves. He encourages the congregation to accept Christ and trust in His power for physical and spiritual healing.

title: Jehovah-Jireh
summary: William Branham preaches on the compound redemptive name Jehovah-Jireh, emphasizing that God provides a sacrifice and that all redemptive names of God are inseparable. title: The Greatest Gift In The Bible
summary: William Branham preaches on the greatest gift in the Bible: Eternal Life, which is found only through knowing Jesus Christ. He contrasts true life with perverted life, using nature illustrations and personal stories to emphasize the soul's thirst for God.

title: Expectations And Leadings Of The Spirit
summary: William Branham speaks on the expectations and leadings of the Holy Spirit, using the example of Simeon and Anna who were led by the Spirit to recognize the infant Jesus in the temple. He emphasizes that God reveals Himself to those who are expecting and longing for Him, and that the same Holy Spirit leads believers today.

title: Time-Tested Memorials of God
summary: William Branham speaks on the theme of memorials, contrasting earthly monuments that decay with God's eternal Word. He uses biblical examples like Joshua's stones, Lot's wife, and the testing of a bridge builder to illustrate that true memorials are built on faith and God's unchanging promises.

title: Hebrews, Chapter One
summary: William Branham begins a verse-by-verse study of the Book of Hebrews, emphasizing the supremacy of Christ over prophets and angels. He discusses the importance of grounding experience in Scripture, using the Urim and Thummim as a type of God's Word. Branham also contrasts the law and grace, and explains the Trinity as one God in three offices.

title: Hebrews, Chapter Two
summary: Paul continues his exposition of Hebrews chapter 2, emphasizing the importance of not neglecting the great salvation brought by Christ. He contrasts the ministry of angels (prophets) with the superior ministry of Jesus, who was made lower than angels to taste death for every man. Branham exhorts believers to give earnest heed to the Word, to place God first, and to recognize the signs of the times through the Holy Spirit's work.

title: Hebrews, Chapter Two #1
subtitle: 57-0825M
summary: William Branham preaches on Hebrews chapter 2, emphasizing the importance of giving earnest heed to the Word of God and not letting it slip. He contrasts the steadfastness of the word spoken by angels (prophets) with the greater salvation spoken by the Lord Jesus, confirmed by signs and wonders. Branham warns against neglecting this great salvation and calls for unity among believers.
themes: Confirmation of the Word by signs

title: Hebrews, Chapter Two #3
summary: William Branham continues his teaching on Hebrews chapter 2, emphasizing the importance of not neglecting so great a salvation. He contrasts this with denominational doctrines and warns against false teachings that do not align with Scripture.

title: Lifting Him Up Out Of History
summary: William Branham speaks about the need to call upon the historical God to act in present-day crises, drawing parallels between biblical figures like Elijah, Moses, and Jesus and the current state of the world, the church, and individual lives. He encourages faith in a God who is the same yesterday, today, and forever, and expresses hope for a new ministry to begin.

title: But From The Beginning It Was Not So
summary: William Branham preaches on the danger of human traditions replacing God's commandments, using Jesus' rebuke of the Pharisees as a foundation. He calls the church to return to the original Pentecostal experience rather than relying on denominational creeds. The sermon emphasizes that God is the same yesterday, today, and forever, and that true salvation comes through a personal encounter with Christ, not through church membership or rituals.
themes: Personal experience of the Holy Spirit

title: Looking At The Unseen
summary: William Branham preaches on the importance of living by faith rather than by sight, using biblical examples like Abraham, Moses, Joshua, and Elisha to illustrate how looking at the unseen God enables believers to overcome barriers of unbelief and receive His promises. He encourages the congregation to pass the 'sound barrier' of doubt and enter into the freedom of faith, where healing and salvation are realized.

title: Faith Is Our Victory
summary: William Branham preaches on faith as the victory that overcomes the world, using examples from history, the Bible, and personal testimonies. He encourages believers to have a settled faith in God's promises, not just drift through life, and calls for an operation of faith to remove doubt and sin.

title: God-Called Man
summary: William Branham preaches on the necessity of God-called, God-trained men for revival. Using the story of Elisha and Elijah, he emphasizes crossing Jordan (separation from the world) and being molded by God rather than relying on theological education.

title: Hear His Voice
summary: William Branham preaches on the rarity of hearing God's voice in a world filled with distractions and false teachings. Using the story of Samuel, he emphasizes the need to quiet oneself and wait on the Lord to hear His voice. He contrasts the modern church's focus on programs and denominations with the necessity of personal communion with God.

title: Church Order
summary: William Branham outlines the order and doctrine of the Branham Tabernacle, emphasizing apostolic teachings, the operation of spiritual gifts, and the authority of the pastor. He details the proper sequence of worship, including silent prayer, tongues and interpretation, testimonies, and preaching, while warning against fanaticism and disorder.

title: The Sudden, Secret Going Away of the Church
summary: William Branham preaches on the sudden, secret rapture of the Church, warning believers to be ready at all times. He uses the analogy of the Pearl Harbor attack to illustrate how the world ignores warnings of Christ's coming, and emphasizes the need for individual readiness and the filling of the Holy Spirit.
themes: corruption of the world and church

title: Watchman, What Of The Night?
summary: William Branham preaches on the role of the watchman in Isaiah 21, warning of approaching danger and the coming of the Lord. He contrasts the world's indifference with the hope of the Morning Star for believers, emphasizing the urgency of repentance and readiness for Christ's return.

title: The Unity of One God in the One Church
summary: William Branham preaches on the unity of believers in God, contrasting true spiritual unity through the Holy Spirit with false unity under man-made systems. He emphasizes that the Holy Spirit is the seal of God and that believers must be born again to achieve God's purpose.
themes: God's control room in the heart

title: Where Is He, King of the Jews?
summary: William Branham preaches a Christmas sermon on the wise men seeking the newborn King, emphasizing that God leads sincere seekers through signs and the Spirit, and that the church often misses God's work due to tradition. He shares testimonies of healings and calls believers to follow the Light of Christ.

title: Why Little Bethlehem?
summary: William Branham explores the prophetic significance of Bethlehem as the birthplace of Jesus, tracing its lineage through Rahab, Ruth, and David to show God's sovereign choice of the humble over the great. He emphasizes that Bethlehem, meaning 'House of Bread,' was the fitting birthplace for Christ, the Bread of Life, and draws parallels to the faithful remnant church today.
themes: Typology of Christ in the Old Testament

title: Be Certain of God
summary: William Branham preaches on the importance of being absolutely certain of God, using the story of Elijah and the widow of Zarephath. He emphasizes that after meeting God's requirements, believers must stand firm in faith even when circumstances seem hopeless, trusting that God will keep His Word.

title: Blind Bartimaeus
summary: William Branham preaches on the story of blind Bartimaeus, emphasizing faith that stops Jesus despite obstacles. He draws parallels to the present, urging the audience to cry out to Jesus as the provided Lamb for their needs. The sermon includes a prayer line with healings and words of knowledge.

title: Simeon And Anna
summary: William Branham preaches on the biblical account of Simeon and Anna, emphasizing the Holy Spirit's guidance and God's faithfulness to His promises. He draws parallels to the present day, encouraging believers to be led by the Spirit and to expect God's miraculous works.

title: What Does Thou Here?
summary: William Branham preaches on the story of Elijah, emphasizing the need to hear the 'still small voice' of God amidst the noise of the world. He contrasts the spectacular signs of wind, earthquake, and fire with the quiet voice that truly carries God's presence, urging believers to seek depth and humility rather than outward displays.

title: Strait Is The Gate
summary: William Branham warns that the gate to eternal life is narrow and few will find it, comparing the current generation to the days of Noah and Sodom. He emphasizes that outward religious acts like speaking in tongues or performing miracles do not guarantee salvation; only a genuine, humble heart transformed by God will enter the Kingdom.

title: The Sign Of The Messiah
subtitle: 59-0329E
summary: William Branham preaches on the Messianic sign of knowing the secrets of the heart, demonstrating that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He calls the sick to believe and receive healing through the Holy Spirit's presence and power.

title: Water Baptism
summary: William Branham preaches on the biblical basis for water baptism by immersion in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, contrasting it with sprinkling and trinitarian formulas. He dedicates several infants and then baptizes eighteen candidates, emphasizing that baptism must follow the apostolic pattern found in Acts.

title: Living, Dying, Buried, Rising, Coming
subtitle: 59-0329S
summary: William Branham delivers an Easter sermon focusing on five key aspects of Christ's work: His life of love, His sacrificial death, His burial carrying away sins, His resurrection as God's receipt of payment, and His promised return. He emphasizes the hope and assurance believers have through Christ's completed work.

title: Living, Dying, Buried, Rising, Coming
summary: William Branham preaches on the five words: Living, Dying, Buried, Rising, Coming, focusing on Christ's love, death, burial, resurrection, and second coming. He emphasizes the need for divine love in the church and calls for repentance and revival.

title: What Is The Works Of God?
summary: William Branham explores the nature of God's works, emphasizing that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He argues that the same signs that identified Jesus as the Messiah—such as discerning thoughts and revealing secrets—must be present in the Church today through the Holy Spirit. Branham calls for unity among believers and warns against attributing the Spirit's work to the devil, which constitutes the unpardonable sin.
themes: The role of the Holy Spirit in the Church
The danger of blaspheming the Holy Spirit
The unity of the Body of Christ

title: It Was Not So From The Beginning
subtitle: 59-0405A
summary: William Branham preaches on returning to the original Pentecostal experience, emphasizing that the church must go back to the beginning where the Holy Spirit had full sway. He argues that modern creeds and denominations have departed from the foundational doctrines of the early church, such as divine healing, speaking in tongues, and water baptism by immersion. Using Matthew 19:8 as a text, he calls believers to abandon man-made traditions and seek the same power and joy experienced at Pentecost.

title: The Queen of Sheba
summary: William Branham preaches on the Queen of Sheba's journey to hear Solomon's wisdom, drawing a parallel to the present generation's need to seek the Holy Spirit. He emphasizes that the same Jesus who performed miracles is alive today and calls for unity among believers. The sermon concludes with a prayer line and an appeal for faith in Christ's presence.

title: New Ministry
summary: William Branham shares his birthday and introduces a new phase of his ministry focused on praying for the sick without necessarily having visions. He recounts a vision from four years ago that foretold this change and testifies to the healing of a baby named Ricky. He then prays for a prayer line, demonstrating the new approach.

title: Led by the Spirit
summary: William Branham preaches on being led by the Holy Spirit, using the biblical account of Simeon and Anna recognizing the infant Jesus in the temple. He shares a personal testimony of being led to pray for a dying boy, emphasizing that God's promises are sure and that the same Spirit leads believers today.

title: Blind Bartimaeus
summary: William Branham preaches on the story of blind Bartimaeus, emphasizing faith and the presence of Jesus Christ as the same yesterday, today, and forever. He connects Bartimaeus's cry for mercy to the need for spiritual and physical healing today, and demonstrates the gift of discernment as a sign of Christ's resurrection power.

title: Mary's Belief
summary: William Branham preaches on Mary's faith in God's promise, using her example to encourage the congregation to take God at His Word for revival and healing. He recounts testimonies of healings, including a baby healed of cancer and a congressman healed from a wheelchair, and calls for a fresh outpouring of the Holy Spirit.

title: Looking At The Unseen
summary: William Branham preaches on the importance of looking beyond the physical and temporal to the spiritual and eternal, using examples from the Bible such as Noah, Abraham, Moses, Joshua, Daniel, and the Hebrew children. He emphasizes that faith comes from hearing God's Word and allowing the Holy Spirit to lead, rather than being guided by what the eyes see.

title: Testimony
subtitle: 59-0411B
summary: William Branham shares a testimony of a blind colored girl healed in Jonesboro, Arkansas, fourteen years prior, emphasizing that healings are not mental but physical through faith in Jesus Christ. He recounts his humble beginnings and the power of God honoring simple faith, urging listeners to accept what Jesus has done for them.

title: Watching His Star
subtitle: 59-0411E
summary: William Branham preaches on the wise men who followed the star to find Jesus, drawing parallels to the Holy Spirit as the sign leading believers to Christ today. He emphasizes the need for expectancy and faith to recognize God's signs, and demonstrates the Spirit's work through words of knowledge and healings.

title: Be Certain of God
subtitle: 59-0412A
summary: William Branham encourages believers to be certain of God's promises, using the story of the widow of Zarephath and Elijah to illustrate that when we meet God's requirements, we can trust Him to fulfill His Word. He shares testimonies of healings and miracles, emphasizing that faith must be acted upon and held onto even when answers are delayed.

title: What Hearest Thou, Elijah?
summary: William Branham preaches on the story of Elijah, focusing on his experiences at Mount Carmel, the juniper tree, and the cave. He emphasizes the importance of listening to the still small voice of God rather than being distracted by noisy manifestations, and calls the church to repentance and faith in God's supernatural power.

title: Thirsting for Life
summary: William Branham preaches on the deep spiritual thirst that God places in every human heart, which can only be satisfied by the Holy Spirit. He contrasts worldly attempts to quench this thirst with the true satisfaction found in Christ, using the analogy of a wounded deer panting for water. The sermon includes prayer for the sick, a call to repentance, and an altar invitation.

title: God's Provided Way
summary: William Branham preaches on the parable of the wedding supper from Matthew 22, emphasizing that many are called but few are chosen. He stresses the necessity of receiving the Holy Spirit as the robe of righteousness, warning against entering by any other way than through Jesus Christ. He urges urgency in preparing for Christ's coming, drawing parallels to the days of Noah and Lot.

title: The Faith of Abraham
summary: William Branham teaches on the faith of Abraham as the model for believers, emphasizing that Christians are Abraham's Seed through Christ and must possess Abraham's unwavering faith in God's promises. He contrasts Abraham's patient trust with modern unbelief, urging separation from worldliness and full acceptance of divine healing and all redemptive blessings.

title: El-Shaddai
summary: William Branham preaches on God's covenant with Abraham, emphasizing that God is El Shaddai, the all-sufficient One who pours His strength into believers. He contrasts intellectual faith with heart faith, and calls the church to a revival that throws out dross and reflects Christ.

title: JEHOVAH-JIREH
summary: William Branham preaches on the faith of Abraham, focusing on God's covenant with Abraham and his seed. He emphasizes that believers are heirs to the same promises, including divine healing and resurrection, and uses the story of Abraham and Sarah's rejuvenation as a type of the believer's transformation at Christ's coming.
themes: the Holy Spirit in the church

title: A Time Of Decision
summary: William Branham preaches on the necessity of making a decision for God, using the story of Abraham's servant Eliezer finding a wife for Isaac as a type of the Church's relationship with Christ. He urges listeners to trust God's supernatural signs rather than human reasoning, and to commit fully to Christ without delay.

title: My Life Story
summary: William Branham shares his life story, from his birth in a Kentucky mountain cabin to his early encounters with the supernatural. He recounts a vision at age three and a voice at age seven that told him not to drink, smoke, or defile his body, preparing him for a future ministry. He also describes his struggles with poverty, his father's moonshining, and his early disdain for smoking and modern women.

title: Show Us The Father And It Will Satisfy Us
summary: William Branham preaches on the desire to see God, using John 14:7-8 as a text. He explores four ways to see God: in His universe, in His Word, in His Son, and in His people. Through personal anecdotes and biblical examples, he encourages faith and trust in God's presence and promises.

title: We Would See Jesus
summary: William Branham opens a three-day meeting in San Jose, emphasizing that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He explains that the same signs that identified Jesus as the Messiah—such as knowing people's hearts and revealing secrets—should be expected in the Church today through the Holy Spirit. Branham calls believers to look beyond programs and denominations to see Jesus manifested in His Church.

title: Abraham's Seed
summary: William Branham preaches on faith using the example of Abraham, emphasizing that believers are Abraham's seed and heirs to God's promises through Christ. He encourages the congregation to separate from unbelief, trust God's Word unconditionally, and call things that are not as though they were.

title: The Faith of Abraham
summary: William Branham discusses the faith of Abraham, emphasizing God's covenant and the importance of believing God's promises despite physical circumstances. He draws parallels between Abraham's experience and the modern believer's walk of faith, highlighting the need for the Holy Spirit as confirmation of faith.
themes: The Last Sign to the Church

title: Hear Ye Him
summary: William Branham preaches on the Mount of Transfiguration, emphasizing the command 'Hear ye Him' as the ultimate directive to listen to Jesus Christ, who is God's beloved Son. He contrasts the law and prophets with Christ's mercy and love, urging believers to heed Christ alone for salvation, healing, and eternal life.

title: Who Is This?
summary: William Branham preaches on the triumphal entry of Jesus into Jerusalem, drawing parallels to the present-day expectation of Christ's return. He emphasizes that the Holy Spirit is forerunning the Second Coming through signs, wonders, and healings, and challenges listeners to recognize Jesus as the same yesterday, today, and forever.

title: Mother's Day
subtitle: 59-0510M
summary: William Branham speaks on Mother's Day, emphasizing the importance of mothers and the hope of the resurrection. He shares personal testimonies of healings and reflects on the reunion with loved ones in the resurrection, urging listeners to rededicate their lives to God.

title: Images Of Christ
summary: William Branham preaches on what it truly means to be a Christian, emphasizing that it is not about outward symbols or church membership but about being inwardly transformed into the image of Christ through the Holy Spirit. He uses the example of Jesus washing the disciples' feet to illustrate the servant nature of true Christianity, calling believers to humility and love for one another.

title: What Hearest Thou, Elijah?
summary: William Branham speaks on the need for the church to wait upon God and hear His still small voice, using the story of Elijah after Mount Carmel. He contrasts noisy, sensational religion with the quiet, transformative power of God's voice, urging believers to seek personal encounters with God rather than relying on denominations or big movements.

title: As I Thought On My Ways
summary: William Branham preaches on the importance of reflecting on one's ways and turning to God's testimonies, especially in times of trouble. He uses personal anecdotes and biblical examples to illustrate how trouble often drives people to seek God, and urges the congregation to turn to God now rather than waiting for crisis.

title: The Time Of Decision
summary: William Branham preaches on the necessity of making a decisive choice for God, using the biblical account of Rebekah's decision to go with Abraham's servant to marry Isaac. He emphasizes the urgency of responding to the Holy Spirit's call and the importance of trusting in the old-time Pentecostal experience.

title: All The Days Of Our Life
summary: William Branham speaks on the need for complete surrender to God, contrasting man's desire for his own way with God's plan. He emphasizes that true Christian life is a continual sacrifice and that believers are bondslaves of Christ, serving Him in holiness all the days of their life.

title: Thirsting for Life
summary: William Branham speaks on the soul's thirst for God, contrasting worldly pleasures with eternal life. He shares a testimony from India where a blind man was healed, and urges believers to live as sons and daughters of the King.

title: Balm in Gilead
summary: William Branham preaches on Jeremiah 8:22, asking why God's people are not healed when there is balm in Gilead. He argues that people refuse God's remedy for sin and unbelief, and calls for repentance and receiving the Holy Spirit.

title: Questions and Answers
summary: William Branham answers questions from the congregation on topics including spiritual gifts, salvation and the Holy Ghost, Communion, and the fall of Satan. He emphasizes the importance of the Holy Spirit in interpreting Scripture and warns against mixing with unbelievers.

title: A Deceived Church, By The World
summary: William Branham uses the story of Samson and Delilah to illustrate how the church has been deceived by the world, losing its spiritual power through compromise, organization, and worldly wisdom. He calls for a return to the Holy Ghost and the new birth, warning that the church's strength has been shaved off by worldliness.

title: Where Has Thy Strength Gone, Samson?
summary: William Branham uses the story of Samson and Delilah as an allegory for the modern church, warning against flirting with the world and losing spiritual power through organization, intellectualism, and worldliness. He calls for a return to the Holy Ghost, old-fashioned revival, and the new birth experience.

title: Thinking On Our Ways
summary: William Branham preaches on the importance of self-examination and repentance, using the text 'I thought on my ways, and turned my feet unto thy testimonies' (Psalm 119:59). He shares personal stories and biblical examples to illustrate that troubles often drive people to God, but urges believers to think on their ways and turn to God before trouble strikes. The sermon emphasizes confession of sins, living righteously, and having a clear conscience before God.
themes: God as a present help in trouble
The importance of a clear conscience
The blood of Jesus for cleansing

title: Balm in Gilead
summary: William Branham preaches on the theme that God has provided a remedy for sin and sickness through Jesus Christ, but people refuse to receive it due to unbelief. He emphasizes the need for the new birth and the baptism of the Holy Spirit, and calls listeners to repent and accept God's provision.

title: Be Certain of God
summary: William Branham preaches on the certainty of God using the story of the widow of Zarephath and Elijah. He emphasizes that God tests faith, and believers must hold onto His Word even in desperate circumstances. The sermon calls for absolute trust in God's promises for salvation, healing, and the Holy Spirit.
themes: the Holy Spirit and the Word

title: Dedication Of Building, To The Lord
summary: William Branham dedicates a church building, using the Old Testament tabernacle as a type to explain the three-room house of God: justification, sanctification, and baptism of the Holy Spirit. He emphasizes the necessity of the Blood of Christ for fellowship and warns against denominational barriers, calling for unity among all believers.

title: A Total Deliverance
summary: William Branham speaks on the need for complete surrender to God and unity within the church, using the Exodus account of Moses and the deliverance of Israel as a type. He emphasizes that total deliverance from sin and sickness comes when everything is brought under the Blood of Christ, and the church is unified in heart and accord.

title: Without Money Or Without Price
summary: William Branham preaches on Isaiah 55, emphasizing that salvation and spiritual blessings are free gifts from God, not to be bought with money. He contrasts worldly pursuits that cost money but bring no lasting satisfaction with the free offer of eternal life through Christ. Using examples like the healing at the Beautiful Gate and the prodigal son, he calls listeners to come to God without price.

title: The Reaction To An Action
summary: William Branham speaks on the importance of drawing nigh to God and confessing sins before prayer, using the story of the widow of Zarephath to illustrate how faith mixed with God's Word and Spirit can bring provision and healing. He encourages believers to hold fast to their testimony and trust God even in dark times.

title: IT IS I, BE NOT AFRAID
summary: William Branham preaches on Jesus walking on water and telling his disciples 'It is I; be not afraid.' He emphasizes that Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever, and that the Holy Spirit is present to heal and save. He calls believers to not be afraid of the Spirit's work, but to accept it as their only hope.

title: Discerning The Body Of The Lord
summary: William Branham preaches on the importance of discerning the Body of the Lord, which is the Church, and warns against taking communion unworthily. He calls for spiritual discernment in all aspects of Christian life, including healing, the baptism of the Holy Spirit, and recognizing the signs of the times. Branham emphasizes that the same signs given to Sodom will be given to this generation before Christ's return.

title: Why?
summary: William Branham preaches on the theme of 'Why?'—why there is sin and sickness in the world despite God's provision of healing and the Holy Spirit. He uses the metaphor of a balm in Gilead to illustrate that God has provided a cure for sin and sickness, but people refuse to take it due to stubbornness and pride. He calls for repentance and receiving the Holy Spirit.

title: As I Thought On My Ways
summary: William Branham reflects on the importance of turning to God in times of trouble, using personal stories and biblical examples to illustrate that God is a present help. He urges listeners to examine their lives, repent, and commit to following Christ before it is too late.

title: As The Eagle Stirreth Up Her Nest
summary: William Branham preaches on Deuteronomy 32:11, comparing the Church to an eagle. He describes the eagle's unique characteristics—its high nest, keen vision, and renewal of youth—as symbols of the believer's life in Christ. Branham urges Christians to rise above worldly entanglements and stand on the unshakable Rock of Ages.
themes: Eagle as symbol of the Church

title: Palmerworm, Locust, Cankerworm, Caterpillar
summary: William Branham preaches on the restoration of the Church using Joel's prophecy of the palmerworm, locust, cankerworm, and caterpillar. He argues that these insects represent stages of spiritual decay that have eaten away the original faith and power of the early Church. Branham calls for a return to the original apostolic faith, contending earnestly for the faith once delivered to the saints.

title: Planting The Vine And Where To Plant It
summary: William Branham preaches on Psalm 80, using the metaphor of a vine to describe God's people. He contrasts the true vine, Christ, with wild vines of denominationalism and unbelief, urging believers to be planted by the rivers of water—the Holy Spirit—to bear spiritual fruit.

title: What Went Ye Out To See?
summary: William Branham preaches on the question Jesus asked about John the Baptist: 'What went ye out to see?' He contrasts the world, the lukewarm church, and true believers, emphasizing that God uses simple, anointed people to accomplish His purposes. Branham calls believers to dedicate their hands and lives to Christ, doing whatever is in their power for the Gospel.

title: Why Cry? Speak!
summary: William Branham preaches on Exodus 14:15-16, urging believers to stop crying to God and instead speak His Word and go forward. He emphasizes that God's anointed messengers must be obeyed, and that the same Holy Spirit who worked in Jesus works today through signs and wonders. The sermon calls for faith and action rather than doubt and complaint.

title: Who Is This?
summary: William Branham preaches on the triumphal entry of Jesus into Jerusalem, using the crowd's question 'Who is this?' to draw parallels to the present-day work of the Holy Spirit. He emphasizes that the Holy Spirit's manifestations—healing, discernment, and transformation—cause the world to question, just as they did when Jesus rode into Jerusalem. Branham calls believers to make a decision for Christ and prepare for His second coming.

title: Possessing The Enemy's Gates
summary: William Branham preaches on the promise that Abraham's seed will possess the gates of their enemies, drawing from Genesis 24 and 22. He emphasizes that believers, as spiritual seed of Abraham, are heirs to this promise and must endure testing before receiving it. The sermon encourages faith in God's promises over natural circumstances, citing biblical examples of those who possessed enemy gates through faith.

title: My New Ministry
summary: William Branham shares a personal experience in the woods where God confirms a new phase of his ministry through the power of spoken words, demonstrating that whatever one says in faith can come to pass. He recounts how the Holy Spirit instructed him to speak and materialize his desires, using the example of calling squirrels to him. This marks a transition from his previous ministry of visions to a greater authority in spoken faith.

title: A Prophet Like Unto Moses
summary: William Branham speaks on the need for the Church to recognize the living presence of Christ through the Holy Spirit, using the account of Jesus walking on water to illustrate how believers often fail to see Him in their midst. He emphasizes that the same miracles Jesus performed are available today through faith, and calls for unity among believers in preparation for the Second Coming.
themes: The Church as the Body of Christ

title: Thy Seed Shall Possess The Gate Of His Enemy
summary: William Branham preaches on the promise that Abraham's seed shall possess the gate of their enemies, drawing from Genesis 24 and 22. He connects this promise to believers in Christ, who as Abraham's seed through faith, have victory over every enemy including sickness, sin, and death. The sermon culminates in a call for repentance and healing, with demonstrations of the Holy Spirit's discernment and power.

title: Who Is This?
summary: William Branham preaches on the question asked by the people of Jerusalem when Jesus entered the city: 'Who is this?' He draws parallels between the first coming of Christ and the latter-day outpouring of the Holy Spirit, emphasizing that the same Spirit that worked in Jesus is working today through signs, wonders, and the gathering of believers. Branham encourages the congregation to know Christ personally and to believe in His promises despite the world's confusion.

title: Speak to This Mountain
summary: William Branham discusses the Scripture Mark 11:23 about speaking to a mountain and having faith. He shares personal experiences of the Holy Spirit's leading, including a vision about a fish coming back to life and a warning about a trap set for him. He emphasizes the importance of being careful with words and the new ministry beginning.
themes: the new ministry of speaking to mountains

title: Balm in Gilead
summary: William Branham preaches on the spiritual condition of the church and the world, using Jeremiah 8:22 to ask why God's people remain sick when there is balm in Gilead. He emphasizes the need for genuine new birth and the inoculation of the Holy Spirit to overcome sin and unbelief.

title: From The Beginning It Wasn't So
summary: William Branham preaches on the unchanging nature of God's Word, contrasting it with man-made traditions and creeds. He emphasizes that the Church must return to the Pentecostal experience of the early believers, where signs and wonders followed. Using Matthew 19:8 as a text, he argues that many modern teachings deviate from what was true 'from the beginning.'

title: Jehovah of Miracles
summary: William Branham preaches on the Annunciation to Mary, emphasizing the importance of taking God at His Word without doubting. He contrasts Mary's faith with Zacharias's doubt and encourages believers to believe God's promises despite impossibilities. The sermon also touches on the power of the name of Jesus and the need for unity and sincerity in the church.

title: Blind Bartimaeus
summary: William Branham preaches on the story of blind Bartimaeus, emphasizing that faith in Jesus Christ can bring healing and salvation. He contrasts Bartimaeus's persistent faith with the unbelief of the religious leaders, and encourages the congregation to trust in the Lamb of God who is present to heal and save today.

title: Door To The Heart
summary: William Branham preaches on Revelation 3:20, emphasizing that Jesus stands at the door of the human heart and knocks, but the latch is on the inside—only the individual can open. He explores various 'doors' within the heart, such as pride, private life, faith, and spiritual sight, urging listeners to let Jesus be not only Savior but also Lord, allowing Him full access to transform their lives.

title: Let Us See God
summary: William Branham preaches on seeing God in four ways: in His universe, in His Word, in His Son, and in His people. He shares personal stories from nature and his ministry to illustrate God's presence and power.

title: What Is The Holy Ghost?
summary: William Branham teaches on the nature and purpose of the Holy Ghost, describing it as a sign, seal, and the Spirit of Christ in believers. He emphasizes that the Holy Ghost is a covenant promise to Abraham's seed, which includes all who are in Christ, and that it seals believers until the day of redemption.

title: What Was The Holy Ghost Given For?
summary: William Branham teaches on the purpose of the Holy Spirit, explaining that God sent the Holy Spirit to dwell in His Church and continue His work through believers. He emphasizes that the Holy Spirit is God Himself living in the Church, restoring fellowship lost in Eden, and preparing the Bride for the Rapture.

title: Questions and Answers on the Holy Ghost
summary: William Branham addresses questions about the Holy Ghost, clarifying the biblical account of Pentecost and the distinction between speaking in tongues as a gift versus the initial evidence of receiving the Holy Spirit. He emphasizes that the Holy Spirit is received by faith according to God's laws, and that true baptism of the Holy Ghost is evidenced by a transformed life and the manifestation of God's presence, not necessarily by speaking in unknown tongues.
themes: Initial evidence of the Holy Spirit

title: Identified With Christ
summary: William Branham discusses the human desire to identify with an example, and how people often choose worldly figures like movie stars or cowboys instead of Jesus Christ. He explains that true identification with Christ comes through repentance and baptism, which unites believers with His death, burial, and resurrection. Branham also addresses questions about speaking in tongues and the Holy Spirit, emphasizing that the fruit of the Spirit, especially love, is the true evidence of receiving the Holy Ghost.

title: Conference With God
summary: William Branham speaks on the importance of holding a conference with God, drawing parallels between earthly conferences and divine meetings. He uses biblical examples such as Moses at the burning bush and the Red Sea, and the incarnation of Christ, to illustrate how God calls His people to reason together and make decisions in crucial moments.

title: Questions and Answers
summary: William Branham answers questions from the congregation on topics including demonology, the fate of the spirits that entered the swine, the nature of eternal life, the importance of the Holy Ghost, and predestination. He emphasizes that only God has eternal life and that believers receive it through the Holy Spirit, becoming part of God and unable to perish. He also warns against religious deception and the need to earnestly seek the Holy Ghost.

title: A Super Sense
summary: William Branham speaks on the concept of a 'super sense'—faith—which is the sixth sense given to Christians that governs and surpasses the five natural senses. He emphasizes that this super sense enables believers to believe God's Word contrary to physical evidence, and he illustrates this with testimonies of healings.

title: A Super Sign
summary: William Branham delivers a Christmas message centered on Isaiah 7:10-16, presenting the virgin birth of Immanuel as God's eternal super sign. He contrasts human achievements like the Titanic and Hitler's fortifications with God's humble sign of a baby, emphasizing that God dwells with His people. Branham connects this sign to the present evening light revival, where the same works of God are manifested through believers.

title: And From That Time
summary: In this New Year's Eve sermon, William Branham emphasizes the necessity of a personal encounter with God that brings eternal change, contrasting it with temporary New Year's resolutions. He illustrates through biblical figures like Abraham, Moses, Mary, Peter, and Paul how meeting God transforms a person forever. Branham urges listeners to seek a genuine meeting with God rather than merely turning a new page.

title: Conference With God
summary: William Branham speaks on the importance of having a personal conference with God, using biblical examples such as the conferences in Eden, at the burning bush, at the Red Sea, in Gethsemane, at Calvary, and at Pentecost. He emphasizes that God invites all to reason together and that through faith, believers can receive healing and salvation.

title: SIRS, WE WOULD SEE JESUS
summary: William Branham preaches on the desire to see Jesus, emphasizing that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He uses biblical examples, such as Nathanael and the Samaritan woman, to show how Jesus revealed His Messiahship through supernatural knowledge, and argues that the same signs should follow believers today.
themes: Christ the same yesterday, today, and forever
Divine healing as part of salvation

title: The Queen of Sheba
summary: William Branham preaches on the Queen of Sheba's journey to hear Solomon's wisdom, drawing a parallel to the present generation's rejection of the Holy Spirit's work. He emphasizes that unbelief is the original sin and that the sign of the resurrection is available today through the same Holy Spirit that empowered Jesus.

title: And From That Time
subtitle: 60-0210E
summary: William Branham preaches on the transformative power of meeting God, using biblical examples like Abraham, Moses, Mary, Peter, Paul, and Bartimaeus. He emphasizes that from the moment one encounters God, life is forever changed, and he demonstrates the presence of Christ through words of knowledge and healing.

title: The Revelation That Was Given to Me
summary: William Branham recounts his early life, supernatural experiences, and the calling to pray for the sick. He describes visions, an angelic visitation, and the validation of his ministry through healings, emphasizing the unity of believers and the fulfillment of biblical prophecy.

title: Hearing, Recognizing, Acting on the Word of God
summary: William Branham preaches on the two spiritual forces represented by Jacob and Esau, emphasizing the difference between the carnal and spiritual believer. He stresses the importance of election, separation from the world, and acting on God's Word, warning against those who come close to the truth but turn away.

title: Conferences
summary: William Branham opens a revival meeting in Phoenix, Arizona, reflecting on the changes in the valley and the unchanging nature of God. He uses the theme of conferences to illustrate how God calls His people to reason together in times of emergency, citing examples from Eden, the burning bush, the Red Sea, Gethsemane, and Pentecost. He urges the church to hold a conference with God to receive orders and move forward in faith.

title: The Oncoming Storm
summary: William Branham warns of an impending spiritual storm, using the parable of the wise and foolish builders and a story of a Florida hurricane to illustrate the need for preparation. He emphasizes that true safety is found only in Jesus Christ and the baptism of the Holy Spirit, urging listeners to heed the warning before judgment comes.

title: He Careth For You
summary: William Branham preaches on God's care for humanity, emphasizing that only Christ can truly comfort and save. He contrasts worldly substitutes for the Holy Spirit with the genuine comfort found in Jesus, sharing personal testimonies of loss and God's faithfulness.

title: From That Time
summary: William Branham preaches on the transformative power of encountering God, using biblical examples like Abraham, Moses, Mary, Paul, and the woman at the well to illustrate that meeting God changes a person forever. He emphasizes that true conversion is not intellectual but a spiritual experience that leads to a changed life.

title: Former and Latter Rain
summary: William Branham preaches on the end-time signs, comparing the watchman's warning in Zechariah and Isaiah to the present day. He emphasizes the coming of the latter rain and the need for believers to shine as morning stars reflecting Christ's imminent return.

title: Thirsting for Life
summary: William Branham speaks on the theme of thirsting for God, using Psalm 63 to emphasize that God's lovingkindness is better than life itself. He shares testimonies of healing, including the story of Florence Nightingale, and calls for unity among believers as sons and daughters of the King.

title: Be Not Afraid, It Is I
summary: William Branham preaches on the biblical account of Jesus walking on water, emphasizing that Jesus is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He encourages believers to recognize Christ's presence in their storms and to have faith in His healing power, demonstrating the gift of discernment as a sign of the Messiah.
themes: Jesus Christ the same yesterday, today, and forever

title: It Wasn't So From The Beginning
summary: William Branham preaches on the unchanging nature of God and the need to return to the original Pentecostal experience. He argues that church traditions have perverted the Word of God, and that true faith requires going back to the beginning—to the baptism of the Holy Ghost, divine healing, and the signs and wonders of the early church.

title: Discernment of Spirit
summary: William Branham teaches on the importance of discerning spirits, emphasizing that believers should judge individuals by their motives and objectives rather than by their denomination or outward gifts. He uses Old Testament examples like Moses, Joseph, and David to illustrate how true prophets are anointed by God to glorify Him and edify the Church, not themselves.

title: Why?
summary: In this sermon, William Branham uses the text from Jeremiah 8:20-22 to ask why people refuse God's provided way of salvation and healing. He compares the Holy Spirit to a perfect balm that can heal sin-sick souls, and warns that at the Judgment, God will ask why people rejected His provision. Branham emphasizes that unbelief is the root sin, and that the Holy Spirit is available to all who will receive it.

title: Elijah and the Meal-Offering
summary: William Branham preaches on the story of Elijah and the widow of Zarephath, emphasizing faith, sacrifice, and the mixing of the Word and the Spirit. He draws parallels to modern believers, urging them to meet God's requirements and trust in His promises even in dark times.

title: Mary's Belief
summary: William Branham preaches on Mary's faith and belief in God's promise, drawing parallels to the need for faith in divine healing. He emphasizes taking God at His Word without doubting, and highlights the power of the name of Jesus.

title: Door To The Heart
summary: William Branham preaches on Revelation 3:20, emphasizing that Jesus stands at the door of the heart and knocks, waiting for individuals to open. He contrasts the honor of receiving earthly dignitaries with the rejection of Christ, and urges listeners to let Jesus be Lord over every area of their lives, including private life, pride, and faith.

title: Hear Ye Him
summary: William Branham preaches on the transfiguration of Jesus, emphasizing the need to hear and obey Christ alone. He contrasts the law of Moses and the prophets with the gospel of Jesus, and calls the church to be filled with the Holy Spirit and do the works of Christ.

title: The Unchangeable God
summary: William Branham preaches on the unchanging nature of God, emphasizing that God is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He uses biblical examples such as Moses, Jacob, Isaiah, and Elijah to illustrate that God works in unexpected ways and times, and calls believers to have faith in God's promises for healing and salvation.

title: Is There Anything Too Hard For The Lord?
summary: William Branham preaches on the theme that nothing is too hard for the Lord, using the story of Abraham and Sarah's visitation by angels in Genesis 18. He emphasizes the importance of maintaining a spiritual atmosphere and recognizing God's presence, even when circumstances seem impossible. The sermon includes testimonies of healing and a demonstration of the Holy Spirit's discernment.
themes: The role of the Holy Spirit

title: IT IS I, BE NOT AFRAID
summary: William Branham preaches on Jesus walking on water and calming the disciples' fear, emphasizing that Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He encourages believers to have faith in God's promises and to recognize the Holy Spirit's presence in the church today.

title: Blind Bartimaeus
summary: William Branham preaches on the story of blind Bartimaeus, emphasizing faith that stops Jesus despite the crowd and distractions. He encourages the audience to cry out for mercy and believe that God has provided a Lamb for their healing and salvation.

title: From That Time
summary: William Branham preaches on the transformative power of encountering God, using the phrase 'from that time' to illustrate how a single moment with God can change a person's life forever. He shares testimonies of biblical figures and modern individuals who were radically changed after meeting God, and calls the congregation to make that decision tonight.

title: The Queen of Sheba
summary: William Branham preaches on the Queen of Sheba's journey to hear Solomon's wisdom, drawing parallels to the present generation's need to seek the Holy Spirit and recognize God's gifts. He emphasizes faith, the supernatural nature of Christianity, and the danger of rejecting divine visitation.

title: Why?
subtitle: 60-0401M
summary: William Branham preaches on the question 'Why?' from Jeremiah 8:22, asking why people remain sick in sin when God has provided the remedy—the Holy Ghost. He compares the balm in Gilead to a divine toxin that inoculates believers from sin, proven by Christ's life, death, and resurrection.

title: Believest Thou This?
summary: William Branham preaches on the story of Lazarus, emphasizing that when Jesus leaves a home or church, trouble follows. He calls the church to return to Pentecostal power and demonstrates faith through a testimony of a baby's healing.
themes: the role of women in the church

title: As the Eagle Stirreth
summary: William Branham uses the metaphor of an eagle to describe the Christian life, emphasizing freedom in the Spirit, trust in God's power, and the need to rise above doubt and denominational constraints. He shares personal experiences with eagles to illustrate how believers should rely on God's wings and voice.

title: Go, Tell
summary: In this Easter sermon, William Branham emphasizes the importance of having a message when we go to tell others about Christ. He contrasts physical preparation with spiritual readiness, urging believers to focus on the resurrection and the power of God rather than on building churches or denominations. The sermon includes baby dedications and a call to believe in the signs that follow believers.

title: I Know
subtitle: 60-0417S
summary: In this Easter sermon, William Branham draws from Job 19:25-27 to emphasize that trials and tribulations are necessary for spiritual growth and to bring believers into a closer fellowship with God. He shares personal experiences of loss and disappointment, testifying that through these 'ash heap' experiences, one can come to the confident declaration, 'I know my Redeemer liveth.' The sermon encourages believers to see beyond present sufferings to the hope of resurrection and the coming of Christ.

title: Adoption 1
summary: William Branham begins a series on the Book of Ephesians, comparing the believer's journey to Israel's journey from Egypt to Canaan. He emphasizes positional truth in Christ and the baptism of the Holy Spirit as the promised land for New Testament believers.

title: The Rejected King
summary: William Branham preaches on the biblical account of Israel's demand for a king, drawing parallels to the modern church's tendency to reject the leadership of the Holy Spirit in favor of human leaders and organizations. He emphasizes that God's will is for His people to be led directly by the Spirit, not by men or denominations.

title: Adoption 2
summary: William Branham continues a series on the Book of Ephesians, focusing on positional placing of the Church in Christ. He discusses predestination, the manifestation of the sons of God, and the inheritance of believers, drawing parallels between Israel's journey to the Promised Land and the spiritual journey of the Church.

title: Adoption 4
summary: William Branham teaches on the mystery of God's will, predestination, and the adoption of sons. He explains that believers are predestined to eternal life and that the church is being prepared as the capstone of the pyramid, perfectly joined to Christ. He emphasizes the coming manifestation of the sons of God and the restoration of man's original dominion.

title: Adoption 3
summary: In this lesson, William Branham continues teaching on the Book of Ephesians, focusing on the theme of adoption and positional placing of the church in Christ. He emphasizes that salvation is by grace alone through the Holy Spirit, not by works or denominational affiliation, and calls believers to sanctification and obedience to God's Word.
themes: The role of the Holy Spirit

title: To Whom Shall We Go?
summary: William Branham preaches on the exclusivity of Jesus Christ as the only way, truth, light, foundation, happiness, achievement, and translation to eternal life. He urges listeners to come to Christ rather than rely on creeds, churches, or worldly pursuits.

title: To Whom Would We Go?
summary: William Branham preaches on the uniqueness of Jesus Christ as the only Way, Truth, Light, Foundation, Happiness, Achievement, and Translation. He urges listeners to turn to Christ alone for eternal life and peace, contrasting worldly foundations with the solid rock of Jesus.

title: Hearing, Receiving, And Acting
summary: William Branham preaches on the necessity of hearing God's Word, recognizing it as truth, and acting upon it. He contrasts the carnal believer (represented by Esau) with the spiritual believer (Jacob), emphasizing that true faith requires separation from the world and obedience to God's promises.

title: Be Not Afraid
summary: William Branham preaches on the disciples' fear during the storm on the Sea of Galilee and Jesus' reassurance, 'Be not afraid.' He draws parallels to the modern church's drift from the Holy Spirit and calls for a return to prayer, holiness, and reliance on God's power.

title: The Rejected King
summary: William Branham preaches on the biblical account of Israel's demand for a king, drawing parallels to modern Christianity's tendency to reject the Holy Spirit's leadership in favor of human organizations and worldly patterns. He warns against denominationalism and emphasizes the need for the Holy Spirit to govern the church.

title: Fellowship
summary: William Branham speaks on the theme of Christian fellowship, emphasizing that true fellowship with God and one another is based solely on the shed blood of Jesus Christ, not on organizations, education, or denominations. He uses the Old Testament tabernacle as a type to illustrate the progression from justification through sanctification to the baptism of the Holy Ghost, which brings believers into the Holiest of holies for divine communion.
themes: Justification, sanctification, baptism of the Holy Ghost
The tabernacle as a type of Christ
The super sign of Christ's incarnation

title: Faith Is the Sixth Sense
summary: William Branham teaches that faith is a sixth sense given by God to deliver and rescue us from the limitations of the five physical senses. He argues that this sense has become dormant in many believers due to lack of use and wrong teaching, and he illustrates its power through testimonies of miraculous healings and deliverances.

title: Speak To This Rock
summary: William Branham preaches on the importance of speaking to the Rock, which represents Christ, for all needs including salvation, healing, and the Holy Spirit. He uses the Old Testament story of Moses speaking to the rock in the wilderness as a type of Christ, emphasizing that believers today must speak to the Rock in faith. The sermon concludes with a prayer line for the sick.

title: The Unfailing Realities of the Living God
summary: William Branham speaks on the need for true, living religion that brings deliverance, contrasting it with mere creeds and rituals. He emphasizes that God's power is available through the Holy Spirit and the Word, but many reject it because it is too unusual. He calls believers to follow the road map of Scripture without compromise.

title: God's Provided Approach to Divine Fellowship
summary: William Branham preaches on the necessity of the Blood of Jesus Christ as the only way to restore fellowship between God and man. He uses the Old Testament type of the red heifer and the waters of separation to illustrate how believers must come under the Blood, apply common faith, and enter into the Shekinah Glory of God through the Holy Spirit for true divine fellowship.

title: Sir, We Would See Jesus
tags: Jesus Christ same yesterday today forever
summary: William Branham opens a ten-day campaign in Oregon, emphasizing that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He uses the account of Philip bringing Nathanael to Jesus to illustrate that Christ's supernatural knowledge and power are still available today. Branham calls for a soul-stirring revival and urges believers to move with the Spirit rather than settling into denominational complacency.
themes: Jesus Christ the same yesterday, today, and forever
Divine healing through faith in Christ's finished work
The need for revival and moving with the Holy Spirit
The urgency of the Gospel in the end times

title: God's Provided Way of Approach to Fellowship
summary: William Branham preaches on the necessity of the blood of Jesus Christ as the only way to restore fellowship with God. He uses Old Testament types like the red heifer and the waters of separation to illustrate how faith in Christ's sacrifice cleanses sin and brings believers into communion with God. Branham emphasizes that true fellowship requires both the Word and the Spirit, and that no creed or denomination can substitute for the blood.

title: The Queen of Sheba
summary: William Branham preaches on the Queen of Sheba as a type of the last-day church, contrasting her faith with the unbelief of Jesus' generation. He emphasizes that the resurrection sign of Jonah is given to this adulterous generation, and that true faith looks away from symptoms to the finished work of Christ.

title: The Door Inside The Door
summary: William Branham preaches on Revelation 3:20, emphasizing that Christ stands at the door of the heart and knocks, but the latch is on the inside. He urges believers not only to accept Jesus as Savior but also to let Him be Lord, opening every area of life—including pride and private habits—to His control.
themes: Christ knocking at the heart's door

title: Hear Ye Him
summary: William Branham preaches on the importance of hearing and obeying Jesus Christ, using the Mount of Transfiguration as a context. He emphasizes that the Holy Spirit is the true Tutor of the Church, and calls for repentance from worldliness and a return to old-fashioned holiness.

title: Blind Bartimaeus
summary: William Branham preaches on the simplicity of faith, using the story of Blind Bartimaeus and personal anecdotes of healings among Native Americans and in Mexico. He emphasizes that God is the same today as in biblical times and that childlike faith brings healing.

title: From That Time
summary: William Branham shares personal testimonies of miracles, including raising a boy from the dead in Finland and healing a crippled girl, emphasizing the power of faith and the importance of a turning point in one's life. He then introduces his sermon 'From That Time' based on Matthew 4:17, discussing how a single moment can change a person's destiny for good or evil.

title: Be Not Afraid
summary: William Branham closes a revival meeting with thanks, encouragement, and a sermon on Matthew 14:27. He explains the operation of the gift of discernment and healing, emphasizing that faith comes from the people. He shares personal stories and calls for unity and cooperation among believers.

title: It Is I
