summary: William Branham speaks on the sign of the Messiah as a prophet, using the story of Jesus walking on water and the disciples' recognition of Him. He emphasizes that Jesus is the same yesterday, today, and forever, and that the Messianic sign of a prophet is still relevant today.
themes: Jesus Christ the same yesterday, today, and forever

title: Watchman, What of the Night?
summary: William Branham preaches on the role of the watchman in the Old Testament and applies it to the present day, warning of the approaching judgment and the second coming of Christ. He emphasizes the need for spiritual vigilance and the reflection of Christ's light through the Church in a dark and pleasure-mad world.

title: Speak To The Rock And It Shall Give Forth His Water
summary: William Branham preaches on the journey of the Israelites in the wilderness, using the story of Moses striking the rock to bring forth water as a type of the Church's journey to the Promised Land. He emphasizes the importance of faith over carnal thinking, claiming God's promises, and the need for a Spirit-filled church that moves forward despite obstacles.

title: The Unchangeable Word of God
summary: William Branham speaks on the unchanging nature of God's Word, using the Annunciation to Mary as an example of God's faithfulness to His promises. He contrasts the power of God's Word with human traditions and emphasizes the need for signs and wonders in missions.

title: What It Takes To Overcome All Unbelief: Our Faith
summary: William Branham speaks about the universal nature of God's Spirit among believers, the importance of faith over reason, and the need for revival to shake out unbelief. He explains that all redemptive blessings were completed at Calvary and that divine healing is received by faith in God's Word.

title: Show Us The Father And It Will Satisfy Us
summary: William Branham preaches on the desire of the human heart to see God, exploring four ways to see Him: in His universe, in His Word, in His Son, and in His people. He uses illustrations from nature and personal experiences to demonstrate God's presence and faithfulness.

title: El-Shaddai
summary: William Branham preaches on God as El-Shaddai, the breasted God who nurses His children back to strength and health. He uses Abraham's story to illustrate total obedience and faith in God's promises, emphasizing that the same Spirit that worked in Christ works in believers today.
themes: The Holy Spirit in the Church

title: Abraham
summary: William Branham continues his series on Abraham, emphasizing simple faith and the importance of obedience to God's Word. He shares testimonies of healing among Native Americans and recounts a personal vision of the afterlife, encouraging believers to press on toward the reward.

title: As The Eagle Stirreth Up Her Nest
summary: William Branham uses the metaphor of an eagle stirring up its nest to describe how God prepares His children for spiritual growth and freedom. He contrasts the eagle's nature—its ability to soar high, renew its youth, and build its nest on high—with the caged condition of believers bound by creeds and worldliness. Branham calls for a return to the power of the Holy Spirit and the Word, urging believers to rise above earthly limitations.
themes: Eagle as symbol of spiritual life
Renewal of youth through the Holy Spirit
The Word of God as spiritual food
The need for revival and the Holy Spirit

title: Lamb And Dove
summary: William Branham preaches on the symbols of the Lamb and the Dove, representing Jesus Christ and the Holy Spirit. He emphasizes the need for believers to be led by the Spirit, bearing fruit rather than manufacturing it, and warns against worldliness in the church.

title: Hear Ye Him
summary: William Branham preaches on the transfiguration of Jesus, emphasizing the command 'Hear Ye Him' as the ultimate authority. He contrasts human values with divine values, using the parable of a valuable stamp and the story of Abraham Lincoln's pardon to illustrate that God's Word must be received as a pardon to be effective. He calls the church to reflect Christ and warns against substituting the Holy Spirit's guidance with human traditions.

title: Debate On Tongues
summary: William Branham discusses the gift of speaking in tongues, arguing that it is not the initial evidence of the Holy Spirit. He uses Scripture to show that on the Day of Pentecost, everyone heard in their own language, and that love is the true evidence of the Holy Spirit. He also warns that Satan can counterfeit tongues.
themes: initial evidence of the Holy Spirit
Scripture as the basis of truth
unity of the Body of Christ

title: Five Definite Identifications of the True Church of the Living God
summary: William Branham teaches on the nature of the true Church as the mystical Body of Christ, called out from the world and governed by Christ as King. He contrasts this with organized denominations, which he identifies as having an anti-Christ spirit, and emphasizes that the Church is a spiritual kingdom, not a human organization.

title: As I Was With Moses, So I Will Be With Thee
summary: William Branham preaches on Joshua 1, emphasizing God's promise to Joshua that as He was with Moses, so He would be with him. He draws parallels between the natural journey of Israel and the spiritual journey of the Church, urging believers to stay true to God's Word and follow the leading of the Holy Spirit.

title: That Day On Calvary
summary: William Branham preaches on the significance of Calvary, emphasizing that it settled the sin question once for all, broke Satan's power, and opened the way for believers to have eternal life and live selflessly for others. He calls for a genuine, automatic Christian life born of the Spirit, not mere religious works.

title: Visions Of William Branham
summary: William Branham recounts early visions and healings following his ordination, including the healing of a crushed colored man, a crippled Armenian woman, a dying baby, and a paralyzed girl. He emphasizes the importance of waiting for the exact fulfillment of visions and the faithfulness of God's guidance.

title: The Kinsman Redeemer
summary: William Branham preaches on the Book of Ruth, using the story of Ruth and Naomi as a type of the Church and the believer's journey of decision, service, rest, and reward. He emphasizes the concept of the Kinsman Redeemer as a picture of Christ's complete redemption.

title: Condemnation By Representation
summary: William Branham warns against spiritual 'hybreeding'—mixing God's Word with man's theology—which produces a faith without life, unable to reproduce. He traces this from Eve's disobedience to modern denominationalism, urging believers to stay pure to the original Word and Spirit.

title: It Is I
summary: William Branham preaches on the account of Jesus walking on water, emphasizing that Jesus is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He encourages believers to recognize Christ's presence and power in their lives, especially in times of trouble, and warns against being afraid of the supernatural works of God.

title: Conference
summary: William Branham speaks on the importance of conferences with God, using biblical examples such as the Eden conference, the Burning Bush conference, the Red Sea conference, and the Gethsemane conference. He emphasizes that God calls people to reason together and make decisions based on His Word, and that true fellowship with God transforms believers.
themes: the danger of relying on creeds
the power of the Holy Spirit

title: Why?
summary: William Branham preaches on the question 'Why?' from Jeremiah 8:20-22, asking why people refuse God's remedy for sin despite His provision. He emphasizes that God has provided a balm in Gilead—the Holy Spirit and new birth—but many reject it due to fear of man or love of sin. Branham calls for repentance and holiness, warning that on Judgment Day God will ask 'Why?' to those who refused His salvation.

title: The Queen of the South
summary: William Branham speaks on the Queen of the South, using the biblical account to emphasize the importance of recognizing and receiving God's gifts. He contrasts the faith of the Queen of Sheba and the Ninevites with the unbelief of the Pharisees, and applies the lesson to the present day, urging believers to rally around the gift of the Holy Spirit.

title: It Wasn't So From The Beginning
subtitle: 60-1127M
summary: William Branham preaches on the importance of returning to the original Pentecostal experience, warning against hybrid religion that mixes human traditions with God's Word. He emphasizes that God's truth is found at the beginning, not in denominational creeds, and calls believers back to the power and signs of the early church.

title: The Patmos Vision
summary: William Branham begins a series on the Book of Revelation, discussing the five foolish virgins, the remnant, and the sealing of the Holy Spirit. He emphasizes the importance of revelation knowledge and the unity of God as revealed in Jesus Christ.

title: The Revelation of Jesus Christ
summary: William Branham introduces a series on the Seven Church Ages from the Book of Revelation, emphasizing the need for a revelation of Christ in the last days. He discusses the historical and spiritual significance of the church ages, the importance of returning to the Pentecostal experience, and the imminent return of Christ.

title: The Ephesian Church Age
summary: William Branham introduces a series on the seven church ages, beginning with the Ephesian church age. He emphasizes the importance of the Blood tag over denominational brands, and discusses the revelation of Jesus Christ as Almighty God. He outlines the seven church ages and their messengers, and begins to expound on the message to the church at Ephesus.

title: The Smyrnaean Church Age
summary: William Branham teaches on the second church age, Smyrna (A.D. 170-312), a persecuted church that wore the martyr's crown. He identifies Irenaeus as the messenger to this age, emphasizing his stand against organization and for the oneness of God. Branham warns against hybrid religion and urges faithfulness unto death, promising a crown of life to overcomers.

title: The Pergamean Church Age
summary: William Branham introduces the third church age, Pergamos, covering the period from 312 to 606 A.D. He discusses the rise of the Nicolaitane doctrine, the consolidation of church and state under Constantine, and the persecution of true believers. Branham highlights the life and miracles of Saint Martin as a faithful witness during this age, emphasizing the importance of holding fast to the original apostolic faith and the Word of God.

title: The Thyatirean Church Age
summary: William Branham discusses the fourth church age, Thyatira, known as the Dark Age (606-1520 AD). He identifies Columba as the star of this age, a man who rejected Roman doctrine and maintained Pentecostal signs. Branham draws parallels between Jezebel and the Catholic church, warning against spiritual fornication and organizational hierarchy.

title: The Sardisean Church Age
summary: William Branham introduces the fifth church age, Sardis, covering the Reformation period from 1520 to 1750. He discusses the messenger Martin Luther, the deadness of the church, and the remnant that escaped. He also reviews previous church ages and emphasizes the continuity of the Holy Spirit through all ages.

title: The Philadelphian Church Age
summary: William Branham discusses the sixth church age, the Philadelphian Church Age, which he identifies as the age of brotherly love and missionary work, lasting from 1750 to 1906. He highlights John Wesley as the messenger of this age and emphasizes the importance of demonstrating the Gospel through signs and wonders, not just through literature. Branham also shares personal missionary experiences in South Africa to illustrate the power of the Holy Spirit in converting souls.

title: The Laodicean Church Age
summary: William Branham concludes his series on the seven church ages with the Laodicean age, warning of apostasy and predicting the end of the age by 1977. He discusses the coming Elijah prophet who will restore the faith of the Pentecostal fathers and prepare the church for the Lord's return.

title: The Ten Virgins, And The Hundred And Forty-Four Thousand Jews
summary: William Branham discusses the end-time events, focusing on the parable of the ten virgins, the sealing of the 144,000 Jews, and the distinction between the Church and Israel. He emphasizes the need for the Holy Spirit baptism and warns against lukewarm Christianity.

title: The Uncertain Sound
summary: William Branham discusses the uncertainty of the times, drawing from 1 Corinthians 14:8 about the trumpet giving an uncertain sound. He contrasts worldly uncertainty with the certainty of God's Word and the coming of Christ, encouraging faith and preparation for the Rapture.

title: God's Wrapped Gift
summary: In this Christmas sermon, William Branham reflects on the humble birth of Jesus in Bethlehem, emphasizing that God's greatest gift was wrapped in swaddling cloth and laid in a manger. He contrasts the world's rejection of Christ then and now, noting that people refuse the gift because it does not come wrapped in their preferred creeds or societal expectations. Branham calls for a return to the simple, powerful truth of the Gospel and the Holy Spirit.

title: Revelation, Chapter Four Part I
summary: William Branham begins a New Year's Eve service by reflecting on the past year and pressing toward the high calling in Christ. He introduces the fourth chapter of Revelation, explaining that after the Church Age, a door opens in heaven and John is called up to see things to come. Branham emphasizes that Christ is the only door to salvation and warns against rejecting His message.

title: Revelation, Chapter Four Part II
summary: William Branham continues his series on Revelation chapter 4, discussing the voice of the trumpet, the throne in heaven, and the living creatures. He emphasizes trusting God's promises, using examples from Abraham, Noah, and John the Baptist, and contrasts worldly wisdom with God's wisdom.
themes: Contrast between worldly and divine wisdom

title: Revelation, Chapter Four Part III
summary: In this sermon, William Branham continues his exposition of Revelation chapter 4, focusing on the throne of God and the mercy seat. He emphasizes that the mercy seat becomes a judgment seat after the Church is raptured, and that only the Blood of Jesus Christ can appease God's wrath. He also shares testimonies of answered prayer and discusses the spiritual condition of the world and the Church in the last days.

title: Questions and Answers
summary: William Branham addresses a group of ministers, deacons, and trustees, answering questions about calling to ministry, speaking in tongues, and the fruit of the Spirit. He emphasizes that the evidence of the Holy Ghost is a Christ-like life, not tongues, and that God's call must be confirmed in one's heart.
themes: Fruit of the Spirit vs. gifts

title: The Messiah
summary: William Branham preaches on the meaning of 'Messiah' as the Anointed One and King, emphasizing that Jesus fulfilled all prophecies. He explains that believers, as 'Messiahettes,' are anointed with the same Spirit to perform signs and wonders, and calls the church to return to the Word and the power of the Holy Spirit.

title: Jesus Christ The Same Yesterday, Today, And Forever
summary: William Branham returns to Beaumont, Texas after twelve years, emphasizing the unchanging nature of Jesus Christ as the same yesterday, today, and forever. He discusses the importance of love, faith, and the Holy Spirit, and prepares to pray for the sick, affirming that healing and salvation were accomplished at Calvary.

title: Queen of Sheba
summary: William Branham preaches on the Queen of Sheba's journey to hear Solomon's wisdom as a type of the end-time generation seeking the sign of the resurrection. He contrasts the faith of those who hunger for God with the unbelief of a wicked and adulterous generation, emphasizing that the same Gospel that blinded the Jews now blinds the Gentiles, while the true Church rallies around the gift of the Holy Spirit.

title: Things That Wasn't So From The Beginning
subtitle: 61-0119M
summary: William Branham preaches on the importance of returning to the original Word of God, emphasizing that truth is found at the beginning. He criticizes denominations for perverting God's Word with creeds and traditions, and calls for a return to the Pentecostal experience and the power of the Holy Spirit as seen in the early church.

title: The Water Baptism
summary: William Branham uses the analogy of a rifle that must be perfectly zeroed to discuss the apparent contradiction between Matthew 28:19 (baptizing in the name of the Father, Son, and Holy Ghost) and Acts 2:38 (baptizing in the name of Jesus Christ). He argues that the Bible must be perfectly consistent and that the solution lies in understanding that Father, Son, and Holy Ghost are titles, not names, and that the one Name is Jesus. He emphasizes that spiritual revelation, not seminary teaching, is the key to understanding Scripture.

title: Mary's Belief
summary: William Branham preaches on Mary's encounter with the angel Gabriel, emphasizing her faith in God's Word despite the impossibility of a virgin birth. He draws parallels to the present day, urging believers to accept God's promises without requiring signs, and highlights the role of the Holy Spirit as God's messenger in the last days.

title: As The Eagle Stirs Her Nest
summary: William Branham uses the metaphor of an eagle to describe the Christian life, emphasizing the need to rise above worldly creeds and distractions through faith in God. He shares personal experiences observing eagles in nature, drawing parallels to spiritual truths about God's protection, the power of the Holy Spirit, and the importance of living a high and holy life. The sermon encourages believers to trust in God's provision and to soar above the limitations of denominationalism.
themes: Eagle as symbol of the believer

title: Be Not Afraid, It Is I
summary: William Branham preaches on the importance of simple faith in Jesus Christ, using the biblical account of Jesus walking on water and the disciples' fear. He shares testimonies of miraculous healings among Native Americans and emphasizes that Jesus is the same yesterday, today, and forever, and that believers should not be afraid but trust in Him.

title: Blind Bartimaeus
summary: William Branham preaches on the story of blind Bartimaeus, drawing parallels between physical blindness and spiritual blindness. He emphasizes the importance of faith, holding onto God's promises, and the need for love and compassion in the church.
themes: The Holy Spirit as God's representative

title: Why?
summary: William Branham delivers a farewell message in Beaumont, Texas, emphasizing love and unity among believers of different denominations. He shares a personal vision where God shows him the cost of sin and the power of forgiveness, leading him to repent of his judgmental attitude. He then preaches from Jeremiah 8:22, asking why people refuse God's provided way of escape through Jesus Christ.
themes: God's provision for healing and salvation

title: Why?
summary: William Branham preaches on the question 'Why?' from Jeremiah 8:22, asking why God's people are not recovered when there is balm in Gilead and a Physician. He uses the story of King Ahaziah and Elijah to illustrate that people reject God's remedy due to stubbornness and selfishness. Branham emphasizes the need for genuine new birth and the Holy Spirit, warning against substitutes and compromise.
themes: the power of the Holy Spirit

title: Turning Northward
summary: William Branham uses Deuteronomy 2:3 to call the church to move beyond denominational divisions and into the fullness of God's promise. He compares Israel's wilderness wanderings to the Pentecostal movement's forty-year stagnation, urging unity and a return to Spirit-led revival.
themes: the danger of adding to grace
the need for a new generation

title: Jesus Christ the Same Yesterday, Today, and Forever
summary: William Branham preaches on the unchanging nature of Jesus Christ, emphasizing that He is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He discusses divine healing as a finished work at Calvary, the importance of faith and confession, and the need for believers to see Jesus through the Holy Spirit's manifestation in the church.

title: Expectation
summary: William Branham speaks on the theme of expectation based on faith in God's promises, using examples from Abraham, Moses, and Simeon. He encourages believers to separate from unbelief and expect God to fulfill His Word, especially regarding healing and the Holy Spirit.

title: Expectation
summary: William Branham opens a revival series in Long Beach, emphasizing the need for genuine revival through prayer and full obedience to God. He uses biblical examples like Noah, Abraham, and Moses to illustrate the power of expectation based on God's Word, and encourages the congregation to prepare their hearts for healing and spiritual renewal.

title: Sirs, We Would See Jesus
summary: William Branham preaches on the need to see Jesus as He is today, the same yesterday, today, and forever. He contrasts the early Pentecostal church's faith with modern complacency, urging believers to recognize God's visitation and return to the Word and Spirit. He emphasizes that the Messiah's sign is a prophet who knows the secrets of the heart, as demonstrated when Jesus called Simon and Nathanael.
themes: Christ the same yesterday, today, and forever

title: JEHOVAH-JIREH
summary: William Branham preaches on the covenant God made with Abraham, emphasizing that it was unconditional and based on grace, not law. He contrasts Abraham's faith with the lukewarm state of the modern church, urging believers to separate from the world and fully trust God's promises.

title: Abraham's Covenant Confirmed
summary: William Branham continues his study in Genesis, focusing on Abraham's covenant with God. He contrasts the faith of Abraham with the lukewarm Laodicean church age, emphasizing the need for separation from the world and a return to original Pentecostal faith. He also discusses the coming of Elijah and the restoration of the church.

title: Abraham
summary: William Branham continues his series on Abraham, discussing the patriarch's faith and obedience to God. He emphasizes the importance of staying true to God's promises and warns against the dangers of worldliness and organization in the church. The sermon includes testimonies of healing and missionary work.
themes: the role of the Holy Spirit

title: IT IS I, BE NOT AFRAID
summary: William Branham preaches on the unchanging nature of Jesus Christ, emphasizing that He is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He encourages faith in Christ's finished work at Calvary for both salvation and healing, and demonstrates through Scripture how Jesus revealed Himself as Messiah through prophetic signs, which continue today through the Holy Spirit.
themes: Jesus Christ the same yesterday, today, and forever

title: Jehovah-Jireh
summary: William Branham shares personal anecdotes and teachings on faith, the Holy Spirit, and the story of Abraham offering Isaac. He emphasizes trusting God's provision and the importance of being led by the Spirit.
themes: the role of the Holy Spirit

title: And Thy Seed Shall Possess the Gate of His Enemies
summary: William Branham preaches on the promise to Abraham that his seed would possess the gate of his enemies, emphasizing that believers are Abraham's seed through Christ and must endure trials to receive the promise. He illustrates this with the story of the three Hebrew children in the fiery furnace and encourages steadfast faith.

title: The Basis of Fellowship
summary: William Branham speaks on the true basis of fellowship with God and one another, emphasizing that human efforts such as education, denominations, and science cannot restore fellowship. He stresses that only through the Blood of Jesus Christ can fellowship be achieved, using examples from the Bible and his own ministry experiences.
themes: the role of the Holy Spirit

title: Thou Son Of David, Have Mercy On Me
summary: William Branham preaches on the story of blind Bartimaeus, emphasizing faith as the sixth sense that defies the five physical senses. He encourages persistent faith and prayer, drawing parallels between Bartimaeus's hope and the believer's trust in God's unchanging power.

title: The Mark Of The Beast And The Seal Of God
summary: William Branham preaches on the biblical concepts of the Mark of the Beast and the Seal of God, tracing their origins from Genesis through Revelation. He argues that the Seal of God is the baptism of the Holy Ghost, while the mark of the beast is the rejection of it, and emphasizes that these two forces are at work in the world today.

title: The Mark of the Beast and the Seal of God 2
summary: William Branham continues his teaching on the Mark of the Beast and the Seal of God, emphasizing that the Seal of God is the Holy Spirit and the mark of the beast is rejection of the Holy Spirit. He traces this conflict from Cain and Abel through history, warning that in the last days, only those sealed with the Holy Spirit will escape God's judgment.

title: Balm in Gilead
summary: William Branham preaches on the question from Jeremiah 8:22, asking why God's people are not recovered if there is balm in Gilead and a physician there. He warns against rejecting God's provision, using examples from Israel's history and contemporary society, and calls the church to holiness and unity.
themes: holiness and separation from the world

title: The Queen of Sheba
summary: William Branham preaches on the Queen of Sheba's visit to Solomon as a type of the church seeking Christ. He contrasts the wisdom of Solomon with the greater wisdom of Christ, emphasizing that true faith comes by revelation and that the same signs and wonders that followed Christ should follow believers today.

title: Be Not Afraid
summary: William Branham preaches on the theme of fear versus faith, using the biblical account of Jesus walking on water and the disciples' testimony meeting in the boat. He emphasizes that Jesus is the same yesterday, today, and forever, and that the sign of the Messiah—discerning the thoughts of the heart—is still active today. Branham encourages the congregation to have faith and not be afraid, as God's presence is with them.

title: Jehovah-Jireh
summary: William Branham preaches on the covenant God made with Abraham, emphasizing that believers are Abraham's Seed through faith in Christ. He explains that God's promises are unconditional and that healing is already provided through Christ's sacrifice. Branham encourages the congregation to look to their Sacrifice rather than their own worthiness.

title: Beyond The Curtain Of Time
summary: William Branham shares a vision of the afterlife given to him by God, describing a place of perfect love, youth, and joy beyond the curtain of time. He encourages believers to press on in faith, love, and obedience to the Word, and to embrace divine healing through genuine faith in Christ's sacrifice.

title: Expectations
summary: William Branham opens a revival meeting in Virginia, explaining his approach to divine healing and the importance of faith in God's Word. He emphasizes that healing was accomplished at Calvary and must be accepted by faith, not feelings. He also outlines the logistics of prayer cards and the meeting schedule.

title: Be Not Afraid
summary: William Branham encourages believers not to fear, using the account of Jesus walking on water. He contrasts the early Pentecostal movement with modern Christianity, emphasizing the need for genuine faith and holiness. Branham also shares testimonies of healings and prophetic ministry, urging the church to prepare for Christ's soon return.

title: Jehovah-Jireh
summary: William Branham preaches on the compound redemptive name Jehovah-Jireh, 'the Lord will provide a sacrifice,' using Abraham's faith as a model for believers. He emphasizes that believers are Abraham's Seed through Christ and must possess Abraham's unwavering faith to claim God's promises, including healing. The sermon also recounts a debate on divine healing and the photographic evidence of the Angel of the Lord.
themes: photographic evidence of Angel of the Lord

title: An Uncertain Sound
summary: William Branham preaches on the uncertainty of the times, including national security, jobs, home life, politics, and the church. He emphasizes that only God's Word is certain and calls for a return to the true gospel and the experience of the Holy Ghost.
themes: the certain sound of the gospel

title: The Church Choosing Law For Grace
summary: William Branham preaches on the parallel between Israel's mistake of choosing law over grace and the Pentecostal church's similar error of organizing and adding works to grace. He warns that unbelief and reliance on human systems keep believers from entering the full promise of God.

title: Abraham's Grace Covenant
summary: William Branham preaches on the covenant God made with Abraham, emphasizing that it was a covenant of grace, not law, and that believers become Abraham's seed through the Holy Spirit. He contrasts faith with unbelief, warning against turning away from revealed truth, and applies the covenant to divine healing and the believer's security in Christ.

title: Abraham's Covenant Confirmed
summary: William Branham continues his series on Abraham, showing how God's covenant with Abraham and the signs given to him are mirrored in the Church age. He emphasizes that the last sign given to Abraham—the Angel revealing the thoughts of Sarah—is the same sign being manifested in the Church today, preceding the change of the body and the rapture.

title: Jezebel Religion
summary: William Branham preaches on the parallels between ancient Israel under Ahab and Jezebel and modern America, warning against spiritual decline, compromise with worldly systems, and the rise of a Jezebel-like religious spirit. He calls for a return to the pure Word of God and the power of the Holy Spirit.
themes: Return to the Word of God

title: The True Easter Seal
summary: William Branham delivers an Easter sermon on the true meaning of the Easter seal, contrasting it with worldly seals and offerings. He traces the conflict between Cain and Abel through history, showing how greed and rejection of God's provided way lead to persecution of the righteous. He emphasizes that Christ's resurrection is the ultimate seal of victory over sin and death, and calls for clean-cut decisions for God.

title: SIRS, WE WOULD SEE JESUS
summary: William Branham opens a revival campaign in Bloomington, Illinois, emphasizing that divine healing and salvation are based on faith in the finished work of Christ at Calvary. He argues that God is infinite and unchanging, and that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever, therefore the same signs and wonders should be seen today. Using the account of the Greeks who said 'Sirs, we would see Jesus,' he challenges believers to seek a living encounter with the risen Christ rather than mere historical knowledge.
themes: divine healing as part of the Gospel
the role of the Holy Spirit
the need for personal encounter with Jesus

title: Conferences
summary: William Branham speaks on the importance of conferences, drawing parallels between worldly conferences and divine conferences with God. He emphasizes the need for the church to come together, lay aside differences, and be inspired by the Holy Spirit, using the example of an eagle's faith and confidence in its wings to illustrate trusting in God's power.
themes: The eagle as a symbol of faith

title: But It Wasn't So From The Beginning
summary: William Branham speaks on the importance of returning to the original Pentecostal experience and warns against hybrid religion that mixes human traditions with God's Word. He uses the analogy of hybrid corn and mules to illustrate how perversion leads to sterility and death, urging believers to be pedigreed Christians tracing their lineage back to Pentecost.

title: A Greater Than Solomon Is Here
summary: William Branham speaks on the greatness of Christ compared to Solomon, using the Queen of Sheba's visit as a type. He shares testimonies of healing and revival in Africa, emphasizing that Jesus is the same yesterday, today, and forever, and that His works vindicate His Word.

title: Why?
summary: William Branham preaches on the importance of faith in God's Word for healing, explaining the nature of his prophetic gift and the role of the believer's faith. He addresses why many are not healed despite God's provision, using biblical examples and personal testimonies to encourage trust in God's promises.

title: Be Not Afraid, It Is I
summary: William Branham preaches on faith and divine healing, emphasizing that healing was accomplished at Calvary and is received by faith. He uses the biblical account of Jesus walking on water and the testimonies of the disciples to illustrate that Jesus is the same yesterday, today, and forever, and that His presence is manifested through spiritual gifts.

title: From That Time
summary: William Branham shares personal anecdotes and a sermon on the transformative power of encountering God. He emphasizes that true change comes from a divine encounter, not external reforms, and calls for unity and love among believers.

title: The Uncertain Sound
summary: William Branham preaches on the uncertainty of the world—in national security, jobs, politics, and the church—contrasting it with the certainty of God's Word. He shares a personal vision of Christ's intercession and urges believers to trust in the unchanging Word of God.

title: Abraham And His Seed After Him
summary: William Branham preaches on the Abrahamic covenant, emphasizing that God's promises to Abraham and his seed are unconditional and based on election. He calls believers to total separation from the world, warning that compromise hinders revival.

title: Abraham And His Seed After Him
summary: William Branham preaches on Galatians 3:29, explaining that believers in Christ are Abraham's seed and heirs according to the promise. He traces the parallels between God's dealings with Abraham and the Church, emphasizing election, grace, justification, sanctification, and the confirmation of the covenant through Christ's sacrifice.

title: The Greatest News Flash in History
summary: William Branham preaches on the resurrection of Jesus Christ as the greatest news flash in history, emphasizing that Christ appears only to His elected believers and that the church must move beyond dead creeds and organizations to experience the living Christ. He calls believers to 'come, see, and go tell' the message of the resurrected Lord.

title: The Godhead Explained
summary: William Branham addresses a gathering of ministers in Chicago, explaining his stance on the Godhead and the divisions among Pentecostal groups over water baptism and the Trinity. He advocates for unity and love among believers, emphasizing that both the Oneness and Trinitarian positions are wrong when they argue, and that the true focus should be on winning souls to Christ.

title: The Forgotten Beatitude
summary: William Branham preaches on Matthew 11:6, 'Blessed is he, whosoever shall not be offended in me,' calling it the forgotten beatitude. He uses the example of John the Baptist, who became discouraged in prison and doubted Jesus, to encourage believers not to be offended when God's ways don't match their expectations. Branham emphasizes that God is always on schedule and that the same works Jesus did are being repeated in the evening time.

title: Micaiah The Prophet
summary: William Branham preaches on the story of Micaiah the prophet from 1 Kings 22, emphasizing the importance of speaking only what God says regardless of popular opinion. He contrasts true prophets with those who compromise, and encourages believers to stay faithful to God's Word.

title: Only Believe
summary: William Branham preaches on the importance of faith, using the story of Jairus from Luke 8:50. He encourages believers to confess their faith openly, even when facing opposition, and emphasizes that God's power is available to meet every need.

title: Getting In The Spirit
summary: William Branham preaches on the need for the Church to return to the Holy Spirit, using the story of Elisha and the minstrel from 2 Kings 3:15. He laments that the Church has become dry and fruitless through organization and division, and calls for a revival of love, unity, and the genuine power of God.

title: One Of The Meanest Men In Town
summary: William Branham preaches on the story of Simon the Pharisee and the sinful woman who anointed Jesus' feet. He contrasts the cold, self-righteous welcome of the religious leader with the humble, tearful devotion of the outcast, urging listeners to truly welcome Jesus and not leave Him with 'dirty feet.'

title: The Uncertain Sound
summary: William Branham preaches on the uncertainty of the world—nations, jobs, homes, politics, and churches—contrasting it with the certainty of God's Word. He uses biblical examples like Noah, Moses, Elijah, and David to illustrate unwavering faith in God's promises, encouraging believers to trust God's Word despite worldly instability.

title: Super Sign
summary: William Branham preaches on the 'Super Sign' promised by God in Isaiah 7:14—a virgin conceiving and bearing a Son, Immanuel. He contrasts man's failed attempts at super achievements (towers, cities, ships, organizations) with God's eternal supernatural sign: God made flesh among His people. Branham emphasizes that the same supernatural signs of Christ's resurrection are available today through a supernatural people born of Abraham's faith.

title: A Greater Than Solomon Is Here
summary: William Branham speaks about the power of prayer, the gifts of the Spirit, and the importance of faith. He shares testimonies of healings and recounts his missionary experiences in Africa, emphasizing that true Christianity is demonstrated through the power of God, not just theology.

title: Jesus Christ The Same Yesterday, Today, And Forever
summary: William Branham preaches on the unchanging nature of Jesus Christ, emphasizing that Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He argues that divine healing and salvation are already accomplished through Christ's sacrifice, and that faith in God's Word is essential to receive these blessings. Branham uses the example of Nathanael's encounter with Jesus to illustrate how Christ reveals Himself as Messiah through supernatural knowledge.
themes: the Messianic sign of a prophet

title: God's Provided Way
subtitle: 61-0516M
summary: William Branham speaks on God's provided way for salvation and healing, contrasting man's failed attempts at achievement through science and human effort with God's perfect provision in Jesus Christ. He emphasizes that faith in God's Word and acceptance of Christ's finished work at Calvary is the only way to receive God's blessings.

title: IT IS I
summary: William Branham speaks on the importance of simple childlike faith and the power of prayer. He recounts the testimonies of the apostles, emphasizing that Jesus is the same yesterday, today, and forever, and that His presence is with believers today.
themes: Jesus as the same yesterday, today, and forever

title: SIRS, WE WOULD SEE JESUS
summary: William Branham speaks on the desire to see Jesus, emphasizing that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He discusses the role of divine healing as a sign of Christ's presence and the importance of faith over education or tradition in recognizing Him.

title: From That Time
summary: William Branham speaks on the phrase 'from that time,' illustrating how pivotal moments—whether sinful or redemptive—change a person's life. He shares personal anecdotes and biblical examples, emphasizing that meeting God transforms a person forever.

title: Show Us The Father
summary: William Branham speaks on the human cry to see God, using the account of Philip in John 14:8. He explores four ways to see God: in His universe, in His Word, in His Son, and in His people. He emphasizes that God is present and can be seen through nature, faith, and the indwelling Holy Spirit.

title: Revelation, Chapter Five Part I
summary: William Branham announces his departure from the ministry due to some followers falsely claiming he is the Messiah, which he denounces as a lie of the devil. He then continues his sermon series on Revelation, focusing on the seven-sealed book and the mercy seat guarded by the four living creatures, emphasizing the earnest of the Holy Spirit as the seal of believers' adoption.

title: Revelation, Chapter Five Part II
summary: William Branham discusses recent events, including a fulfilled vision and a doctrinal controversy that was resolved. He emphasizes staying true to the Word of God, warns against false spiritual gifts, and introduces the theme of redemption through the Lamb as a Kinsman Redeemer, using the story of Ruth and Boaz as an illustration.

title: God Being Misunderstood
summary: William Branham addresses questions from the congregation on topics including baptism, the Godhead, tithing, spiritual gifts, and biblical prophecy. He emphasizes the importance of reverence in church, correct baptismal formula, and discerning the Holy Spirit's work without judging individuals.

title: The Ever-Present Water From The Rock
summary: William Branham shares a personal dream and his struggle with God's leading regarding his ministry location. He then teaches from Exodus 17, using the rock struck by Moses as a type of Christ, emphasizing that the Holy Spirit (the water) follows believers continually, just as the rock followed Israel.

title: The Sixfold Purpose of Gabriel's Visit to Daniel
summary: William Branham continues his series on Daniel, focusing on the sixfold purpose of Gabriel's visit to Daniel as recorded in Daniel 9:24. He explains each purpose: to finish transgression, make an end of sins, make reconciliation for iniquity, bring in everlasting righteousness, seal up vision and prophecy, and anoint the Most Holy. Branham connects these purposes to the future restoration of Israel and the second coming of Christ.

title: Gabriel's Instructions to Daniel
summary: William Branham begins a study on Daniel's Seventy Weeks, explaining its connection to the Book of Revelation and the end times. He emphasizes the need for prayer and understanding as the Church approaches the final week of Daniel's prophecy.

title: The Seventieth Week of Daniel
summary: William Branham explains the prophecy of Daniel's seventy weeks, demonstrating how it applies to the Jewish people and reveals the timeline of the Messiah's coming. He emphasizes that the Jews are God's timepiece and that the Church age is separate from the prophetic weeks. Branham concludes that the prophecy precisely points to Jesus Christ as the Messiah.

title: Thy House
summary: William Branham speaks on the promise that believing on the Lord Jesus Christ brings salvation to one's household, using the examples of the Philippian jailer and Job. He encourages faith for family members and emphasizes that God honors the faith of parents for their children.

title: Faith
summary: William Branham teaches that the power of God resides within every believer through the Holy Spirit, and that faith is the law that activates that power for salvation, healing, and all needs. He uses the examples of Jesus' resurrection, Abraham's faith, and the Philippian jailer to illustrate that faith in God's promises brings forth what is already within. He also addresses a Catholic convert and warns against organizational formalism.

title: The Message of Grace
summary: William Branham shares a personal experience of seeing three rainbows in a field, confirming his message that Jesus is Jehovah of the Old Testament. He then preaches on grace, using Zechariah 4 to emphasize that salvation is not by might or power but by God's Spirit, and that grace has been God's plan from Eden onward.

title: Let Your Light So Shine Before Men
summary: William Branham speaks on the importance of Christians being living examples of Christ, using the metaphor of a billboard to illustrate how believers should attract others to God through their actions. He emphasizes that the world sees Christ through believers, and that a genuine Christian life will make others hunger for righteousness.

title: The Comforter
summary: William Branham speaks on the Holy Spirit as the Comforter, emphasizing that the Word of God is our comfort and heritage. He draws examples from Noah, Job, and Abraham to illustrate unwavering faith in God's promises, even in times of trial and suffering.

title: It Becometh Us to Fulfil All Righteousness
summary: William Branham, facing his mother's imminent death, preaches on the necessity of fulfilling all righteousness as exemplified by Jesus' baptism. He shares personal testimonies of visions and healings to demonstrate God's faithfulness, urging believers to stand firm on God's Word despite criticism.

title: Respects
summary: William Branham speaks on the importance of giving respect and reverence to God and His messengers. He uses biblical examples such as Noah, Moses, and Elijah to illustrate how God demands respect and how disrespect leads to judgment. He encourages believers to honor God's Word and His anointed servants.
themes: Fear of God as beginning of wisdom
God's mercy and way of escape
Vindication of God's servants through signs

title: Questions and Answers
summary: William Branham answers questions from the congregation on topics including water baptism in Jesus' name, the interpretation of Hebrews 6:4-6 and 10:26-39, the meaning of Jesus' command to 'feed my sheep,' and whether being slain in the Spirit is a sign of a husband's salvation. He emphasizes the importance of following Scripture and warns against rejecting further light from God.
themes: the promised land as type of Holy Spirit baptism

title: The Testimony of a True Witness
summary: William Branham shares his gratitude for the congregation's support during his mother's illness and death, describing a vision where he saw her restored to youth. He emphasizes the certainty of the Christian faith through the testimony of nature, Scripture, and personal experience, urging believers to be true witnesses of Christ's resurrection.

title: A True Sign That's Overlooked
summary: William Branham preaches on how God uses prophets as signs to a generation, but these signs are often overlooked. He draws parallels from Noah, Moses, Ezekiel, and Elijah to show that true prophets are rejected by the world but are God's deliverance for His people.

title: Perfect Strength By Perfect Weakness
summary: William Branham preaches on the paradox that God's strength is made perfect in human weakness, using Paul's testimony in 2 Corinthians 12:9 as the text. He emphasizes that believers must surrender their own abilities, education, and strengths to become vessels God can use, drawing examples from biblical heroes like Paul and the apostles.
themes: human weakness as a prerequisite for divine strength
surrender of self and abilities to God
God's choice of the weak and rejected
dependence on God rather than human wisdom or education
the danger of relying on denominational strength
the need for a 'killing' of self before revival

title: Paradox
summary: William Branham discusses the concept of paradox as something incredible but true, using examples from nature and Scripture. He shares a vision of a deadly mamba snake and emphasizes the need for sincerity in faith. The sermon culminates in the account of Joshua commanding the sun to stand still, illustrating God's power over creation.

title: Christianity Versus Idolatry
summary: William Branham contrasts true Christianity with idolatry, tracing its origins from pagan Rome to modern practices. He warns against false spirits and emphasizes the importance of adhering to Scripture, using examples from history and his own ministry.

title: Sirs, We Would See Jesus
summary: In this Christmas message, William Branham contrasts the true meaning of Christmas with its modern commercialization and pagan traditions. He emphasizes that to truly see Jesus, one must die to self and be crucified with Christ, pointing to the cross rather than to celebrations or church affiliations.
themes: The Cross as the Way to See Jesus

title: If God Be With Us, Then Where Is All The Miracles?
summary: William Branham preaches on the need for God's people to return to the Word and experience His miracles. Using the story of Gideon, he challenges the church to move beyond denominational barriers and doubt to see God's supernatural power manifested today.
themes: the baptism of the Holy Spirit

title: You Must Be Born Again
summary: William Branham teaches on the necessity of the new birth, emphasizing that it is a spiritual experience beyond church membership or creed recitation. He uses the conversation between Jesus and Nicodemus to explain that being born again is essential to see and enter the Kingdom of God.
themes: the role of the Holy Spirit

title: Presuming
summary: William Branham warns against presuming upon God's grace without actual biblical authority. Using the example of Israel at Kadesh-barnea and Samson, he urges believers to fully obey God's Word rather than relying on past experiences or denominational creeds.
themes: The danger of relying on past experiences
Need for holiness and separation from the world

title: Convinced Then Concerned
summary: William Branham preaches on the importance of being convinced of the truth of the Gospel before becoming concerned for others. Using John the Baptist as an example, he emphasizes the need to stay with Jesus long enough to be absolutely sure, which then produces a burden for the lost. He contrasts this with the lack of concern in modern churches and calls for a return to holiness.
themes: John the Baptist as a model
the need for personal assurance of salvation
the failure of modern religious systems
holiness and separation from the world
the urgency of the last days

title: An Ensign
summary: William Branham speaks on the concept of an 'ensign' as a God-given sign or authority for believers. He contrasts man's failed attempts to save himself through science, education, and human achievement with God's provision of faith and the cross of Christ as the ultimate ensign. Branham encourages the congregation to hold fast to the authority Christ has given His Church.
themes: The cross as the ultimate ensign
Contrast between human achievement and divine provision

title: The Unchangeable God Working In An Unexpectable Way
summary: William Branham preaches on the unchanging nature of God, who works in unexpected ways, times, and places. Using biblical examples like Moses, Jacob, and the birth of Jesus, he encourages believers to hold fast to God's promises despite opposition or unexpected circumstances.

title: The Marriage of the Lamb
summary: William Branham speaks on the marriage of the Lamb, using the analogy of earthly marriage to describe the relationship between Christ and His Church. He emphasizes the need for a genuine connection with Christ through the Holy Spirit, not just an artificial profession of faith.

title: And Thy Seed Shall Possess The Gate Of His Enemy
summary: William Branham preaches on the promise to Abraham that his seed would possess the gate of his enemy, emphasizing that this promise applies to spiritual seed—those who are born of the Spirit. He contrasts true faith in God's Word with reliance on organizations, and stresses the need for testing and separation from the world.

title: Confirmation Of The Commission
summary: William Branham speaks on the necessity of divine confirmation for those commissioned by God, using the analogy of a U.S. marshal's credentials. He emphasizes that true believers will have signs following them as promised in Mark 16 and John 14:12, contrasting this with mere human credentials or denominational affiliations.

title: Forsaking All
summary: William Branham preaches on the necessity of forsaking all to follow Christ, using examples from Scripture such as Abraham, Israel, and the disciples. He emphasizes that God rewards those who leave behind worldly possessions, relationships, and traditions to obey His Word.

title: Have Not I Sent Thee?
summary: William Branham preaches on the need for God's people to return to His Word and experience His miracles, using the story of Gideon as an example. He emphasizes that God sends prophets to call His people back, and that true faith is demonstrated by God confirming His Word with signs and wonders.

title: The Meanest Man I Know
summary: William Branham speaks at a Full Gospel Business Men's Fellowship breakfast, sharing personal experiences of visions and healings, and then preaches on the Pharisee who invited Jesus to dinner, contrasting the world's ways with the humility of Christ.

title: A Paradox
summary: William Branham preaches on the theme of paradox, using biblical examples such as Joshua commanding the sun to stand still, Noah building the ark, Abraham and Isaac, David and Goliath, and Moses leading Israel. He emphasizes that God works in incredible but true ways, and that believers must hold fast to God's Word to see His paradoxical power manifest.

title: Unbelief Does Not Hinder God
summary: William Branham preaches on Romans 3:3, arguing that unbelief does not hinder God's plans but only destroys the unbeliever. He contrasts faith and unbelief, using biblical examples like Noah and Jesus, and encourages believers to stay rooted in God's Word.
themes: the baptism of the Holy Spirit

title: Explaining The Ministry
summary: William Branham explains his ministry and the operation of spiritual gifts, emphasizing that God's Word is the ultimate authority and that the same Holy Spirit that worked in biblical times works today. He shares personal testimonies of visions and healings, and calls the congregation to faith in Jesus Christ.

title: Communion
summary: William Branham shares experiences from a recent convention in Arizona, emphasizing the need for genuine communion with God through the Holy Spirit rather than mere ritual. He explains that true communion is a two-way conversation with God, and the bread and wine are only memorials of Christ's sacrifice.

title: Oneness
summary: William Branham preaches on the theme of oneness with God, emphasizing that true fellowship requires believing every word of Scripture. He uses Adam and Eve's fall as a warning that doubting even one word breaks union with God, and calls the church to reject man-made creeds and hold fast to God's Word.

title: Perseverance
summary: William Branham preaches on the importance of perseverance in faith, using the example of the Canaanite woman from Matthew 15. He emphasizes that true faith is persistent, rooted in God's Word, and does not mix with unbelief. Branham encourages believers to hold fast to God's promises despite circumstances, as God is the same yesterday, today, and forever.
themes: The Word of God as seed
The Holy Spirit in the Church

title: The Greatest Battle Ever Fought
summary: William Branham announces a forthcoming message on the greatest battle ever fought, drawing from 1 Peter 5:8-10, Ephesians 6:10-17, and Daniel 12:1-14. He explains that the battleground is the human mind, where decisions are made between faith and doubt, and emphasizes the need to clear all channels to let God's Word take root.

title: Expressions
summary: A funeral sermon for Sister Bell, using nature's cycles—trees, flowers, and the sun—as expressions of God's promise of resurrection. Branham comforts the family by affirming that death is not the end but a transition to eternal life, as demonstrated by Christ's resurrection.

title: The Spoken Word Is The Original Seed 1
summary: William Branham begins a series explaining his ministry and beliefs, emphasizing that the spoken Word of God is the original seed that cannot be hybridized. He argues that the Bible is the infallible Word of God, that it does not contradict itself, and that adding to or taking from it brings judgment. He traces the pattern of hybridization from Eve to modern denominations, asserting that true life comes only from the original seed.
themes: The Word of God is eternal and cannot be changed
Each generation has its own revival
The Bible is the only standard for judgment
Faith must rest on the Word alone

title: The End-Time Sign Seed
summary: William Branham preaches on the end-time sign seed, emphasizing that God's Word is the original seed that cannot be hybridized with human creeds or doctrines. He uses examples from nature and Scripture to show that God reveals His secrets to prophets and that believers must accept the Word without doubt to bring forth life.
themes: The Word of God as seed
Faith and acceptance of God's Word

title: Wisdom Versus Faith
summary: William Branham teaches on the two sources of life: wisdom and faith. He traces wisdom back to Satan's deception in the Garden of Eden, where he offered Eve knowledge contrary to God's Word, while faith comes from God and requires believing His Word without reasoning. Branham emphasizes that believers must reject human reasoning and hold fast to God's Word, as faith alone leads to eternal life.
themes: the Word of God as final authority

title: The Signs Of His Coming
summary: William Branham speaks on the signs of Christ's coming, emphasizing that God always gives signs before judgment. He contrasts the dismay of unbelievers with the encouragement believers receive from these signs, and stresses the importance of staying true to God's Word.

title: Presuming
summary: William Branham teaches on the danger of presuming in spiritual matters, using the Old Testament account of Israel at Kadesh-barnea as a warning. He contrasts faith in God's Word with human reasoning and presumption, emphasizing that unbelief is the root of sin. Branham calls believers to stand alone on the Word, fight for every promise, and reject denominational creeds that contradict Scripture.

title: The Restoration of the Bride Tree
summary: William Branham speaks on Easter Sunday about the concept of restoration, using Joel 2:25 and Genesis 20:7 as texts. He explains that believers have the legal right to enforce God's promises against Satan, restoring what was lost through sin, sickness, and death. The sermon emphasizes the power of the Holy Spirit to bring restoration and resurrection.

title: Possessing All Things
summary: William Branham shares a testimony of surviving a rifle accident, then preaches on the believer's inheritance as heirs of all things through Christ, using Abraham's victory over the kings and his meeting with Melchizedek as a type. He encourages believers to claim God's promises by faith and fight the enemy for what is rightfully theirs.

title: Letting Off The Pressure
summary: William Branham preaches on the pressures of modern life and the spiritual refuge found in Jesus Christ. Using the Old Testament cities of refuge as a type, he explains that Christ is the place where believers can release their burdens and find safety. He encourages the congregation to cast their cares on God and trust in His promises.
themes: Pressure and tension in modern life
Christ as the city of refuge
The blood of Christ as protection

title: The Way of a True Prophet of God
summary: William Branham discusses the characteristics of a true prophet, using the example of Amos from the Bible. He contrasts the prophet's reliance on 'Thus Saith the Lord' with modern religious systems that depend on human credentials and organization. Branham emphasizes that a true prophet is sent by God, fearless in delivering God's Word, and often rejected by the established religious order.

title: Letting Off The Pressure
summary: William Branham speaks on the pressures of modern life and the refuge found in God. Using the Old Testament cities of refuge as a type, he explains that Christ is our refuge where we can let off pressure. He encourages believers to trust in God's promises and find safety in His presence.

title: Fellowship
summary: William Branham speaks on the true basis of Christian fellowship, emphasizing that it can only be found under the shed blood of Jesus Christ, not through denominations, education, or human efforts. He uses biblical examples like Job and Israel to illustrate that fellowship requires coming under the blood and aligning with God's Word.
themes: The Word of God as the standard
The red heifer as a type of Christ

title: Perseverance
summary: William Branham preaches on the theme of perseverance, using biblical examples such as Noah, Moses, David, Samson, John the Baptist, and the Syrophoenician woman to illustrate how faith in God's Word enables believers to persist despite obstacles. He encourages Christians to remain steadfast in their faith, trusting in God's promises and the evidence of the Holy Spirit.

title: Convinced And Then Concerned
summary: William Branham speaks about the need to be convinced of the truth of the Gospel before becoming concerned for others. He uses biblical examples like John the Baptist, Andrew, Jacob, and Shamgar to illustrate how conviction leads to action, especially in missionary work.

title: Questions and Answers
summary: William Branham answers questions from the congregation on topics including remarriage after divorce, the resurrection body of the wicked, the meaning of conjunctions in Genesis regarding Eve's conception, and restoration for a backslidden believer. He emphasizes scriptural consistency and the assurance of salvation through Christ.

title: The Conflict Between God and Satan
summary: William Branham preaches on the conflict between God and Satan, emphasizing that God equipped His children with the Word as the ultimate weapon against the enemy. He uses the examples of Eve's fall and the days of Noah to illustrate how human reasoning leads to defeat, while faith in God's Word brings victory.

title: Taking Sides With Jesus
summary: William Branham addresses a gathering of ministers, sharing his heart about the church's position and his own ministry. He discusses the early church model, the need for faithful leadership, and his uncertainty about the future direction of his calling—whether as an evangelist or prophet. He encourages the brethren to remain steadfast and continue building for God's kingdom.
themes: The role of the prophet vs evangelist

title: The End-Time Evangelism
summary: William Branham preaches on the urgency of end-time evangelism, emphasizing that the last commission of Christ to preach the Gospel with signs following is for all believers. He contrasts the world's nervous anticipation of destruction with the Christian's hope in Christ's appearing, and calls for a return to the pure Word of God without denominational additions.
themes: the appearing and coming of Christ
the Word of God as final authority
moral decay in the last days
the role of the Holy Spirit

title: Putting On The Whole Armor Of God
summary: William Branham preaches on Ephesians 6:10-18, emphasizing the need for Christians to put on the whole armor of God to stand against the wiles of the devil. He contrasts the ever-changing weapons of earthly warfare with the unchanging, perfect Word of God, which is the believer's ultimate defense. Branham warns against Satan's tactics of reasoning and misinterpreting Scripture, urging believers to stay fortified behind God's Word.

title: Perseverance
summary: William Branham preaches on the theme of perseverance, using the story of the Syrophoenician woman (Matthew 15:21-28) as a central example. He emphasizes that true faith must be based on God's Word and persist through all barriers—race, criticism, ministerial opposition, and even apparent rejection by Christ. Branham encourages believers to press past the 'sound barrier' of doubt to receive God's promises.

title: Show Us The Father And It Will Sufficeth Us
subtitle: 62-0609B
summary: William Branham shares a testimony about leading an infidel to Christ by pointing to the intelligence in nature, such as the sap retreating to the roots of a tree. He emphasizes that God's life is evident all around us, and that true fellowship in Christ is the closest thing to heaven on earth.

title: Letting Off The Pressure
summary: William Branham speaks on the pressures of modern life and the refuge found in Christ. Using biblical examples like the cities of refuge and the Passover, he encourages believers to find safety and peace in the Lord, letting go of worldly anxieties.

title: Convinced Then Concerned
summary: William Branham preaches on the need to be convinced of the truth before being concerned for others. He uses the examples of John the Baptist, Andrew, Jacob, and Shamgar to illustrate how conviction leads to action, and laments the lack of concern in the current age due to a lack of conviction.

title: Presuming
summary: William Branham shares personal testimonies of visions and healings, then teaches from Numbers 14:41-45 on the danger of presuming without God's authority. He warns against taking God's will for granted and emphasizes the need for genuine faith and obedience.

title: IT IS I, BE NOT AFRAID
Behold, A Greater Than Solomon Is Here
summary: William Branham preaches on the sign of Jonah and the wisdom of Solomon, emphasizing that Jesus is greater than both. He encourages believers to look to God's promises rather than symptoms, and warns against rejecting the signs of God's presence in the last days.

title: Be Not Afraid
summary: William Branham opens a West Coast campaign in Los Angeles, expressing gratitude for fellowship and recounting a recent gun accident that nearly killed him. He uses the biblical account of Jesus walking on water to encourage believers to be of good cheer and not afraid, emphasizing the importance of being convinced of Christ's divinity and the power of testimony.

title: The Path of Life
summary: William Branham speaks at a Jewish synagogue, expressing his appreciation for the Jewish people and his belief that the Gentile Church will eventually take the message to the Jews. He discusses his ministry, the importance of unity among brethren, and the need for the Holy Spirit in the Church. He emphasizes that true life comes from God and that only those with God's own life (Zoe) can have eternal life.

title: Confirmation And Evidence
summary: William Branham preaches on the importance of confirmation and evidence in faith, using biblical examples like Abraham and the Israelites to illustrate how God confirms His promises. He emphasizes that faith is a substance, not just hope, and that the Holy Spirit is the evidence of Christ's resurrection. The sermon includes a prayer line where Branham demonstrates the gift of discernment.

title: Letting Off The Pressure
subtitle: 62-0622B
summary: William Branham speaks at Clifton's Cafeteria in Los Angeles, sharing testimonies of healing and encouraging believers to release the pressures of life by finding refuge in Christ, the Rock in a weary land. He uses the analogy of an eagle renewing its strength by beating its head against a rock to illustrate how believers can beat off unbelief and find new life in God.
themes: the Rock in a weary land

title: WHY?
summary: William Branham preaches on the question 'Why?' when God provides a way of escape and people refuse it. He uses the story of Ahaziah and Elijah to illustrate how people reject God's remedy and seek worldly alternatives, and calls the church to return to the Holy Ghost and the Word.

title: Perseverant
summary: William Branham preaches on the theme of perseverance, using biblical examples such as Noah, Moses, David, Samson, and John the Baptist to illustrate the importance of holding fast to God's Word despite opposition and delay. He emphasizes that true faith requires persistence, being sealed by the Holy Spirit, and waiting on God's timing.
themes: the Ark as type of the Church

title: Super Sign
summary: William Branham speaks on the theme of 'super' in the modern world, contrasting human attempts at greatness with God's super sign: the virgin birth of Christ. He emphasizes that Christ is the eternal, supernatural sign, and that believers, as Abraham's spiritual seed, share in His victory over all enemies.

title: We Would See Jesus
summary: William Branham opens his first meeting in Santa Maria, expressing gratitude for the fellowship and weather. He emphasizes the need to see Jesus as He is revealed in Scripture, noting that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever. Using the example of Nathanael, he explains that Jesus reveals Himself through prophetic knowledge, and that the same works should be expected today.

title: A Greater Than Solomon Is Here
summary: William Branham preaches on the sign of Jonah and the resurrection, contrasting the faith of Abraham and Jonah with the unbelief of the Pharisees. He emphasizes that the same Messianic signs are present today, and that believers must look to God's promises rather than symptoms.

title: Be Not Afraid, It Is I
summary: William Branham encourages believers to trust in Christ's presence and promises, sharing testimonies of healing and divine provision. He emphasizes faith over fear, using the biblical account of Jesus walking on water to illustrate that Christ is with His people in every storm.

title: It Wasn't So From The Beginning
summary: William Branham discusses the nature of visions and spiritual gifts, using biblical examples like Jesus and Lazarus to illustrate how God works through believers. He emphasizes that true ministry comes from yielding to the Holy Spirit, not human intellect, and warns against counterfeit spiritual experiences.
themes: the role of the Holy Spirit

title: The Meanest Man In Santa Maria
summary: William Branham shares testimonies of healings from his early ministry in Arkansas, then preaches on Luke 7:36-50, focusing on the Pharisee's invitation to Jesus and the contrast between the Pharisee's lack of hospitality and the sinful woman's devotion. He emphasizes the need for spiritual preparation and warns against inviting Christ but ignoring Him.

title: To Take On The Whole Armor Of God
summary: William Branham preaches on the spiritual armor of God from Ephesians 6, emphasizing that the Word of God is the believer's ultimate weapon against Satan's tactics of reasoning and deception. He contrasts the ever-changing weapons of earthly armies with the unchanging, perfect Word, and warns against intellectualism and false religion that undermine faith.
themes: the Word of God as armor

title: We Would See Jesus
summary: William Branham opens a five-day campaign in Grass Valley, emphasizing that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He uses the story of the Greeks seeking Jesus and the calling of Nathanael to illustrate that Christ is revealed through the Word and through prophetic discernment, not through creeds or denominations.
themes: Jesus Christ the same yesterday, today, and forever
The Word of God as the standard
Divine healing as a sign of Christ's presence
Rejection of creeds that nullify God's Word

title: Jehovah-Jireh
summary: William Branham preaches on the Abrahamic covenant and the faith of Abraham, emphasizing that believers are Abraham's seed through Christ and must hold fast to God's Word without wavering. He contrasts true faith with emotionalism and denominationalism, calling for complete separation from unbelief and worldly systems.

title: Jehovah-Jireh 2
summary: William Branham continues his series on Abraham, focusing on God's covenant with Abraham and the significance of El Shaddai. He emphasizes the importance of holding fast to God's Word despite circumstances, and contrasts the faith of Abraham with the perversion of the last days. Branham also discusses the restoration of the Bride tree and the need for the Church to return to the pure Word.

title: Jehovah-Jireh 3
summary: William Branham continues his series on Abraham, emphasizing the importance of obeying God's Word without reasoning. He contrasts the faith of Abraham with the disobedience of Lot's wife and Eve, and discusses the covenant God made with Abraham and its fulfillment in Christ. Branham also shares testimonies of healing and the work of the Holy Spirit in the meetings.

title: A Super Sign
summary: William Branham concludes a five-day campaign in Grass Valley, expressing gratitude and love for the congregation. He emphasizes the need for a super sign from God, contrasting human attempts at greatness with God's humble sign of a virgin conceiving Emmanuel. He calls for unity among believers and warns against relying on human achievements.

title: Hear Ye Him
summary: William Branham opens a revival in Spokane, emphasizing the authority of God's Word and the need to hear Christ alone. He shares testimonies of healing from his overseas ministry and calls believers to die to self and be born again, using the Transfiguration account to highlight that Jesus is God manifested in flesh.

title: We Would See Jesus
summary: William Branham preaches on the unchanging nature of Jesus Christ, emphasizing that He is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He discusses faith, divine healing, and the importance of believing God's Word, using Scripture to show that Jesus' works testify of His identity.

title: From That Time
summary: William Branham preaches on the importance of recognizing God's moving in the present, using the example of Israel following the Pillar of Fire. He discusses the need for the Church to remain open to the Holy Spirit beyond denominational boundaries, and emphasizes that true Pentecost is an experience, not an organization. He also shares personal testimonies and reflections on the assurance of resurrection and the authority believers have in Christ.

title: The Uncertain Sound
summary: William Branham preaches on the theme of uncertainty in the world, using 1 Corinthians 14:8 as a text. He shares personal testimonies of divine guidance and healing, emphasizing that anything uncertain cannot be trusted and that believers must be certain in their faith and actions.

title: Behold, A Greater Than All Of Them Is Here
summary: William Branham preaches on the need to recognize Christ's presence and works, rebuking a generation that fails to see the greater One among them. He emphasizes that true faith is built on the Word and the Spirit's manifestation, and warns against being caged by tradition and organization.

title: Jesus Christ The Same Yesterday, Today, And For Ever
summary: William Branham opens a series of meetings in Salem, Oregon, emphasizing the unchanging nature of Jesus Christ as the same yesterday, today, and forever. He calls for unity among believers, stresses the importance of the Word of God, and explains that divine healing and salvation are already accomplished through Christ's sacrifice, to be received by faith.
themes: Divine healing as a redemptive blessing

title: Life
summary: William Branham shares personal anecdotes and reflections on unity among Christians, the dangers of rigid organization, and the importance of fellowship. He emphasizes that God is a God of variety and that believers should work together despite differences. The sermon concludes with a meditation on eternal life through Christ.

title: Perseverant
summary: William Branham preaches on the importance of being perseverant in faith, using biblical examples like the Canaanite woman, Noah, Moses, David, and Samson. He emphasizes that true perseverance comes from hearing God's Word and holding onto His promises despite opposition or delay.

title: A Testimony On The Sea
summary: William Branham preaches on the importance of character and faith, using the biblical account of Jesus walking on water to illustrate that believers must trust in the resurrected Christ. He emphasizes that outward expressions of faith must align with the Word of God, and that the Holy Spirit seeks character in the Bride of Christ.

title: Behold, A Greater Than Solomon Is Here
summary: William Branham contrasts the faith of the Queen of Sheba and the Ninevites with the unbelief of his generation, emphasizing that the sign of the resurrection is given to an adulterous generation. He urges believers to look to Christ rather than symptoms, and warns against rejecting the Holy Spirit's gifts.

title: Show Us The Father And It Will Suffice Us
summary: William Branham preaches on the desire of the human heart to see God, using the text John 14:8 where Philip asks Jesus to show them the Father. He explores four ways to see God: in His universe, in His Word, in His Son, and in His people. Branham illustrates God's presence in nature through personal anecdotes and calls believers to trust in the Holy Ghost as instinctively as animals trust their God-given instincts.

title: Sir, We Would See Jesus
summary: William Branham shares testimonies of ministering to Native American tribes, emphasizing simple faith and the unchanging nature of Jesus Christ. He calls believers to see Jesus through the same works He did yesterday, today, and forever, and prepares the congregation for a healing service.

title: A Greater Than Solomon Is Here
summary: William Branham preaches on recognizing God's gifts and signs, using the biblical text of Matthew 12:41-42 to contrast the faith of the Queen of Sheba and the Ninevites with the unbelief of Jesus' generation. He emphasizes that Jesus is greater than Solomon and Jonah, and calls believers to simple faith in the resurrected Christ for healing and salvation.
themes: Gifts and offices in the Church

title: A Testimony Upon The Sea
summary: William Branham preaches on the testimony of the disciples after Jesus fed the five thousand, using the account of Peter walking on water as a metaphor for faith. He encourages believers to trust in God's Word and maintain their healing despite temporary setbacks.

title: We Would See Jesus
summary: William Branham speaks on the desire to see Jesus, emphasizing that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He encourages believers to look beyond outward appearances and seek the anointed Christ, who is the Word made flesh. Branham stresses the importance of faith in God's Word and the simplicity of the Gospel.
themes: Jesus Christ the same yesterday, today, and forever

title: God Has A Provided Way
summary: William Branham preaches on God's provided way for humanity to escape judgment and find salvation. Using examples from nature and Scripture, he emphasizes that God always provides a way, and man must walk in it by faith and obedience to His Word.

title: Perseverant
summary: William Branham preaches on the importance of perseverance in faith, using the story of the Canaanite woman and Abraham as examples. He emphasizes that true faith is a substance that holds onto God's promises despite circumstances, and encourages believers to be persistent in their trust in God's Word.

title: Present Stage of My Ministry
