summary: William Branham reflects on his ministry, recounting a vision from thirty years ago and its fulfillment. He discusses the separation that comes with standing true to the Word, using Paul and Demas as an example, and explains the different dimensions of existence after death.

title: In His Presence
summary: William Branham preaches on the profound effect of coming into the presence of God, using biblical examples like Isaiah, Moses, and Paul to show how holy men recognized their sinfulness. He emphasizes that encountering God transforms a person, leading to confession, cleansing, and a responsibility to share the message with others.

title: Countdown
summary: William Branham preaches on the parallels between scientific achievements and spiritual achievements in the church age. He traces the progression from horse and buggy (justification) to automobile (sanctification) to airplane (Pentecostal baptism of the Holy Ghost) and finally to astronaut (the present spiritual age where believers can go beyond denominational thinking). He emphasizes that natural things reflect spiritual realities and that believers must stay true to the Word.

title: The Key To The Door
summary: William Branham preaches on the key of faith that unlocks the door to God's promises, using Revelation 20:1 as a text. He emphasizes that Jesus is the Door and faith is the key, illustrating with biblical heroes and personal testimonies. The sermon includes announcements about church building, a baby dedication, and upcoming meetings.
themes: Faith as the key to unlock God's promises
Jesus Christ as the only Door to salvation, healing, and peace
The importance of holding to God's Word over creeds and denominations
Personal testimony of God's faithfulness in calling and provision
The danger of unbelief and the need for full Gospel faith

title: The Influence Of Another
summary: William Branham preaches on the influence of King Uzziah on the prophet Isaiah, emphasizing the importance of staying in one's God-given calling and not being lifted up with pride. He warns against compromising the Word for organizational creeds and urges believers to remain faithful to God's order.
themes: The power of a godly example

title: A Guide
summary: William Branham preaches on the Holy Spirit as the God-given Guide for believers, using the analogy of a wilderness guide to illustrate the necessity of following the Spirit's leading into all truth. He warns against relying on human creeds, denominations, or traditions, and emphasizes that the Holy Spirit will always align with the Word of God.

title: The Stature of a Perfect Man
summary: William Branham teaches on building the living Tabernacle of God, emphasizing that believers must be born again and then add virtue, knowledge, temperance, patience, godliness, brotherly kindness, and love to their faith. He explains that these qualities cannot be manufactured but naturally flow from a changed nature in Christ.

title: Ordination
subtitle: 62-1104E
summary: William Branham discusses the biblical basis for ordination, emphasizing that gifts and callings come from God alone, not through human impartation. He then ordains Brother McKinney, a former Methodist minister, by laying on of hands and the right hand of fellowship. The sermon concludes with a communion service and feetwashing.

title: Blasphemous Names
summary: William Branham discusses the need for a larger church building, commemorates Brother Taylor, and interprets a sister's dream about the Holy Spirit. He emphasizes that the Holy Spirit is poured out on individuals, not organizations, and that true faith requires adding virtue, knowledge, temperance, patience, godliness, brotherly kindness, and love.

title: Why I'm Against Organized Religion
summary: William Branham explains his opposition to organized religion, arguing that it is unscriptural and based on human tradition rather than God's Word. He uses biblical examples such as Adam, Nimrod, Korah, and the Pharisees to show that organization leads to rejection of God's messengers and message. Branham emphasizes that salvation is a birth, not a membership, and calls believers to separate from man-made systems.

title: Dedication
subtitle: 62-1111M
summary: William Branham speaks at a rededication service for a small church in Elizabethtown, Kentucky. He uses the biblical examples of David's desire to build a temple and Solomon's construction to illustrate that God's true temple is not a building but the hearts of believers. He emphasizes the need for personal dedication and the filling of the Holy Spirit.

title: Return And Jubilee
summary: William Branham speaks on the biblical concept of Jubilee from Leviticus 25, drawing parallels to the Pentecostal outpouring fifty years prior in Louisiana. He warns against losing the original spiritual inheritance through organization and creeds, calling believers to return to the Holy Spirit and the Word.

title: The Way Back
summary: William Branham preaches on the need for the church to return to God through the inoculation of the Blood of Jesus Christ and the baptism of the Holy Spirit. He uses the story of King Ahaziah and Elijah to illustrate how people often reject God's provided way back, preferring popular but ineffective methods. Branham calls for a genuine new birth that involves dying to self and taking God's serum for sin.

title: Investments
summary: William Branham uses the story of the rich young ruler to discuss the concept of spiritual investments, urging believers to invest in eternal life through faith in Christ rather than worldly possessions. He draws parallels to Noah, Daniel, and other biblical figures who trusted God's promises despite opposition.

title: All Things
summary: William Branham preaches on the theme of 'All Things' from Romans 8:32, emphasizing that all things are ours through Christ. He discusses the importance of sincerity in worship, warning against ritualistic forms that lack power, and stresses that only the shed blood of Jesus Christ can bridge the chasm between man and God.

title: The Countdown
summary: William Branham uses the analogy of a countdown for a space launch to describe the progression of the church through the seven church ages, culminating in the rapture. He contrasts the natural astronaut age with the spiritual astronaut age, urging believers to rise above earthly denominations and creeds to be ready for Christ's return.

title: Convinced And Then Concerned
summary: William Branham preaches on the need to be convinced of God's Word and then concerned for others. He contrasts the early church's zeal with modern complacency, emphasizing that true conviction leads to action and concern for the lost.

title: Remembering The Lord
summary: William Branham speaks on the importance of remembering Christ, especially through communion, and warns against the dangers of prejudice, jealousy, and personal gain that can cause one to miss their visitation. He uses examples from Scripture, such as Herod and Judas, to illustrate the consequences of failing to recognize and honor the Lord.

title: The Falling Apart of the World
summary: William Branham delivers a Christmas message at the tabernacle, discussing the true meaning of Christmas and critiquing its commercial and pagan origins. He emphasizes the importance of spiritual birth over church membership and dedicates several children to the Lord.

title: The Reproach For The Cause Of The Word
summary: William Branham shares a vision of five mighty angels and reflects on the reproach that God's servants bear for the sake of His Word. He encourages believers to stand firm in faith despite scoffers and trials, using examples from Noah and personal testimonies of healing.

title: Is This The Sign Of The End, Sir?
summary: William Branham preaches on the urgency of the times, interpreting Revelation 10:1-7 and discussing visions and dreams that point to the end of the age. He shares personal experiences and prophetic insights, emphasizing the need to stay true to the Word and the Spirit's guidance.

title: Absolute
summary: William Branham shares a personal testimony about the resolution of a tax case with the U.S. government, emphasizing the importance of having an 'absolute'—a firm, Christ-centered foundation. He draws on biblical examples like Job, Abraham, Moses, and Paul to illustrate how unwavering faith in God's Word enables believers to stand firm amidst trials.

title: The Contest
summary: In this New Year's Eve sermon, William Branham encourages believers to recognize the spiritual contest between the Church and Satan, emphasizing the power of God's Word as the believer's strength. He shares a testimony of a healing in India to demonstrate God's power over demonic forces, and calls the congregation to enter the new year with faith and the full armor of God.

title: Influence
summary: William Branham speaks on the theme of influence, using the example of King Uzziah and the prophet Isaiah to illustrate how one's life and actions affect others. He emphasizes the importance of sincerity, humility, and adherence to God's Word over popularity or organizational loyalty, warning against pride and the loss of spiritual influence.

title: Perseverance
summary: William Branham preaches on the theme of perseverance, using biblical examples such as Noah, Moses, David, and the Syrophoenician woman to illustrate the importance of persistent faith. He encourages believers to hold fast to God's Word despite opposition and to remain steadfast in their faith.

title: Letting Off Pressure
summary: William Branham speaks on the pressures of modern life and the need for a refuge in Christ. Using the Old Testament cities of refuge and the Passover as types, he emphasizes that true safety and relief from pressure come only by being under the Blood of Jesus, not by church membership or denominational affiliation.

title: A Trumpet Gives an Uncertain Sound
summary: William Branham speaks on the uncertainty of worldly systems—government, politics, home life, and church organizations—contrasting them with the certainty of God's Word. He emphasizes that the Bible is the only sure foundation, and believers must be trained to recognize the clear sound of the Gospel trumpet, standing firm on God's promises.
themes: faith and trust in God's promises

title: Accepting God's Provided Way At The End Time
summary: William Branham speaks on accepting God's provided way, using nature as an illustration. He shares a vision of the afterlife and recounts leading an infidel to Christ through a simple lesson about an apple tree. The sermon emphasizes that God has a perfect way for everything, and we must follow it rather than manufacturing our own.

title: The Evening Messenger
summary: William Branham preaches on the concept of the evening messenger, drawing from Zechariah 14:6-7. He discusses how God sends a prophet at the end of each age to call His people back to the Word, and how the current age is the end time where light will come in the evening.

title: Awakening Jesus
summary: William Branham preaches on the account of Jesus calming the storm, using the disciples' fear and lack of faith as a lesson for believers today. He emphasizes that Jesus is the same yesterday, today, and forever, and that He is present with His people even in times of trouble. Branham encourages the congregation to trust in the Word and the Spirit rather than being flustered by circumstances.

title: Spirit of Truth
summary: William Branham preaches on the Holy Spirit as the Spirit of Truth who guides into all truth and shows things to come. He shares testimonies of visions and healings, emphasizing that God is interested in all creation and that believers must yield to the Holy Spirit.

title: The Way of a True Prophet
summary: William Branham uses the prophet Amos as a model to contrast true prophetic ministry with modern evangelism. He warns that the church has drifted from the Word into sin and compromise, and calls for a return to holiness and the authority of Scripture.

title: Just One More Time, Lord
summary: William Branham preaches on the story of Samson as a warning to the modern church, particularly the Pentecostal movement, which he argues has fallen into the same traps of glamour, organization, and compromise with the world. He calls for a return to the power of the Holy Spirit and the Word of God.

title: The Voice of God in This Last Days
summary: William Branham preaches on the need to hear the Voice of God amidst the many confusing voices of the last days—political, Hollywood, philosophical, and false religious voices. He uses the examples of Samuel, Noah, Moses, and Adam to show how hearing and obeying God's Word changes lives and brings judgment on the world.

title: Zacchaeus, the Businessman
summary: William Branham tells the story of Zacchaeus, a wealthy tax collector who climbed a sycamore tree to see Jesus. He uses this narrative to encourage businessmen and others to seek Jesus earnestly, regardless of social pressure or personal cost, and emphasizes that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever.

title: Remembering The Lord
summary: William Branham speaks on the importance of remembering the Lord through communion and the examples of biblical figures who remembered God's faithfulness. He emphasizes that true communion is communing with God and waiting for His response, and he encourages believers to stand firm on God's Word despite worldly pressures.

title: Identification
summary: William Branham preaches on identifying oneself with Bible characters by looking into the mirror of God's Word. He emphasizes Christ as the perfect example of God's character and calls believers to let that same mind be in them, reflecting Christ in their lives.

title: Investments
summary: William Branham speaks to a businessmen's breakfast about making the best investment—eternal life in Jesus Christ. He contrasts the rich young ruler who turned away because the cost was too great with the need for sincere, Word-based faith. Branham warns against gambling with religion, organizational pride, and worldly attachments that hinder true discipleship.

title: An Absolute
summary: William Branham preaches on the necessity of having an absolute in life, using Christ and His Word as the ultimate anchor. He illustrates through personal stories and analogies that every area of life requires a final authority, and for believers, that must be Christ, who is the same as His Word.

title: A Door In A Door
summary: William Branham speaks at a Full Gospel Business Men's Fellowship breakfast in Tucson, using the metaphor of a door to discuss Christ's knocking at the heart of the Laodicean church. He emphasizes the importance of recognizing God in unusual ways and places, and urges believers to open their hearts to Jesus.

title: A Absolute
summary: William Branham speaks on the necessity of having an absolute—something unchanging to anchor one's faith—especially in times of crisis. He uses biblical examples like Noah, Moses, Daniel, and Paul to illustrate how God's Word is the ultimate absolute that never fails. The sermon is part of a series of prayer meetings for two children facing death, urging believers to pray with unwavering faith in God's promises.

title: The Breach Between The Seven Church Ages And The Seven Seals
God Hiding Himself In Simplicity, Then Revealing Himself In The Same
summary: William Branham rededicates the Branham Tabernacle, emphasizing reverence and order in worship. He then introduces a message on how God hides Himself in simplicity, revealing Himself to the humble rather than the wise.

title: The First Seal
summary: William Branham begins the study of the Seven Seals, focusing on the First Seal of Revelation 6. He emphasizes that the Book is sealed and can only be opened by the Lamb, and that the mysteries are revealed in the last days. He warns against denominationalism and stresses the importance of being ready for the Rapture.

title: The Second Seal
summary: William Branham opens the service with prayer and introduces the study of the Second Seal from Revelation 6:3-4. He discusses the four horsemen, emphasizing that the white horse rider represents the antichrist spirit in three stages. He connects the revelation of the seals to the last days and the role of prophets, citing Amos 3:7. Branham also shares personal testimonies of supernatural events and warns against false impersonations of true spiritual movements.

title: The Third Seal
summary: William Branham opens the Third Seal from Revelation 6:5-6, describing the black horse and its rider with a pair of balances. He contrasts the fall of the natural Eve with the fall of the spiritual Eve (the church) at the Nicaea Council, warning against substituting man-made creeds for God's Word.

title: The Fourth Seal
summary: William Branham opens the Fourth Seal from Revelation 6:7-8, revealing the pale horse and its rider named Death. He connects this seal to the antichrist spirit and the end-time revelation of mysteries, emphasizing the vindication of God's Word and the stimulation of new wine through revelation.

title: The Fifth Seal
summary: William Branham opens the Fifth Seal from Revelation 6:9-11, revealing the souls under the altar who were slain for the Word of God. He explains that no beast announces this seal because the church age has ended and the antichrist's ride is complete. Branham contrasts the four beasts of God with the four horses of the antichrist, showing how God's power combated each stage of false teaching.
themes: Martyrdom and the souls under the altar

title: The Sixth Seal
summary: William Branham opens the Sixth Seal from Revelation 6:12-17, comparing it with Matthew 24 to show the judgment that comes after the Church is taken. He discusses the martyrs under the altar, the hundred and forty-four thousand Jews, and the great earthquake and cosmic disturbances that mark the beginning of the Tribulation period.

title: The Seventh Seal
subtitle: 63-0324E
summary: In this closing sermon of the series on the Seven Seals, William Branham discusses the Seventh Seal from Revelation 8:1, emphasizing the silence in heaven. He explains the interval between the Sixth and Seventh Seals, focusing on the sealing of the 144,000 Jews from the tribes of Israel during the Tribulation period, and distinguishes this from the Gentile Bride. He also reflects on the week's services and the importance of divine revelation.

title: Questions and Answers on the Seals
summary: William Branham answers questions from the congregation regarding the Seven Seals, the wise and foolish virgins, the Rapture, and other biblical topics. He emphasizes the importance of not interpreting revelations personally and encourages believers to continue faithfully in their duties.

title: God Hiding Himself In Simplicity
summary: William Branham speaks on how God hides Himself in simplicity, revealing Himself to the humble rather than the wise. He emphasizes that faith in God's Word, not education or science, is the path to knowing God, and that the Church must stay behind the Word.
themes: The Word of God as the standard

title: The World Is Falling Apart
summary: William Branham warns that the world is falling apart due to corruption in politics, education, and religion, including Pentecostalism. He calls for a return to the pure Word of God and the Holy Spirit, rejecting man-made systems and traditions. He emphasizes that only the coming of Jesus Christ can save the world.

title: Victory Day
summary: William Branham speaks on the concept of victory, contrasting worldly victories with the spiritual victory found in Christ. He emphasizes focusing on the innocent substitute, Jesus Christ, and warns against jealousy and division that lead to conflict.
themes: Unity in the Body of Christ

title: Look
summary: William Branham preaches on the theme of 'Look,' urging believers to focus their faith on Jesus Christ and the Word of God. He uses analogies like a camera's range finder and a rifle's accuracy to illustrate the need to zero in on God's promises, emphasizing that the same power that worked in the apostles is available today through the Blood of Christ.
themes: The Word as the focus of faith
Cleansing by the Blood of Christ

title: Come, Follow Me
summary: William Branham speaks to young people about the importance of following Jesus Christ, using the story of the rich young ruler as a cautionary tale. He emphasizes that Eternal Life is not inherited but must be accepted through a born-again experience, and warns against rejecting the call of Christ for worldly possessions or popularity.

title: Jesus Christ The Same Yesterday, Today, And Forever
summary: William Branham opens a four-night campaign in Tucson, emphasizing that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He discusses how to identify Christ through His works and the Scriptures, and encourages believers to seek a personal encounter with the living God.

title: Greater Than Solomon Is Here
summary: William Branham preaches on the need for genuine faith and the demonstration of God's power, using the examples of Jonah and Solomon to show that Jesus Christ is greater than both. He challenges the congregation to look beyond symptoms and believe in the resurrection power of Christ, which is present today.
themes: the power of the Holy Spirit

title: Show Us The Father
summary: William Branham preaches on the human longing to see God, explaining that God can be seen in His universe, His Word, His Son, and His people. He uses personal stories and nature illustrations to demonstrate God's presence and faithfulness.

title: Be Not Afraid
summary: William Branham preaches on the account of Jesus walking on water, using the disciples' testimony meeting on the sea as a backdrop. He encourages believers to have faith, separate from man-made doctrines, and let the life of Christ produce His works in them.

title: Conferences
summary: William Branham speaks on the importance of conferences, drawing parallels between world conferences and God's conferences throughout Scripture. He emphasizes the need for unity among believers and the power of faith, sharing personal anecdotes and testimonies of healing.

title: The Flashing Red Light Of The Sign Of His Coming
summary: William Branham preaches on the signs of Christ's coming, comparing the days of Noah to the present time. He discusses the multiplication of people, the increasing beauty of women, and the moral decay as flashing red lights signaling that the end is near.

title: Standing In The Gap
summary: William Branham returns to his home church after several months, sharing personal updates and plans for upcoming ministry trips. He dedicates several children to the Lord, emphasizing the biblical basis for child dedication over infant baptism. He also briefly mentions a healing testimony and announces his intention to preach on 'The Flashing Red Light Of His Coming' that evening.

title: Why?
summary: William Branham preaches on the question 'Why?' using the story of King Ahaziah who sought Baal-zebub instead of God, and Jeremiah's lament about no balm in Gilead. He argues that God's remedy for sin—the Blood of Jesus—is still available, but people refuse it due to stubbornness and fear of losing popularity. He calls for a return to the Word and a Spirit-filled life.

title: Jesus Christ The Same Yesterday, Today, And Forever
A Greater Than Solomon Is Here
summary: William Branham preaches on the sign of the resurrection and the greater works of Christ, comparing the faith of the queen of Sheba and the repentance of Nineveh to the present generation's need to accept God's gift of the Holy Spirit.

title: O Lord, Just Once More
summary: William Branham preaches on the state of the Pentecostal church, using the story of Samson as a symbol of a fallen church that has lost its spiritual power by compromising with the world and organizing into denominations. He calls for a return to the original Pentecostal experience and warns against hybrid Christianity that lacks the genuine Spirit of God.

title: Is Your Life Worthy Of The Gospel?
summary: William Branham preaches on the parable of the great supper, warning against making excuses to reject God's invitation. He traces how nations and individuals have spurned the Holy Spirit's call, leading to judgment, and urges believers to live lives worthy of the Gospel by following Christ daily.
themes: Seal of God vs. mark of the beast

title: The Third Exodus
summary: William Branham preaches on the parallel between the exodus of Israel from Egypt and a spiritual exodus of the true church in the last days. He warns against denominationalism and the ecumenical movement, calling believers to separate from organized religion and return to the pure Word and Spirit of God.

title: Communion
subtitle: 63-0707E
summary: William Branham leads a communion service, emphasizing self-examination and holiness before partaking. He reads from 1 Corinthians 11, explaining the importance of discerning the Lord's body and living a life worthy of the Gospel. The service includes prayers for forgiveness and sanctification of the bread and wine.

title: The Indictment
summary: William Branham delivers a sermon titled 'The Indictment,' in which he charges the denominational churches of his day with crucifying Jesus Christ afresh by rejecting the Word of God and clinging to creeds and organizations. He draws parallels between the religious leaders who crucified Christ physically at Jerusalem and modern churches that spiritually crucify Him by refusing to accept the full revelation of the Word. Branham argues that the same spirit of jealousy, spiritual blindness, and compromise is at work today, and he calls for a return to the sole authority of Scripture under the shed blood of Christ.

title: Humble Thyself
subtitle: 63-0714E
summary: William Branham speaks on the necessity of humility and unity among believers, urging the congregation to confess faults, love one another, and work together in harmony. He anticipates a healing service and the manifestation of the Third Pull, emphasizing that God exalts the humble.

title: Why Cry? Speak!
summary: William Branham preaches on Exodus 13-14, focusing on God's command to Moses to stop crying and speak to the people to go forward. He draws parallels between Moses' calling and the present-day church, emphasizing the need for a personal encounter with God that anoints faith and brings supernatural reality to the Word.

title: A Prisoner
summary: William Branham preaches on Paul's declaration of being 'a prisoner of Jesus Christ,' emphasizing total surrender to God's will and the Word. He contrasts being yoked to Christ versus being bound by personal ambition or denominational ties, urging believers to become prisoners to Christ alone.

title: He Cares. Do You Care?
summary: William Branham speaks on God's care for humanity, emphasizing the Holy Spirit as the Comforter who continues Christ's work. He addresses the lack of sincerity in modern society and the church, urging genuine confession and faith for healing and salvation.

title: God Doesn't Call Man To Judgment Without First Warning Him
summary: William Branham preaches on God's nature to always warn before judgment, using Hezekiah, Jonah, and Amos as examples. He emphasizes the urgency of the present hour and the need for repentance, drawing parallels to the end times.

title: Christ Is The Mystery Of God Revealed
summary: William Branham teaches that the entire Bible is the revelation of God's mystery in Christ, hidden from ages but now revealed to saints. He emphasizes that Christ is the image of the invisible God and the fullness of God dwells in Him, and that believers must continue in faith grounded and settled.
themes: Christ as the Image of God

title: There Is Only One Way Provided By God For Anything
summary: William Branham preaches that God has only one way to accomplish anything, and any deviation from that way is perversion. He uses examples from nature, such as hybrid seeds and the migration of geese, to illustrate how man's attempts to improve upon God's ways lead to corruption. He emphasizes that the only way to eternal life is through Jesus Christ, the Word made flesh, and that believers must cry out for the promises of God until they are fulfilled.
themes: the baptism of the Holy Spirit

title: A Paradox
summary: William Branham preaches on the concept of a paradox as a miracle that seems incredible but is true. He uses biblical examples such as Joshua commanding the sun to stand still, the feeding of the five thousand, and the virgin birth to illustrate that God is still performing paradoxes today through the new birth and the Holy Spirit.

title: Perseverant
summary: William Branham preaches on the virtue of perseverance, using the example of the Syrophoenician woman who persisted in seeking Jesus' help for her daughter. He emphasizes that true faith is based on God's Word and leads to persistence despite obstacles, and he encourages believers to hold fast to God's promises.

title: Investments
summary: William Branham uses the story of the rich young ruler to discuss the concept of spiritual investments, urging believers to invest in eternal life through Jesus Christ rather than worldly possessions or denominational affiliations. He contrasts the Laodicean church age with the opportunity for true conversion and the new birth.

title: Influence
summary: William Branham preaches on the theme of influence, using the story of King Uzziah and the prophet Isaiah to illustrate how even godly people can fall when they become self-sufficient. He emphasizes the importance of humility, reverence for God, and the need for Christians to live righteously as examples to others.

title: Once More
subtitle: 63-0804A
summary: William Branham uses the story of Samson to draw a parallel with the modern church, which he sees as having lost its spiritual power by compromising with the world and denominationalism. He calls for repentance and a return to the Word of God, urging believers to cry out for a revival of the Holy Spirit's power.

title: Calling Jesus On The Scene
summary: William Branham preaches on Mark 4:35-41, using the story of Jesus calming the storm to illustrate that believers have Jesus in their ship (their lives) and can call on Him in times of trouble. He emphasizes that Jesus is the same yesterday, today, and forever, and that His Word is the remedy for every problem.

title: The Uniting Time And Sign
summary: William Branham speaks on the importance of discerning the signs of the times, emphasizing that God gives signs to believers. He draws parallels between the rejection of Jesus by the Jews and the current rejection of God's Word by churches uniting in ecumenical movements, warning of coming judgment.

title: Perfect Faith
summary: William Branham teaches on the nature of perfect faith as a substance, not imagination, that comes by hearing the Word of God. He emphasizes that believers must recognize their position in Christ and have unwavering confidence in God's promises, illustrated through biblical examples and personal testimonies of healing.

title: How Can I Overcome?
summary: William Branham encourages believers to overcome the world by yielding to Christ, using examples from Noah, Daniel, and Lot. He emphasizes that true overcoming comes through the Holy Spirit, not human effort, and warns against becoming spiritually stagnant in the Laodicean church age.

title: Desperations
summary: William Branham preaches on the necessity of desperation in seeking God, using biblical examples like Jacob and Hezekiah. He emphasizes that the Holy Spirit is the Token of the Blood applied, and that true faith requires love and fervent prayer.

title: Token
summary: William Branham preaches on the concept of the 'Token' from Exodus 12:13, explaining that the blood of the lamb in Egypt was a token of God's protection. He draws a parallel to the Holy Spirit as the Token for believers today, emphasizing that it is the only sign God will recognize for salvation and deliverance from coming wrath.

title: Pardon
summary: William Branham preaches on the theme of pardon through the blood of Jesus Christ, emphasizing that true pardon requires acceptance and sincerity, not mere ritual or tradition. He contrasts the Old Testament blood sacrifices with the New Testament reality of Christ's sacrifice, urging believers to display the token of the Holy Spirit in their lives.

title: Go, Wake Jesus
summary: William Branham preaches on the account of Jesus calming the storm, emphasizing that Christ is present with believers in every trial. He encourages the congregation to recognize Jesus' presence and to have faith in His power to calm life's storms, just as He did on the Sea of Galilee.

title: He That Is In You
summary: William Branham preaches on the power of God within believers, emphasizing that 'greater is He that is in you than he that is in the world.' He discusses the end times, the Seven Seals, and the importance of staying true to the Word. The sermon includes baby dedications, testimonies of healing, and a call to faith and repentance.
themes: Greater is He that is in you

title: Souls That Are In Prison Now
summary: William Branham preaches on the fate of souls imprisoned in hell, drawing from visions he experienced as a youth and recent observations of modern women's appearance that reminded him of those visions. He explores the biblical passages in Jude, 2 Peter, and 1 Peter about angels and spirits in prison, and questions whether current times reflect the judgment he foresaw.

title: Sir, We Would See Jesus
summary: William Branham opens a series of meetings by expressing his desire to see Jesus Christ, not just hear about Him. He emphasizes that Jesus is the same yesterday, today, and forever, and that believers should reflect His life. Branham contrasts true Christianity with reliance on education, entertainment, or religious dress, urging a return to the Word and the power of the Holy Spirit.

title: The Sign Of This Time
summary: William Branham preaches on the signs of the times, emphasizing that as in the days of Noah and Sodom, the last days will be marked by God's judgment and the manifestation of His Spirit in human flesh. He warns against seeking signs for entertainment and calls for genuine faith in the finished work of Christ.

title: Influence
summary: William Branham preaches on the theme of influence, using the story of King Uzziah and the prophet Isaiah from Isaiah 6. He emphasizes that Christians must be careful of their influence on others, avoid pride, and keep their eyes on God rather than on fallible humans. The sermon calls for reverence, humility, and staying in one's God-given position.

title: Investments
summary: William Branham speaks to businessmen in New York City about the investment of eternal life. He contrasts worldly investments with the assurance of salvation through Jesus Christ, using the story of the rich young ruler and examples from Noah and Daniel.
themes: The role of the Holy Spirit

title: Perseverance
summary: William Branham preaches on the importance of perseverance in faith, using biblical examples such as the Canaanite woman, Noah, Moses, David, and Samson. He encourages believers to persist in trusting God's Word despite opposition or lack of immediate results, and concludes with a prayer line for the sick.
themes: the power of the Holy Spirit
the church as a reflection of Christ

title: Once More
summary: William Branham preaches on the parallel between Samson's fall and the modern church's loss of spiritual power. He laments that the church has compromised with the world, lost its spiritual sight, and become captive to denominational systems, just as Samson was captured by the Philistines. He calls for a return to the Word and the power of the Holy Spirit.
themes: Return to the Word of God

title: I Am The Resurrection And Life
summary: A funeral sermon for a young Christian named Garnett, using nature's cycles of death and resurrection to illustrate the certainty of the believer's resurrection through Christ. Branham emphasizes that only those 'germitized' by the Holy Spirit will rise again, and comforts the bereaved with the hope of reunion.

title: Three Kinds of Believers
summary: William Branham preaches on three categories of believers: true believers, make-believers, and unbelievers, using biblical examples such as Peter, Noah, Daniel, David, Abraham, Job, Joseph, Nathanael, and Bartimaeus to illustrate genuine faith that trusts God's Word despite opposition or impossibility.

title: What Shall I Do With Jesus Called Christ?
summary: William Branham opens with a prayer for the Kennedy family after the President's assassination, then transitions to a Sunday school lesson on the trial of Jesus before Pilate. He emphasizes that the religious system of the day rejected Christ despite knowing He was the Messiah, and draws parallels to modern times where denominational systems prevent people from accepting the truth of God's Word.

title: The World Is Again Falling Apart
summary: William Branham speaks on the world's moral, political, and religious decay, comparing it to the time of Christ's first coming. He warns that the world is again falling apart and calls for a return to the anointed Word of God for the hour.

title: The Token
summary: William Branham preaches on the Passover token of blood in Exodus 12, explaining it as a type of Christ. He emphasizes that the Holy Ghost is the believer's token today, identifying those who have accepted Christ's sacrifice. Branham calls for sincerity and separation from the world as the end-time exodus approaches.

title: Testimony
summary: William Branham gives a personal testimony of his recent experiences with God, including a supernatural encounter in the Colorado mountains where he commanded a storm to cease and it obeyed. He reflects on the burden he has carried for five years and shares a vision of his wife as a young woman, leading to a deeper sense of God's presence and guidance.

title: The Super Sign
summary: William Branham preaches on the theme of the 'super sign' as God's supernatural intervention in human history, culminating in the incarnation of Christ and the indwelling of the Holy Spirit in the Church. He contrasts worldly 'super' achievements with God's eternal sign of a virgin conceiving and God dwelling with man, emphasizing that God always sends a prophet as a sign before judgment.

title: Influence
summary: William Branham speaks to the young people of Shreveport, using the story of King Uzziah and the prophet Isaiah to illustrate the power of influence and the importance of staying in one's God-ordained place. He warns against pride and the danger of trying to take a position God has not given, emphasizing that God's Word is the ultimate standard.
themes: The Word of God as the standard

title: Go, Awake Jesus
summary: William Branham preaches on the account of Jesus calming the storm, using it as a metaphor for the church facing trials. He discusses three classes of people—believers, unbelievers, and make-believers—and encourages the congregation to recognize Jesus' presence in their midst, even when trouble arises.

title: Just Once More, Lord
summary: In this closing sermon of a convention, William Branham uses the story of Samson to draw a parallel to the modern church, which he sees as having lost its spiritual power by compromising with denominational systems and abandoning the Word of God. He calls for a return to the original Pentecostal experience and a willingness to die to the world in order to regain God's power.

title: An Absolute
summary: William Branham preaches on the necessity of having an absolute in the Christian life, using Paul's conversion as an example of meeting Christ as the ultimate tie post. He contrasts man-made absolutes with God's Word, which is the final authority for believers.

title: Wedding Ceremony
summary: William Branham officiates a wedding ceremony, joining a man and woman in holy matrimony. He prays for God's blessing on the couple and reflects on the parallel between earthly marriage and the coming of Christ for His Bride.

title: Why Little Bethlehem
summary: William Branham delivers a Christmas message explaining why God chose the small, humble town of Bethlehem for the birth of Jesus. He emphasizes that God works through the insignificant and humble to display His glory, contrasting worldly tinsel with the true meaning of Christmas. The sermon calls believers to humility and to abide in Christ, the Bread of Life.

title: We Have Seen His Star And Have Come To Worship Him
summary: William Branham speaks on the true meaning of Christmas, contrasting it with commercialism and Santa Claus. He examines the biblical account of the wise men, the star, and Joseph's dream, emphasizing that God reveals truth through His Word and supernatural signs.

title: God's Gifts Always Find Their Places
summary: William Branham reflects on the true meaning of Christmas, contrasting it with pagan traditions. He examines the gifts of the Magi—gold, frankincense, and myrrh—as symbols of Christ's deity, service, and death, emphasizing that believers should dedicate themselves wholly to God.

title: Church Order
summary: William Branham addresses church leaders on proper order and operation of the local church, covering roles of deacons, trustees, and pastor, handling of spiritual gifts like tongues and interpretation, Sunday school organization, and maintaining discipline. He emphasizes following Scripture and the need for orderly conduct in worship services.

title: Look Away to Jesus
summary: William Branham speaks about the Third Pull being vindicated and identified, urging the congregation to remain faithful as the end times approach. He shares testimonies of healings and miracles, including the salvation of Hattie Wright's sons and the calming of a storm, emphasizing that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever.

title: There Is A Man Here That Can Turn On The Light
Shalom
summary: In this New Year's message, William Branham addresses the Church as the elect Bride of Christ, contrasting the gross darkness covering the world with the Light of God's revelation. He emphasizes that God reveals His events in heaven before they occur on earth, citing recent signs such as the moon's blackout and the pope's visit to Jerusalem as fulfillments of prophecy. Branham calls the Church to peace (Shalom) and to arise and shine in the midst of darkness.

title: Shalom
summary: William Branham delivers a New Year's message on the theme of 'Shalom' (peace), contrasting the gross darkness covering the earth with the light of God's Word for the elect. He warns against ecumenical movements and denominationalism, urging believers to stand on the vindicated Word and look forward to Christ's coming.

title: His Unfailing Words of Promise
summary: William Branham preaches on the unfailing nature of God's promises, using Matthew 24:32-35 as his text. He discusses the signs of the times, including the fig tree representing Israel becoming a nation, and shares a personal testimony of his wife's miraculous healing from a tumor.

title: God's Word Calls For A Total Separation From Unbelief
summary: William Branham preaches on the necessity of total separation from unbelief, using biblical examples from Genesis, the Nazarite vow, and the life of Jesus to illustrate how God's Word separates light from darkness, faith from doubt, and believers from the world. He emphasizes that true believers must separate themselves from anything contrary to God's Word, including church traditions and worldly cares, to become a Bride prepared for Christ.

title: Looking Unto Jesus
summary: William Branham preaches on the importance of looking unto Jesus as the Word of God for this hour, emphasizing that each generation must see Christ revealed in the promised Word. He contrasts those who see only tradition or criticism with those who, like the prophets and disciples, recognize the vindicated Word and find salvation, healing, and life.
themes: Word of God for the hour

title: Turn On The Light
summary: William Branham preaches on the necessity of accepting the present light of God's Word rather than living in the glare of past ages. He uses the analogy of the sun to illustrate how each age has its own revelation, and warns against rejecting the current light as the Pharisees did. He calls the church to mature with the light and prepare for the coming of Christ.

title: What Shall We Do With This Jesus Called Christ?
summary: William Branham preaches on the parallel between the trial of Jesus before Pilate and the spiritual condition of the modern church. He warns against rejecting the Holy Spirit's work and the vindicated Word of God, urging listeners to accept Jesus Christ before it is too late.

title: God Is His Own Interpreter
summary: William Branham preaches that God interprets His own Word through manifestation, using examples from Scripture such as Abraham, the virgin birth, and the ministry of Jesus. He emphasizes that in the last days, the same signs seen in the days of Sodom will be repeated among the spiritual seed of Abraham.

title: God's Provided Way for This Day
summary: William Branham preaches on God's unchanging way of providing for His people in every age, emphasizing that God always works through His Word and His chosen prophets. He calls believers to come God's way—through the new birth and the baptism of the Holy Ghost—rather than relying on human traditions or denominational systems. The sermon encourages persistent faith and crying out to God until His promises are vindicated.
themes: the baptism of the Holy Ghost
God's provided way for each age

title: The Patriarch Abraham
summary: William Branham preaches on the faith of Abraham, the father of faith, emphasizing that true Seed of Abraham believe God's Word regardless of circumstances. He uses examples from the Bible to show how Abraham's Seed possess the gates of their enemies through faith, and concludes with a prayer for the sick.
themes: Possessing the gates of the enemy

title: The Token
summary: William Branham preaches on the biblical token of the blood of the lamb in Exodus 12, which prefigures the Holy Spirit as the required token for believers today. He emphasizes that without the baptism of the Holy Ghost, one cannot be identified with Christ and will face judgment.

title: Countdown
summary: William Branham uses the analogy of scientific progress from horse and buggy to astronaut to illustrate the spiritual progression of the church through justification, sanctification, and the baptism of the Holy Ghost. He declares that the church is now in the 'astronaut age,' where believers are empowered by the Holy Spirit to rise above creeds and denominations, awaiting the rapture. The sermon emphasizes that natural achievements are types of spiritual realities, and the countdown of church ages is complete, with the next event being the catching away of the Bride.
themes: the astronaut age of the church

title: When Their Eyes Were Opened, They Knew Him
summary: William Branham preaches on the resurrection of Jesus Christ, using the account of the disciples on the road to Emmaus to illustrate how Christ reveals Himself through the Word and through the same works He did before His crucifixion. He emphasizes that God always fulfills His promises, and that believers must invite Him in to have their eyes opened to His presence and power today.

title: Then Jesus Came And Called
summary: William Branham preaches on the story of Lazarus from John 11, emphasizing that Jesus comes in the darkest hour when all hope is gone. He contrasts the evidence of true faith—vindication of the Word in the hour—with outward signs like speaking in tongues or shouting. Branham encourages believers to recognize Jesus as the manifested Word and to believe for the impossible.
themes: Jesus comes in the darkest hour

title: The Voice Of The Sign
summary: William Branham teaches on the relationship between signs and the voice of God, using Moses and the burning bush as a primary example. He explains that God gives signs to attract attention, and then the voice of the sign speaks through His Word, often through a prophet. Branham applies this pattern to the present day, urging believers to recognize the signs of the times and heed the voice of God's vindicated Word.

title: Influences
summary: William Branham preaches on the theme of influences, using the biblical account of King Uzziah and the prophet Isaiah to illustrate how pride and irreverence lead to downfall. He warns against compromising with the world and emphasizes the need for holiness and reverence in the presence of God.
themes: Influence of godly vs. ungodly examples
Holiness and separation from the world

title: Identification
summary: William Branham preaches on the necessity of spiritual identification, using Bible characters as mirrors for believers to examine their own faith and alignment with God's Word. He emphasizes that true Christians are identified by the Holy Spirit and by their adherence to Scripture, contrasting them with those who follow popular religious trends.

title: Sirs, We Would See Jesus
summary: William Branham preaches on the desire to see Jesus, emphasizing that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He uses biblical examples, such as the Greeks seeking Jesus and the encounter with the Samaritan woman, to illustrate that God manifests His Word through prophets and signs. Branham calls the church to recognize the present hour and the promised signs of the end times.
themes: Jesus Christ the same yesterday, today, and forever

title: Perseverant
summary: William Branham preaches on the virtue of perseverance in faith, using biblical examples such as the Syrophenician woman, Noah, Moses, David, Samson, and John the Baptist. He emphasizes that true faith is persistent, based on the Word of God, and overcomes all hindrances.

title: A Greater Than Solomon Is Here Now
summary: William Branham preaches on Matthew 12:38-42, comparing the generation that rejected Jesus to the queen of Sheba who traveled far to hear Solomon's wisdom. He emphasizes that Jesus is greater than Solomon and that the Holy Spirit's work today is the sign of the resurrection for this adulterous generation.
themes: God's gift of the Holy Spirit

title: A Testimony On The Sea
summary: William Branham uses the biblical account of Jesus walking on water to illustrate the need for a genuine revival and warns against the dangers of denominationalism and the Ecumenical Council. He calls the church to return to the power of the Holy Ghost and a humble, separated life.

title: The Token
summary: William Branham preaches on the biblical token of the blood in Exodus as a type of the Holy Spirit today. He emphasizes that the Holy Spirit is the token of identification with Christ, the paid price for redemption, and that only those displaying this token will be saved in the coming exodus of the Bride from the church.

title: God Is Identified By His Characteristics
summary: William Branham preaches that God is identified by His characteristics, which are supernatural and vindicate His Word. He uses biblical examples like Moses, Balaam, and Jesus to show that true identification comes through God's supernatural signs, not just fundamental teaching. He emphasizes that in the last days, the Son of man will be revealed to the elect as in the days of Sodom.

title: When Their Eyes Were Opened, They Knew Him
summary: William Branham preaches on the road to Emmaus story, emphasizing that the disciples failed to recognize the resurrected Jesus because they did not understand the Scriptures. He draws parallels to the present day, where believers often fail to recognize Christ's work because of creeds, programs, and unbelief. Branham urges the congregation to invite Jesus in so He can open their eyes to the promised Word for this age.

title: The Voice Of The Sign
summary: William Branham preaches on the relationship between God's signs and the voice that accompanies them, using the example of Moses and the burning bush. He emphasizes that God always sends a prophet with a sign to attract attention, and the voice behind the sign must be scriptural. Branham applies this to the present day, warning of judgment and calling for repentance.

title: The Investments
summary: William Branham uses the metaphor of a businessman offering an 'Eternal Life Assurance' policy to discuss the rich young ruler's encounter with Jesus. He contrasts worldly investments with the eternal investment of faith, emphasizing that true life comes only through a personal relationship with Christ, not church membership or moral living.
themes: Rejection of Christ by the religious

title: Influence
summary: William Branham preaches on the power of influence, using the story of King Uzziah and the prophet Isaiah to illustrate how a man's life can impact others for good or ill. He warns against pride and stepping outside one's God-given calling, and emphasizes the need for reverence, humility, and action in serving God.
themes: The Blood of Christ as our covering

title: Sir, We Would See Jesus
summary: William Branham preaches on the desire to see Jesus, emphasizing that Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He uses the biblical account of Greeks seeking Jesus and the encounters with Nathanael and the Samaritan woman to illustrate how Jesus identified Himself as the Word made flesh, discerning the thoughts of the heart. Branham urges believers to look forward to what God is doing now rather than clinging to past traditions.
themes: Christ the same yesterday, today, and forever
Looking forward to God's present work

title: Calling Jesus On The Scene
summary: William Branham preaches on the disciples' experience of calling Jesus during a storm, drawing parallels to the present-day revival and the need to call on Jesus in times of trouble. He emphasizes that Jesus is the same yesterday, today, and forever, and that believers must have faith in His Word and presence.
themes: The Word of God as interpreter

title: God Identifying Himself By His Characteristics
summary: William Branham preaches on how God identifies Himself through His characteristics, using examples from nature, the Old Testament, and the life of Jesus. He emphasizes that God's characteristics are supernatural and unchanging, and that believers today should be identified by the same characteristics as Christ.
themes: the Spirit of God vs. church spirit

title: He Was To Pass This Way
summary: William Branham preaches on the story of Zacchaeus, emphasizing the importance of seeking Jesus despite obstacles and the transformative power of encountering the real Christ. He encourages believers to be persistent in their faith and to examine the Word for themselves.

title: The Voice Of The Sign
summary: William Branham preaches on the theme of God's signs and their accompanying voice, using the Exodus narrative as a type. He emphasizes that true signs from God are followed by a Scriptural voice, and that prophets are signs of impending judgment, calling the elect to readiness.

title: Possessing The Gate Of The Enemy After Trial
summary: William Branham preaches on Abraham's faith and the promise that his seed would possess the gate of his enemies. He draws parallels between Abraham's test and the believer's trials, emphasizing that the Royal Seed (Christ) has already conquered every enemy—sickness, death, hell—and that believers, as Abraham's spiritual seed, can possess the gates of their enemies through faith in God's Word and the sealing of the Holy Spirit.

title: The Identified Christ of All Ages
summary: William Branham opens a revival in Louisville, Mississippi, emphasizing the need for unity and faith. He discusses the nature of God as the same yesterday, today, and forever, and how He identifies Himself through His Word in each age, often through a single anointed individual.

title: Jehovah-Jireh
summary: William Branham preaches on the covenant God made with Abraham, emphasizing that God's promises are unconditional and require total separation from unbelief. He draws parallels between the Old Testament covenant and the New Covenant in Christ, highlighting that the same Spirit that was in Christ is in believers today, confirming the covenant through signs and wonders.
themes: the Spirit of Christ in believers

title: Jehovah-Jireh 3
summary: William Branham continues his series on Abraham, focusing on the promise of Isaac and the revelation of God as Elohim. He draws parallels between Abraham's encounter with God in human flesh and the present-day manifestation of God's Word through discernment and healing, emphasizing faith and the imminent return of Christ.

title: A Trial
summary: William Branham presents a courtroom allegory where God's Word is on trial against the world, with Satan as prosecutor and the Holy Ghost as defense witness. He calls biblical witnesses like Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Joshua to testify that God keeps His promises, and offers his own testimony of God's faithfulness. The sermon challenges believers to trust God's Word despite delays or opposition.
themes: the Word of God as seed

title: The Identification of Christ in All Ages
summary: William Branham introduces his ministry in Birmingham, emphasizing that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He explains that God identifies Himself through prophets in each age, and that true faith rests on God's unchanging Word.

title: Scriptural Signs Of The Time
summary: William Branham preaches on the importance of recognizing Scriptural signs and voices in the last days, warning against living in the glare of past revivals and urging believers to heed the present-day message of God. He emphasizes that God sends signs to attract attention, followed by a Scriptural voice, and that the generation that rejects the sign goes into chaos.

title: Spiritual Amnesia
summary: William Branham preaches on the spiritual condition of the church, drawing from Amos 3 to warn against forgetting God's Word and holiness. He identifies 'spiritual amnesia' as a disease causing believers to lose their identity in Christ and adopt worldly ways.

title: A Court Trial
summary: William Branham presents a courtroom allegory where God is on trial for breach of promise regarding His Word. The prosecuting attorney Satan calls witnesses Unbeliever, Skeptic, and Impatient to testify that God's promises of healing have failed. The defense witness, the Holy Spirit, argues that the promises are only for true believers and that the witnesses have misinterpreted the Word.

title: Christ Is Identified The Same In All Generations
summary: William Branham preaches on the unchanging nature of Jesus Christ, emphasizing that Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He explains that God identifies Himself in each generation by manifesting His Word through prophets, and that the true interpretation of Scripture comes when God makes His promise live. Branham calls believers to recognize the present hour and the promised Word for this age, rather than living in the glare of past revivals.

title: And When Their Eyes Were Opened, They Knew Him
summary: William Branham preaches on the account of the two disciples on the road to Emmaus, emphasizing that even though Jesus had promised His resurrection and explained the Scriptures, they did not recognize Him. He draws parallels to the present day, urging believers to recognize God's fulfillment of His Word and not be blinded by tradition or intellectualism.

title: Then Jesus Came And Called
summary: William Branham preaches on the story of Lazarus from John 11, emphasizing that Jesus comes in the darkest hour to bring hope and resurrection. He contrasts human faith with God's power, urging believers to trust God's Word even when circumstances seem impossible.

title: A Paradox
summary: William Branham speaks on the concept of a paradox—something incredible but true—using biblical examples such as Joshua commanding the sun to stand still, Moses parting the Red Sea, Noah's flood, and David defeating Goliath. He emphasizes that God works through ordinary men who are in the line of duty and have faith in His Word, and warns against relying on human intellect and organization rather than the power of God.

title: Jesus Keeps All His Appointments
summary: William Branham preaches on Jesus keeping all His appointments, using the story of the Pharisee who invited Jesus to dinner but failed to honor Him. He draws parallels to modern church revivals where Christ is invited but not truly welcomed, and emphasizes the need for repentance and recognition of His presence.
themes: the pyramid as a type of the Church

title: The Trial
summary: In this sermon, William Branham presents a courtroom drama where the Word of God is put on trial for breach of promise. The prosecuting attorney, Satan, calls witnesses Unbelief, Skeptic, and Impatience to testify that God's promises fail. The defense witness, the Holy Spirit, calls biblical figures like Noah, Abraham, Moses, Joshua, and Isaiah to show that God's promises are fulfilled in His timing. Branham concludes by testifying to his own calling and the revelation of the Son of man in the last days.
themes: the role of the Holy Spirit
the revelation of the Son of man

title: A Trial
summary: William Branham presents a courtroom-style sermon where the Word of God is put on trial. The prosecuting attorney (Satan) calls witnesses Unbeliever, Skeptic, and Impatient to testify that God's promises have failed. The defense Witness (Holy Spirit) calls Noah, Abraham, and Moses to show that God's Word is always fulfilled in His timing.
themes: The role of the Holy Spirit

title: The Oddball
summary: William Branham uses the metaphor of a 'nut' (oddball) to describe those who are called out from the world to serve Christ. He traces biblical figures like Noah, Moses, Elijah, and Paul, as well as reformers like Luther and Wesley, who were considered fools by their contemporaries but were used by God to hold the Church together. Branham encourages believers to embrace being 'odd' for Christ, threaded to the Word, and to separate from worldly systems.

title: The Oddball
summary: William Branham preaches on the theme of being considered a 'nut' or 'oddball' for Christ, drawing from 1 Corinthians 1:18-25 and 2 Corinthians 12:11. He uses biblical examples like Noah, Moses, Elijah, John the Baptist, Jesus, and Paul, as well as historical figures like Martin Luther and John Wesley, to show that those who stand on God's Word are often ridiculed. Branham encourages believers to be threaded to the Word rather than the world, and shares testimonies of healings and miracles as evidence of God's power.

title: The Unveiling of God
summary: William Branham preaches on how God has always veiled Himself throughout history, changing His form (en morphe) from the Pillar of Fire to Jesus Christ to the Holy Spirit, and now reveals Himself to His elect in the last days. He emphasizes that God is the same yesterday, today, and forever, and that believers must accept His Word by faith even when they cannot fully understand it.

title: The Identified Christ of All Ages
summary: William Branham preaches on Jesus Christ as the same yesterday, today, and forever, emphasizing that God reveals Himself through His Word and identifies Himself in each age. He uses biblical examples to show that Christ is the Word made flesh and that the same signs and wonders are available today.

title: The Presence Of God Unrecognized
summary: William Branham preaches on the unrecognized presence of God, drawing from Matthew 12:38-42. He emphasizes that God's presence is often missed because people are blinded by traditions and creeds, and he calls for a revival of faith to recognize God's work in the current age.

title: Perseverant
summary: William Branham preaches on the importance of perseverance in faith, using biblical examples such as Noah, Moses, David, Samson, and the Syrophenician woman to illustrate how those who have encountered God's presence and heard His voice become unstoppable. He encourages the congregation to be persistent in their faith despite obstacles, criticism, or lack of understanding from others.

title: Who Is Jesus?
summary: William Branham speaks at a Full Gospel Business Men's Fellowship breakfast, sharing personal anecdotes and a dramatic retelling of the story of Zacchaeus to illustrate the importance of seeking Jesus despite obstacles and societal opinions.

title: God Has A Provided Lamb
summary: William Branham preaches on the story of blind Bartimaeus from Mark 10, emphasizing that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He illustrates how Bartimaeus's persistent faith stopped Jesus, and draws parallels to modern faith, including a personal testimony of a woman's prayer being answered. The sermon concludes with an altar call, urging listeners to cry out to Jesus, the provided Lamb of God.
themes: Jesus as the Lamb of God

title: The Trial
summary: William Branham presents a courtroom drama where God's Word is put on trial. The prosecutor (the devil) calls witnesses—Unbeliever, Skeptic, and Impatient—who claim God's promises have failed. The defense witness (the Holy Spirit) counters by calling biblical witnesses like Noah, Abraham, and Moses, showing that God's Word is always fulfilled in His timing.

title: The Mighty God Unveiled Before Us
summary: William Branham explains why believers appear odd to the world, using biblical examples like Noah and Moses. He discusses how God veils Himself from unbelievers but reveals Himself to believers, and how the Holy Spirit continues to work in the present age.
themes: the role of the Holy Spirit
the continuity of God's work through history

title: The Masterpiece
summary: William Branham uses the analogy of Michelangelo's statue of Moses to illustrate God's work in creating humanity as His masterpiece. He traces the fall of man and God's redemptive plan through the patriarchs, prophets, and ultimately Jesus Christ, the perfect Masterpiece. Branham emphasizes that Christ is the fulfillment of all Old Testament promises and the only means of redemption.

title: Private Interview
subtitle: 64-0705X
summary: William Branham interviews Sister Georgia Bruce, reassuring her of her salvation and the sealing of the Holy Ghost. He prays for her healing, emphasizing that Christ's blood covers her sins and that her desire to serve God is evidence of her faith.

title: Going Beyond The Camp
summary: William Branham preaches on the necessity of leaving man-made religious camps and traditions to follow Christ outside the camp, bearing His reproach. He contrasts the camp of God's Word with denominational camps, emphasizing that true sanctification comes through Christ's sacrifice and that believers must go beyond human reason and tradition to experience God's presence and power.
themes: Rejection of tradition for the Word

title: The Feast Of The Trumpets
summary: William Branham teaches on the Feast of Trumpets from Leviticus 23, explaining why the Holy Spirit prevented him from preaching on the Seven Trumpets at this time. He reviews the revelation of the Seven Church Ages and Seven Seals, emphasizing that the Trumpets pertain to Israel, not the Church, and that the Church is in the Laodicean age awaiting the return of Christ.

title: Broken Cisterns
summary: William Branham preaches on Jeremiah 2:12-13, comparing man-made denominational systems to broken cisterns that hold stagnant, polluted water, while God is the Fountain of Living Water. He warns against apostasy and the mark of the beast, urging believers to come out of denominationalism and drink freely from Christ, the smitten Rock.

title: Recognizing Your Day And Its Message
summary: William Branham preaches on recognizing the spiritual hour and message of the day, drawing from Hosea 6 to discuss Israel's restoration and the church's condition. He emphasizes the fulfillment of prophecy, the opening of the Seven Seals, and the imminent Rapture of the Bride.

title: The Future Home of the Heavenly Bridegroom and the Earthly Bride
summary: William Branham preaches on the future home of the Bride of Christ, explaining that the earth will be cleansed by fire and restored as the eternal dwelling place of God and His people. He draws parallels between the three stages of redemption for individuals (repentance, sanctification, Holy Ghost baptism) and the three stages of the earth's redemption (water baptism of Noah's flood, Christ's blood, and final fire).

title: Proving His Word
summary: William Branham preaches on the importance of proving God's Word, using the examples of the woman with the issue of blood and the Queen of Sheba. He emphasizes that God always keeps His promises and that faith must rest on the proven Word of God, not on human reasoning or scientific proof.

title: Questions and Answers
summary: William Branham answers questions from the congregation on topics including Christian living, marriage, the Holy Spirit, and the end times. He warns against deception by signs and wonders, emphasizing the importance of staying true to the Word of God.

title: Questions and Answers
summary: William Branham opens a question-and-answer session at the Branham Tabernacle, addressing topics such as the interpretation of Matthew 24, the nature of false prophets, the gathering of the Bride at the Rapture, and the relationship between water baptism, the Holy Spirit, and salvation. He emphasizes the primacy of the Word as the test of truth and clarifies that water baptism is an outward symbol of regeneration, not the means of remission of sins.

title: Questions and Answers
summary: William Branham answers a series of written questions from the congregation on topics including the Bride, the Holy Spirit, miracles, the resurrection, angels, and the end times. He also shares personal anecdotes and teachings on spiritual warfare and obedience to the Holy Spirit.

title: Questions and Answers
summary: William Branham answers questions from the congregation on topics including the Bride of Christ, the baptism of the Holy Spirit, speaking in tongues, marriage and divorce, and the resurrection. He emphasizes that the Bride comes from all over the world, that the Holy Spirit's evidence is a life in harmony with God's Word, and that believers should not force spiritual gifts but let the Spirit work as He wills.

title: The Identified Masterpiece of God
summary: William Branham speaks on God's masterpiece of creation, from Adam to Christ, emphasizing that Jesus Christ is the perfect reflection of God's Word. He calls believers to be beaten and purified by the Holy Spirit to reflect Christ, warning against worldly social gospel and denominational divisions.

title: The Harvest Time
summary: William Branham speaks on the importance of living by every Word of God, using the metaphor of bread and harvest to illustrate how spiritual life is sustained by God's Word alone. He contrasts natural bread with Jesus as the Bread of Life, and warns against adding or subtracting from Scripture.
themes: Living by every Word of God
Jesus as the Bread of Life
The danger of adding to or subtracting from Scripture
The unity of believers in Christ

title: Why It Had To Be Shepherd
summary: William Branham explores why the birth of Jesus was first revealed to humble shepherds rather than to the religious leaders and theologians of the day. He argues that God bypassed the proud and learned because their theological training blinded them to the simple, humble arrival of the Messiah. Branham draws parallels to the present day, warning that modern religious institutions may similarly reject God's Word when it does not fit their denominational expectations.

title: Who Do You Say This Is?
summary: William Branham preaches on the question asked when Jesus entered Jerusalem: 'Who is this?' He contrasts the world's confusion and tension with the need to recognize the Messiah as the anointed Word for the hour, warning that many reject God's answer to their prayers because it doesn't fit their expectations.

title: Wedding Ceremony
subtitle: 65-0116X
summary: William Branham officiates the wedding of Marilyn Simpson and Gerald Martens, performing a traditional Christian ceremony with prayers for the couple's future. He then offers brief remarks and blessings, connecting the earthly wedding to the coming of Christ for His Bride.
themes: Symbolism of the Bride of Christ

title: A Paradox
summary: William Branham speaks on the theme of paradox—things that seem incredible but are true—using biblical examples such as Joshua commanding the sun to stand still, the virgin birth, and the resurrection. He emphasizes that God's promises are fulfilled through faith, not human effort, and that the same God who performed miracles in the past is still active today.

title: The Seed Of Discrepancy
summary: William Branham preaches on the parable of the wheat and tares from Matthew 13, explaining that the seed of discrepancy (tares) sown by the enemy represents anything contrary to God's Word. He warns against false teachings, organizations, and compromise, emphasizing that only the genuine Word of God, quickened by the Holy Spirit, produces true believers. The harvest at the end of the age will separate the wheat from the tares.

title: The God Who Is Rich In Mercy
summary: William Branham preaches on Ephesians 2, emphasizing God's mercy in quickening those dead in sin. He contrasts true believers (eagles) with impersonators (chickens), using Old Testament examples like Noah, Moses, and the brass serpent to show God's provision for those who follow His Word. He warns against idolizing denominations and calls for a return to the full Word of God.

title: Lean Not Unto Thy Own Understanding
summary: William Branham preaches on Proverbs 3:5, warning against relying on human understanding instead of God's Word. He uses examples from Eden, the Pharisees, and modern churches to show how leaning on creeds and denominations leads to spiritual blindness and death.
themes: The eagle as a symbol of the believer

title: Broken Cisterns
summary: William Branham preaches on Jeremiah 2, contrasting the living water of God with man-made religious systems, which he likens to broken cisterns that cannot hold water. He warns against relying on denominational structures and emphasizes the need for a personal, Spirit-quickened relationship with Christ.

title: Birth Pains
summary: William Branham preaches on the theme of birth pains, drawing parallels between natural childbirth and spiritual rebirth. He discusses the necessity of pain and distress for new life, both in individuals and in the world, and interprets current world events as signs of the impending new creation.

title: This Day This Scripture Is Fulfilled
summary: William Branham speaks at a Full Gospel Business Men's Fellowship convention, recounting a recent incident where a misprinted Bible led him to reflect on Luke 4:21, 'This day this Scripture is fulfilled.' He draws parallels between Jesus' ministry and the present day, emphasizing that the signs of the end times, as in the days of Sodom, are being fulfilled before our eyes.
themes: Revelation of the Son of man

title: Doors In Door
summary: William Branham speaks at a Full Gospel Business Men's Fellowship breakfast in Flagstaff, Arizona, sharing personal anecdotes and a message on the Laodicean church age. He emphasizes the importance of every word of God and the need to open the door to Christ, who stands outside the church knocking.

title: A Man Running From The Presence Of The Lord
The Seed Is Not Heir With The Shuck
summary: William Branham preaches on Galatians 4:27-31, using the allegory of Abraham's two sons (Ishmael and Isaac) and the virgin Mary to illustrate three stages of spiritual development: the stalk (Luther), the tassel (Wesley), and the shuck (Pentecost). He argues that denominational systems are merely carriers of the true Seed, which is the full Word of God manifested in a Bride Church in the last days.

title: This Day This Scripture Is Fulfilled
summary: William Branham preaches on the fulfillment of Scripture in the present age, drawing from Jesus' reading of Isaiah 61 in the synagogue. He emphasizes that God interprets His own Word by making it come to pass, and warns against man-made traditions that blind people to God's work. Branham applies this to the current state of the church and world, declaring that the prophecies for this day are being fulfilled.

title: God's Chosen Place of Worship
summary: William Branham preaches on Deuteronomy 16:1-3, arguing that God's chosen place of worship is not a denomination or church but in Jesus Christ alone. He contrasts the law of death from Mount Sinai with the law of life from Mount Calvary, emphasizing that God put His name in His Son, and only through Christ can one truly worship God.

title: Wedding Ceremony
subtitle: 65-0220X
summary: William Branham officiates a wedding ceremony uniting Linda Reliford and Charles Branham at the Branham Tabernacle. He performs the traditional vows and pronounces them husband and wife, then offers a prayer reflecting on marriage as a symbol of the Church's waiting for the Bridegroom.

title: Who Is This Melchisedec?
summary: William Branham explores the identity of Melchisedec, arguing that He is God in a theophanic form, the Word before becoming flesh in Jesus Christ. He discusses the concept of en morphe (God changing His form) and the predestination of believers, who were in God's thoughts before the foundation of the world. Branham also contrasts the theophany of Melchisedec with the fleshly existence of believers, who bypass the theophany to be tempted by sin, but will receive a glorified body after death.
themes: Eternal Life and the Book of Life
Resurrection and the earnest of the Spirit
The Word as attribute and expression

title: Marriage And Divorce
summary: William Branham teaches on the biblical view of marriage and divorce, emphasizing that God's original plan was one man and one woman for life. He argues that divorce was permitted only because of human hardness of heart, and that the church must return to the beginning for the true answer.

title: The Easter Seal
summary: William Branham preaches on the significance of Easter as the seal of Christ's resurrection, emphasizing that the same Spirit that raised Jesus from the dead dwells in believers, quickening them to eternal life and empowering them for this age. He uses the analogy of an eagle and a magnet to illustrate how God's Spirit calls His elect out of denominational systems into the truth of the present hour.

title: Does God Ever Change His Mind About His Word?
summary: William Branham preaches on the sovereignty of God's Word, using the story of Balaam to argue that God never changes His mind about His Word. He contrasts the spiritual church (Israel) with organized religion (Moab), warning against denominationalism and emphasizing election and the sealing of the Holy Spirit.
themes: Conflict between spiritual and carnal religion
The sealing of the Holy Spirit

title: It Is The Rising Of The Sun
summary: William Branham preaches on Easter morning about the resurrection of Jesus Christ as the ultimate proof of God's Word.
